title: UN urges continued commitment to Sustainable Development Goals despite challenges
content:
In a global landscape increasingly described as a patchwork of “parallel realities,” stark socioeconomic disparities are widening the gap between communities and eroding confidence in multilateral cooperation. Against this backdrop, the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) offer a unifying framework designed to bring people together and foster a more equitable future. The SDGs set a common agenda of 17 interconnected targets, from eradicating poverty to ensuring inclusive governance, that seeks to align national policies with shared global priorities.

The SDGs explicitly address inequality through Target 10, which calls for reducing income disparities and protecting vulnerable groups, while Target 17 emphasizes the need for robust partnerships among governments, civil society, and the private sector. By establishing measurable indicators and encouraging data-driven policy, the goals provide a shared language for tracking progress and mobilizing resources across borders. Multilateral institutions such as the World Bank and regional development banks have begun incorporating SDG metrics into their lending criteria, signaling a shift toward accountability that transcends individual national agendas.

Ultimately, the SDGs serve as a common reference point for nations grappling with divergent realities. Their success hinges on sustained collective action and the willingness of states to cooperate under a shared vision of sustainable, inclusive development.
author: UN News

title: UN calls for Yemen de‑escalation as Saudi strikes and Iranian aircraft raise tensions
content:
The United Nations Secretary‑General’s Special Envoy for Yemen, Hans Grundberg, urged a rapid de‑escalation after reports emerged that Saudi Arabian aircraft carried out airstrikes in Yemen and that Iranian aircraft had landed in the country. The call came ahead of an emergency Security Council meeting scheduled for 3 p.m. local time on Monday.

During the session, senior officials delivered briefings on the evolving humanitarian crisis and the political dynamics on the ground. The updates highlighted the continued displacement of civilians, the strain on medical and food supplies, and the need for a coordinated diplomatic response to the new military activity in the region.

The Council’s meeting aimed to assess the situation and explore options for restoring stability. While no immediate resolutions were adopted, the discussion underscored the urgency of preventing further escalation and protecting civilian populations in Yemen.
author: UN News

title: UN agencies urge de‑escalation in Strait of Hormuz amid US‑Iran tensions
content:
Washington and Tehran each assert that they dominate the narrow Strait of Hormuz, the vital commercial artery through which a significant share of global oil and gas passes. The competing claims have intensified after a recent surge in missile and drone strikes in the region, actions that both sides link to the ongoing US‑Iran confrontation. The heightened military activity has raised concerns about the safety of merchant vessels and the potential for broader disruption of international energy supplies.

On Monday, United Nations agencies issued a joint appeal for de‑escalation, urging all parties to refrain from further attacks and to ensure the free flow of commerce through the strait. The UN statement highlighted the risk that continued hostilities pose to regional stability and to the global economy, and called for diplomatic measures to resolve the dispute and prevent further escalation.
author: UN News

title: WFP Urges Increased Aid Access to Gaza Amid Restrictions
content:
The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has urged for expanded humanitarian access to Gaza, citing that current restrictions on aid deliveries, ongoing violence, and funding shortfalls are critically limiting its capacity to reach civilians in need. The organization highlighted that these constraints have hampered the distribution of essential food supplies and other relief items, jeopardizing the well‑being of the population in the conflict zone.

WFP officials stressed that the blockade of entry points and intermittent shelling have disrupted supply chains, while the lack of adequate financial resources has forced the program to reduce the scale of its operations. They called on all parties to the conflict to facilitate safe, unimpeded passage for aid convoys and to ensure that humanitarian corridors remain open for the duration of the crisis.

The WFP’s appeal underscores the urgent need for coordinated international action to secure both logistical and financial support for Gaza’s humanitarian relief efforts, as the population faces escalating shortages of food and basic necessities.
author: UN News

title: UN Supports ICC's Role in Global Justice Efforts
content:
The United Nations reaffirmed on Monday the indispensable role of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in the worldwide effort to eradicate impunity for the most serious crimes, countering growing calls from some states and political groups to dismantle the tribunal. In a formal statement issued by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, the organization highlighted the ICC’s mandate to prosecute genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and the crime of aggression, emphasizing that its existence strengthens the international rule of law.

The UN’s endorsement comes amid heightened debate over the court’s jurisdiction and effectiveness, with several nations arguing that the ICC infringes on national sovereignty and has been selectively applied. Critics have pointed to perceived biases in investigations and the court’s limited enforcement capabilities, urging reforms or outright abolition. Nevertheless, the United Nations underscored that the ICC remains the only permanent, independent judicial body with universal jurisdiction to hold perpetrators accountable, and it called on member states to cooperate fully with ongoing investigations and prosecutions.

By reiterating support for the ICC, the United Nations aims to reinforce international mechanisms that deter grave violations and provide justice for victims. The statement signals a continued commitment to multilateral legal frameworks, despite dissenting voices, and underscores the expectation that the court will persist as a cornerstone of global accountability for the most egregious offenses.
author: UN News

title: India bans film Satluj about activist Jaswant Singh Khalra
content:
A documentary titled *Satluj*, which chronicles the life and 1995 murder of human‑rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, continues to attract viewers despite an official ban imposed by Indian authorities. Khalra, a former police officer turned advocate, exposed the illegal detention and disappearance of thousands of Sikhs during the 1980s insurgency, leading to his abduction and death at the hands of security forces. The film, directed by independent filmmaker Amrit Singh, was completed in early 2024 and initially slated for theatrical release before the ban was enforced on grounds of “sensitive content” and alleged defamation of state institutions.

Since the prohibition, *Satluj* has been circulated through underground screenings, online peer‑to‑peer platforms and select international film festivals, where it has garnered attention for its investigative depth and personal testimonies from Khalra’s family and former colleagues. Legal challenges filed by the producers argue that the ban violates freedom of expression, while officials maintain that the documentary could inflame communal tensions. Audience numbers, though unverified, suggest a growing interest in the case, reflecting broader public demand for accountability regarding past human‑rights violations. The film’s persistence underscores ongoing debates over censorship, historical memory and the role of documentary cinema in confronting contested narratives.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan urges US-Iran dialogue amid renewed tensions
content:
Islamabad has reiterated its call for diplomatic dialogue between Washington and Tehran as tensions between the United States and Iran intensify following a series of retaliatory strikes and heightened rhetoric in the region. The Pakistani foreign ministry emphasized the need for a negotiated settlement to prevent further destabilisation of South‑Asia, noting that the escalation threatens trade routes, energy supplies and the security of its own borders. The latest flare‑up began after a U.S. drone strike that killed senior Iranian Revolutionary Guard officers, prompting Iran to vow “proportionate” retaliation and to increase its naval presence in the Arabian Sea.

Security analysts argue that Pakistan possesses limited leverage to curb the confrontation, lacking both the military capacity and the diplomatic clout to compel either side to de‑escalate. While Islamabad can offer mediation and host back‑channel talks, its influence is constrained by competing interests with both the United States and Iran, and by domestic political pressures. Consequently, experts warn that without external pressure or a shift in U.S. or Iranian strategy, the risk of broader regional spillover remains high, leaving Pakistan to manage the fallout rather than halt the escalation outright.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Bangkok bar fire kills 30, 24 remain in critical condition
content:
Thai authorities reported that 24 individuals are still in critical condition at hospitals following a fire that engulfed a popular pub in the capital city. The blaze, which broke out late Wednesday night, prompted an immediate emergency response, with fire crews battling the flames for several hours before bringing the inferno under control. Initial reports indicated that more than 50 patrons were inside the establishment when the fire erupted, and at least 12 people have been confirmed dead, while dozens more sustained injuries ranging from minor to severe.

Officials from the Ministry of Public Health and the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration said that medical teams are closely monitoring the critical patients, many of whom suffered from smoke inhalation and burn injuries. An investigation into the cause of the fire has been launched, with preliminary findings pointing to potential electrical faults, though authorities have not ruled out other possibilities. The incident has prompted calls for stricter safety inspections of entertainment venues, and the government has pledged to support the victims' families and ensure that similar tragedies are prevented in the future.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Al Jazeera tests nine AI models to predict 2026 FIFA World Cup champion
content:
Al Jazeera has evaluated nine leading artificial‑intelligence models to forecast the champion of the 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico. The media outlet supplied each system with extensive historical match data, player performance metrics, team rankings and tournament‑specific variables, then asked the models to generate a single prediction for the tournament winner.

The test revealed a range of outcomes, with several models converging on traditional powerhouses such as Brazil and France, while others highlighted emerging contenders like England and the United States. The AI predictions were compiled alongside expert commentary to assess the reliability of machine‑learning approaches in sports forecasting. Al Jazeera’s experiment underscores the growing interest in leveraging advanced analytics for major sporting events and sets a benchmark for future AI‑driven predictions as the 2026 World Cup approaches.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Lord of the Rings Cast Announced
content:
A new film project is underway, boasting an impressive ensemble cast. Kate Winslet, known for her versatile performances in a range of genres, has been confirmed to join the production, alongside Jamie Dornan, who has demonstrated his acting chops in various roles. Additionally, Anya Taylor-Joy, a rising star with a string of notable credits to her name, has also been cast in the film.

The inclusion of these talented actors suggests that the movie is shaping up to be a highly anticipated release. With their collective experience and range, Winslet, Dornan, and Taylor-Joy are likely to bring depth and nuance to their respective roles. While details about the film's plot and production are still scarce, the caliber of the cast is generating excitement among fans and industry insiders alike. As more information becomes available, it is expected that the buzz surrounding the project will continue to build.

The film's production team has not yet announced a release date or revealed further details about the story or characters, but with Winslet, Dornan, and Taylor-Joy on board, the project is already garnering significant attention. As the cast and crew continue to work on bringing the film to life, audiences can look forward to learning more about this promising new project in the coming months. With its talented cast and growing buzz, the film is poised to make a notable impact when it eventually hits theaters.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: France Reach 2026 World Cup Semi-Finals
content:
The 2026 World Cup has been a thrilling tournament so far, with France emerging as one of the top contenders. The team has made it to the semi-finals, where they will face off against Spain in a highly anticipated match. France's journey to the semi-finals has been marked by impressive performances, with the team showcasing their skills and scoring some remarkable goals.

As France progressed through the tournament, they demonstrated their ability to score goals against a variety of opponents. From clinical finishes to spectacular long-range shots, the team has shown its versatility and depth in attack. With a talented squad and a strong team dynamic, France has been able to overcome challenges and secure crucial wins. Their semi-final tie against Spain promises to be an exciting encounter, with both teams boasting a wealth of talent and a strong desire to reach the final.
