The transfer is a significant blow to Newcastle, who had earmarked the player as a potential long‑term solution for their midfield. Villa’s willingness to meet the price tag reflects their ambition to compete on the European stage, while Newcastle will need to reassess their summer recruitment strategy.

With the deal expected to be completed shortly, Villa will add depth to a squad that will face tougher opposition in the Champions League. Newcastle, meanwhile, will look to other targets to fill the void left by the failed bid, as the English club prepares for the new season’s challenges.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England Trails India in Women's Test at Lord's
content:
At the Lord’s Test on Day 3, England’s innings has stalled at 139‑7, with the batting line‑up still missing a breakthrough. Over‑by‑over commentary from 11 a.m. (BST) has shown the team struggling to find rhythm, but a recent 44th‑over drive from opener Lauren Ecclestone has provided a brief lift, adding eight runs to her personal tally. The wicket‑keeper, Rachael Wong, remains stranded at the crease with a duck, while the bowling side continues to apply pressure.

The match report notes that the English side has yet to register a significant partnership, and the scoreline suggests a cautious approach amid a challenging pitch. Ecclestone’s shot has given fans a moment of optimism, yet the team still faces the task of consolidating early wickets and building a competitive total. As the innings progresses, England will need to accelerate while maintaining discipline to avoid further setbacks.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cristo Fernandez Makes Pro Debut
content:
Cristo Fernández, best known for his role as Coach Ted Lasso, made his professional football debut for American second‑tier club El Paso Locomotive in a match against the San Antonio FC on Saturday. The 28‑year‑old Spanish midfielder appeared as a substitute in the second half, contributing to a 2‑1 victory that secured the team’s first win of the season.

The debut follows Fernández’s transition from acting to the sport, a move that has attracted attention from both media and fans. El Paso’s coaching staff praised his enthusiasm and adaptability, noting that his experience in high‑pressure environments has translated well to the pitch. The club’s manager highlighted the importance of integrating new talent into the squad as the season progresses.

With the debut completed, Fernández is set to continue training with the team and may see more playing time as the season unfolds. The club’s management remains optimistic about his potential impact, while supporters welcome the addition of a high‑profile player to the squad.
author: BBC Sport

title: BBC Experts Select England's World Cup Semi-Final XI
content:
England have secured a place in the World Cup semi‑finals after a decisive victory in the quarter‑final, setting the stage for a high‑stakes clash in the next round. The national team, under manager Gareth Southgate, will be looking to balance experience and recent form as they prepare to face their next opponent.

Analysts and fans alike are speculating on the optimal starting eleven for the semi‑final. A lineup that reflects current performance and squad fitness could include: goalkeeper Jordan Pickford; defenders John Stones, Harry Maguire, Ben White, and Luke Shaw; midfielders Declan Rice, Mason Mount, and Phil Foden; forwards Harry Kane, Jadon Sancho, and Marcus Rashford. This selection draws on recent match data, injury status, and tactical considerations, offering a blend of defensive solidity and attacking potency.

With the squad announcement due shortly before the semi‑final, the team will aim to field a balanced side that can adapt to the opponent’s strategy while capitalising on England’s strengths. The match will be a decisive test of Southgate’s tactical acumen and the players’ resilience as they push toward a World Cup title.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump Fires Election Assistance Commission Members
content:
NPR host Michel Martin interviewed former Election Assistance Commission (EAC) member Benjamin Hovland, who was one of three commissioners dismissed by President Donald Trump last week. Hovland, who served on the commission since 2018, was cited for alleged violations of the Hatch Act, a federal law that restricts political activity by public officials. The dismissal followed a federal investigation that found Hovland had engaged in political campaigning while in office, a breach of the commission’s nonpartisan mandate.

The EAC, charged with overseeing the integrity of federal elections, has faced scrutiny over its independence amid the Trump administration’s broader efforts to influence electoral processes. Hovland’s removal is the latest in a series of high‑profile staff changes that critics say undermine the agency’s credibility. Trump’s administration defended the action as a lawful enforcement of the Hatch Act, while the Department of Justice confirmed the findings that led to the firings. The incident has prompted calls from bipartisan lawmakers for clearer safeguards to preserve the commission’s impartiality in future elections.
author: NPR Politics

title: Maine Secretary of State Runs for Senate Seat
content:
Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows told NPR’s Michel Martin she is entering the race for the state’s U.S. Senate seat vacated by Graham Platner, who resigned to pursue a federal appointment. Bellows, a Democrat who has overseen elections and business registrations since 2018, said her candidacy is driven by a desire to continue Platner’s progressive agenda and to strengthen Maine’s representation in Washington. She highlighted her experience in managing statewide elections and her commitment to expanding access to voting as key reasons for her decision to run.

In the interview, Bellows explained that she plans to focus on issues such as climate change, healthcare access, and economic equity—areas that have been central to Platner’s platform. She also noted the importance of maintaining a robust and transparent electoral process, citing her record of modernizing Maine’s voting infrastructure. Bellows acknowledged the challenges of stepping into a high‑profile race but expressed confidence in her ability to connect with voters across the state’s diverse regions.

Bellows’ entry into the Senate race is expected to shift the dynamics of the upcoming election, bringing a seasoned public official with a strong electoral background into the field. The Democratic Party will now have a high‑profile candidate to build on Platner’s legacy, while Republicans will need to adjust their strategy in response to Bellows’ statewide name recognition and policy priorities. The race is slated to be a key contest in the 2024 election cycle, with both parties eyeing the seat’s potential to influence national policy debates.
author: NPR Politics

title: Maine Democrats Seek Replacement for Senate Candidate Graham Platner
content:
Maine Democrats have announced a formal procedure to select a replacement for U.S. Senate candidate Graham Platner, who suffered a serious fall during a campaign rally last month. The party will convene a special committee of state‑wide Democratic leaders to review potential candidates and hold a closed meeting to vote on a successor. The replacement will be announced by the end of the month, allowing the campaign to resume before the primary.

Platner’s accident, which left him hospitalized with a fractured vertebra, shocked voters and raised questions about the campaign’s momentum. Despite the setback, the party’s leadership emphasized that the replacement process will maintain the integrity of the electoral race and provide voters with a clear choice. The committee will consider candidates with statewide recognition and a record of public service, ensuring the new nominee can effectively compete in the upcoming primary and general elections.

The announcement comes as voters grapple with the abrupt change in the race. While the Democratic Party seeks to stabilize the campaign, many constituents remain uncertain about the implications for the broader electoral landscape. The committee’s decision will be closely watched, as it could influence voter turnout and the party’s prospects in Maine’s highly contested Senate contest.
author: NPR Politics

title: Memphis Task Force Agent Kills 25‑Year‑Old Jonah Neal in May; Four Other Fatal Shootings Reported
content:
Jonah Neal, a 25‑year‑old resident of the area, was struck by a Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agent in May, according to local authorities. The incident occurred during a routine operation conducted by the HSI task force, which has been active in the region for several months. Neal sustained serious injuries and was transported to a nearby hospital for treatment.

This event follows a troubling pattern, as the task force has been linked to at least four deadly shootings in the past year. Investigators are examining the circumstances surrounding each incident, with law enforcement agencies coordinating to determine whether the shootings were connected to the agents’ official duties or involved other factors. The HSI agency has stated that it is cooperating fully with the investigation and has temporarily paused certain operations pending the outcome of the inquiry.

The investigation remains ongoing, with authorities urging anyone with additional information to come forward. Officials have emphasized that the safety of the community is a priority and that the agency will take appropriate action based on the findings of the inquiry.
author: NPR Politics

title: MP appears in court over sexual assault charges
content:
A defendant in a sexual‑assault case has entered a plea of not guilty to two counts of sexual assault and is now awaiting trial. The charges stem from allegations that the defendant engaged in non‑consensual sexual conduct with two individuals, as reported by the local police department. Prosecutors say the incidents occurred over a period of several months and that evidence, including video footage and witness statements, supports the allegations.

The trial is scheduled to begin at the County Courthouse on July 22, 2026, with the case overseen by Judge Maria Sanchez. The defendant, a 34‑year‑old resident of the city, has maintained his innocence and has retained legal counsel to challenge the evidence presented by the state. The prosecution’s case will rely on forensic analysis, expert testimony, and the testimonies of the alleged victims, while the defense will argue that the encounters were consensual and that the evidence is insufficient to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

If found guilty, the defendant faces potential sentences ranging from 10 to 20 years in state prison, depending on the severity of the charges and any prior criminal history. The outcome of the trial will be closely watched by community leaders and advocacy groups who are monitoring the case as part of a broader effort to address sexual‑violence allegations within the region.
author: BBC Politics

title: Suspect in Ann Widdecombe murder seen on CCTV entering car in Rotherham
content:
A man wearing a white shirt and shorts was captured on surveillance footage entering a red car outside a residence in Rotherham. The clip, which has been released by local authorities, shows the individual walking to the vehicle and getting in before the camera pans away. The footage was taken in the early evening and has been circulated to assist in identifying the person and vehicle involved.

Police are reviewing the video as part of an ongoing investigation into a suspected burglary at the Rotherham house. The suspect’s description and the colour of the car match reports from residents who observed the incident. Investigators are urging anyone with additional information or further footage to contact the Rotherham Police Service.

The authorities have not yet confirmed whether the individual is a suspect or a witness. They continue to request cooperation from the public and will provide updates as the investigation progresses.
author: BBC Politics

title: Zaghari‑Ratcliffe Criticizes Iran’s Rearrest of Wildlife Activists
content:
Nazanin Zaghari‑Ratcliffe, the British‑Iranian dual‑national who has been held in Iranian custody since 2016, has publicly condemned the recent rearrest of two Iranian environmentalists. Speaking from Evin Prison, she described the arrests as “unimaginably cruel and alarming,” underscoring the growing concern over the treatment of activists in the country.

The detained pair, husband and wife Houman Jokar and Sepideh Kashani, had been working to protect the endangered Asiatic cheetah when they were taken by the Ministry of Intelligence from their home on 1 July. No official justification has been released, and their current whereabouts remain unknown. Kashani had previously been a fellow inmate of Zaghari‑Ratcliffe, a fact that has drawn additional international attention to the case.

The incident adds to a broader pattern of detentions in Iran, raising questions about the motives behind the arrests and the safety of those who engage in environmental and human‑rights work. As of now, no further information has been provided by Iranian authorities regarding the fate of Jokar and Kashani.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Study advises RSV therapies for infants target virus and immune response
content:
Researchers at University College London and Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children have published a study indicating that effective future treatments for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) will need to address both the virus itself and the host immune response. The findings suggest that targeting only viral replication or solely modulating inflammation may be insufficient to achieve optimal outcomes for infants, who are the most vulnerable group.

The study, which involved collaboration between virology and immunology teams at UCL and GOSH, highlights the complex interplay between RSV infection and the developing immune system. By demonstrating that dual‑mechanism approaches can more comprehensively reduce viral load and mitigate harmful inflammatory responses, the research provides a framework for designing next‑generation therapeutics that could improve survival and reduce long‑term respiratory complications in newborns.

These insights are expected to guide clinical trial design and drug development strategies, emphasizing the importance of integrated antiviral and immunomodulatory interventions. The authors call for continued investment in research that bridges virology and immunology to deliver safer, more effective RSV therapies for the most at‑risk pediatric populations.
author: Medical Xpress

title: China’s Green Great Wall Uses Grid Sticks to Plant Trees in Northern Deserts
content:
For the past fifty years, a vast network of workers has been methodically transforming the shifting sands of northern China into green belts. In the dry expanses of the Gobi and adjacent desert regions, teams have laid down forearm‑length wooden stakes in straight rows, then intersecting lines, creating a precise grid across the landscape. At the center of each resulting square, a sapling is planted, gradually turning barren ground into a forested patchwork.

This large‑scale afforestation effort, part of China’s long‑running desert‑reclamation initiatives, involves millions of laborers and thousands of hectares each year. The grid technique ensures even spacing and optimal root development for the young trees, which are chosen for their resilience to arid conditions. Over the decades, the cumulative effect has been a significant increase in vegetation cover, a reduction in wind erosion, and a measurable improvement in local microclimates.

The continued expansion of this program underscores its role in mitigating desertification and supporting ecological stability in northern China. As the country maintains its commitment to expanding green infrastructure, the grid‑based planting method remains a cornerstone of its strategy to restore degraded lands and promote sustainable environmental stewardship.
author: Phys.org

title: Heat Wave Claims Over 2,700 Lives in England and Wales
content:
A recent study has revealed that the heat waves that affected England and Wales in May and June resulted in a significant number of deaths. According to the findings, at least 2,700 people lost their lives due to the extreme temperatures during this period. This data highlights the severe impact of heat waves on public health, particularly among vulnerable populations such as the elderly and those with pre-existing medical conditions.

The study's results provide valuable insight into the consequences of heat waves, which are becoming increasingly common due to climate change. The high temperatures experienced in England and Wales in May and June were exceptional, even by the standards of a region accustomed to mild summers. The fact that these heat waves occurred early in the summer season is also noteworthy, as it suggests that the traditional notion of a brief, warm summer may be giving way to more prolonged and intense heat waves. As the climate continues to evolve, it is essential to develop strategies for mitigating the effects of extreme temperatures on human health.

The release of this study serves as a reminder of the importance of preparing for and responding to heat waves. As the world grapples with the challenges posed by climate change, understanding the human impact of extreme weather events is crucial for developing effective public health policies and emergency response plans. The findings of this study will likely inform discussions around heat wave mitigation and response in England and Wales, with the aim of reducing the risk of heat-related illnesses and deaths in the future.
author: Phys.org

title: Quantum Heat Engine Demonstrated
content:
Aalto University researchers have announced the first demonstration of a cyclic quantum heat engine operating within a superconducting circuit, a milestone that could accelerate the development of quantum technologies and deepen insights into classical thermodynamics. The experiment, conducted by a team of physicists and engineers, employed a carefully engineered superconducting qubit system to convert thermal energy into work in a closed cycle, mirroring the operation of a conventional heat engine but at the quantum scale.

The study highlights how recent advances in applying thermodynamic principles to quantum systems are beginning to yield practical devices. By harnessing quantum coherence and entanglement, the engineered engine achieves energy conversion efficiencies that challenge classical limits, offering a new platform for exploring quantum thermodynamic cycles. Moreover, the findings suggest that a clearer understanding of quantum thermodynamics may feedback into classical theory, potentially refining models of energy transfer and entropy in macroscopic systems.

While the prototype remains in the laboratory, its successful operation marks a significant step toward integrating quantum heat engines into future quantum computing and sensing architectures. The research underscores the growing synergy between fundamental physics and applied quantum engineering, pointing the way to more efficient quantum devices and a richer theoretical framework for both quantum and classical thermodynamics.
author: Phys.org

title: RNA-Only Repair Enzyme Sheds Light on Early Genome Protection
content:
The fundamental components of life, DNA and proteins, have a deeply intertwined relationship in modern cells. DNA serves as the primary storage of the genetic blueprint, containing the instructions necessary for various cellular processes. Conversely, proteins are responsible for replicating, repairing, and building based on the information encoded in the DNA. This dynamic interplay highlights the intricate dependency between these two essential molecules.

The relationship between DNA and proteins is further complicated by the fact that proteins require instructions from DNA to be produced in the first place. This creates a chicken-and-egg problem, where DNA needs proteins to carry out its instructions, but proteins need DNA to provide the necessary instructions for their own creation. This paradox underscores the complex and highly regulated nature of cellular processes, where the synthesis and function of DNA and proteins are carefully coordinated to maintain the integrity and viability of the cell.

In conclusion, the interdependent relationship between DNA and proteins is a crucial aspect of cellular biology, with each component playing a vital role in the functioning of the cell. The intricate dance between these molecules allows cells to replicate, grow, and respond to their environment, ultimately giving rise to the vast diversity of life on Earth. This fundamental relationship continues to be the subject of ongoing research, as scientists seek to unravel the complexities of cellular biology and uncover new insights into the workings of life itself.
author: Phys.org

title: Useless If Statement Boosts Code Performance Fourfold
content:
A recent blog post on PurpleSyringa titled “Quadrupling code performance with a useless if” has attracted attention from the developer community. The author argues that inserting a seemingly redundant conditional statement can, under certain circumstances, lead to a significant increase in execution speed—up to four times faster in the examples provided. The post explains that the trick exploits compiler optimization heuristics, such as branch prediction and instruction cache behavior, which can be unintentionally improved by the presence of the extra if clause.

In the article, the author presents a series of benchmarks comparing a baseline implementation with one that includes the “useless” conditional. The results show a dramatic reduction in runtime for CPU‑bound tasks, particularly in tight loops where the compiler is able to better predict branch outcomes and streamline instruction pipelines. The post also discusses potential pitfalls, noting that the performance gain is highly dependent on the specific compiler, target architecture, and code context, and that the technique should be applied judiciously rather than as a universal optimization.

The post has sparked discussion on Hacker News, where it has garnered 60 upvotes and 8 comments. Readers praise the clear demonstration of a counterintuitive optimization, while some caution against overreliance on such tricks without thorough profiling. Overall, the article highlights how a deep understanding of compiler behavior can uncover unexpected performance improvements, even from seemingly superfluous code constructs.
author: Hacker News

title: Berkshire's $397 Billion Market Bet
content:
Berkshire Hathaway has reportedly placed a $397 billion bet against what it sees as an overheated equity market. The investment arm of the conglomerate, led by long‑time investor Warren Buffett, is said to have used a combination of derivatives and short‑sale strategies to position itself for a potential market correction. Analysts note that the size of the bet is unprecedented for a single investor, signaling a significant shift in Berkshire’s risk appetite amid concerns over valuation levels and macroeconomic uncertainty.

The strategy reportedly involves a mix of credit default swaps, put options and futures contracts that allow Berkshire to profit from a decline in major indices while limiting downside exposure. The move comes as market volatility has risen and investor sentiment has become increasingly bullish, prompting some large institutions to hedge aggressively. While Berkshire’s precise methodology remains confidential, the sheer scale of the position suggests a belief that the current market trajectory is unsustainable and could lead to a sharp correction in the near term.

If the bet proves successful, it could send a strong signal to other institutional investors about the health of the equity markets, potentially prompting a reevaluation of risk models and portfolio allocations. Conversely, a market rally would expose Berkshire to significant losses, underscoring the high stakes of such a large short position. The outcome of this bet will be closely watched by market participants and could influence future investment strategies across the financial sector.
author: Hacker News

title: Top Kitchen Composters for 2026
content:
Indoor food‑scrap disposal has become a growing concern for urban households, prompting a new wave of appliances that promise both convenience and minimal odor. WIRED recently evaluated a selection of countertop composter and waste‑processing units, highlighting models that effectively break down kitchen scraps while keeping unpleasant smells at bay. The devices tested range from compact, countertop‑mounted units that use heat and moisture to convert food waste into compost, to larger, freestanding models that incorporate sealed chambers and carbon‑activated filters for odor control.

The WIRED‑tested devices share several common features: a sealed processing chamber, a built‑in filtration system, and a user‑friendly interface that signals when the unit is ready for emptying. Many models also offer smart connectivity, allowing users to monitor progress via a smartphone app. According to the review, the odor levels during operation were consistently below detectable thresholds, and the compost output is suitable for home gardens or can be safely disposed of in municipal composting programs. The devices are priced between $200 and $600, with the higher‑end models offering additional safety certifications and longer warranties.

These indoor composter options provide a practical solution for residents looking to reduce landfill waste without sacrificing space or hygiene. By converting food scraps into nutrient‑rich compost on the kitchen counter, users can participate in sustainable waste management while keeping their living spaces odor‑free and clutter‑free.
author: Wired

title: Far‑Right Extremists Praise Citizen Vigilante
content:
A new film, *Citizen Vigilante*, has drawn attention from far‑right circles after one extremist commentator labeled it the “feel‑good movie of white‑boy summer.” The film, which follows a suburban teenager who takes on local crime, has been promoted by certain far‑right groups as a tool to appeal to moderate audiences and potentially broaden their support base.

The movie’s storyline and themes—emphasizing individual action against perceived injustice—have resonated with factions that view it as a narrative of empowerment for white youth. Analysts note that the film’s marketing has been leveraged in online forums and social media to frame the narrative as a call to civic engagement, while critics argue it can serve as a recruitment vehicle for extremist ideology. The film’s release has sparked debate over the role of popular media in shaping political attitudes among young viewers.
author: Wired

title: Waze adds Gemini AI features to improve voice navigation
content:
Google has announced an AI‑powered overhaul of its Waze navigation app, integrating its flagship Gemini assistant to give drivers more personalized routing options. The update is part of a broader strategy to make navigation more conversational and responsive, allowing users to interact with the app in a way that mirrors natural speech.

Among the four new features, two specifically leverage Gemini. First, Waze is upgrading its Conversation Reporting tool—introduced in 2024—to enable drivers to issue voice commands that report traffic incidents or suggest map edits, such as road closures or outdated addresses. Second, the Destination Search feature lets users ask Gemini to locate nearby points of interest, for example, “Find me a coffee shop that’s open,” and receive instant, context‑aware results. These enhancements aim to streamline the reporting process and improve the accuracy of the map data.

The Verge reports that the AI integration is designed to make navigation more intuitive, reducing the need for manual input while driving. By embedding Gemini’s conversational capabilities, Waze seeks to enhance user experience and keep its map data up‑to‑date through real‑time, voice‑activated contributions.
author: The Verge

title: EU weighs new social media limits for teens
content:
The European Union is preparing to introduce comprehensive restrictions on children’s and teenagers’ use of social‑media platforms. The proposed measures would set new age limits, allow for a complete ban on users under a certain age, and introduce a phased‑access system that gradually unlocks features as users reach older age thresholds. Platforms could also be required to demonstrate that their services pose no harmful risks before young people are permitted to join.

Under the draft framework, social‑media companies would need to prove that their content, algorithms, and data‑handling practices do not expose minors to undue harm. This would involve independent audits and compliance certifications, ensuring that the platforms meet safety standards before they can offer services to younger audiences. The EU’s approach seeks to shift the focus from whether children can access social media to when and how they are allowed to do so.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the executive arm could propose new legislation within months after reviewing a panel of experts’ recommendations, released today. “This is not about whether children can access social media. It is about when social media can access our children,” she said. The proposed rules aim to tighten regulatory oversight and protect minors while balancing the digital economy’s growth.
author: The Verge

title: Free Mac App WhatCable Reveals USB‑C Cable Performance
content:
A new utility for Apple‑silicon Macs is giving users a free, built‑in way to evaluate the performance of their USB‑C cables after the discontinuation of a popular $8 hardware tester. The app, called WhatCable, taps into diagnostic information that macOS already gathers about connected USB devices—data that Apple does not normally expose to end users—and presents it in a simple menu‑bar widget. By clicking the widget, users can instantly see whether a cable is capable of high‑speed data transfer, power delivery, or if it is limited or faulty.

WhatCable’s functionality mirrors the earlier handheld tester that identified “fast, slow, powerful, or weak” cables, but it does so without additional hardware and at no cost. The software reads the cable’s electronic identifiers and reports its specifications, allowing consumers to verify the quality of third‑party or older cables directly from their computers. The tool expands the utility of Apple’s own diagnostics, offering a convenient solution for anyone needing to confirm cable performance in a growing ecosystem of USB‑C accessories.
author: The Verge

title: Azerbaijan mulls full withdrawal from Council of Europe
content:
Baku is weighing a complete exit from the 46‑member Council of Europe after the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) suspended Azerbaijan’s voting rights earlier this year. President Ilham Aliyev announced the consideration of full withdrawal in response to the suspension, which was imposed in 2024 amid concerns over the country’s compliance with the body’s democratic standards and human‑rights obligations.

The suspension follows a series of criticisms by PACE and other European institutions regarding the conduct of elections, freedom of expression, and the treatment of political opponents in Azerbaijan. While the Council of Europe has offered avenues for remedial action, Baku’s leadership has signaled that the loss of voting privileges could prompt a decisive break. Analysts note that a withdrawal would remove Azerbaijan from a platform that monitors legal and political reforms across Europe, potentially reshaping the nation’s diplomatic engagement with the continent.
author: Euronews

title: Heatwaves Shift France's Real‑Estate Market
content:
Crude oil prices jumped sharply after a series of renewed strikes between the United States and Iran, reigniting concerns over supply disruptions in the global energy market. The escalated hostilities prompted traders to reassess risk premiums, pushing Brent crude above $90 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate toward $85 a barrel, levels not seen since early 2023. Analysts linked the price surge to the potential for broader regional instability, noting that any interruption to Persian Gulf shipments could tighten inventories and affect downstream industries worldwide.

In parallel, French real‑estate agents reported a shift in buyer preferences as increasingly frequent heatwaves drive demand toward properties with better climate resilience, such as homes equipped with efficient cooling systems and greener building materials. Meanwhile, Cuba experienced a nationwide blackout, authorities attributing the outage to the cumulative strain of U.S. sanctions on the island’s power infrastructure. Both developments underscore how environmental pressures and geopolitical tensions are reshaping markets and daily life across different regions.
author: France 24

title: France ready for semi‑final clash with Spain after Morocco win
content:
France is set to face Spain in the upcoming semi‑final after securing its place with a victory over Morocco. The French side, buoyed by the win, will meet a Spanish team that has conceded just one goal throughout the tournament, making the encounter the most formidable challenge for Les Bleus to date. FRANCE 24’s correspondent James Vasina reported that the French camp is intensifying preparations, focusing on tactical adjustments and defensive solidity to counter Spain’s potent attack.  

Organizers confirmed the match will take place later this week, with both teams expected to field their strongest line‑ups. While France looks to build on its recent momentum, Spain aims to maintain the defensive record that has carried it this far. The outcome will determine which nation advances to the final, concluding a tightly contested tournament.
author: France 24

title: Coalition of the Willing Meets in Paris to Boost Ukraine Support
content:
Ukrainian drone attacks on July 13 resulted in four fatalities and seven injuries in Russia, with the majority of casualties reported in the Moscow region, according to Russian authorities. Kyiv has increased the frequency of such strikes, citing retaliation against recent Russian artillery barrages that have intensified across the front lines. The incidents mark a notable escalation in cross‑border hostilities, underscoring the heightened tension between the two nations as the conflict enters its second year.

At the same time, a gathering of the “coalition of the willing”—a group of Ukraine’s principal allies—convened in Paris to coordinate diplomatic and military support for Kyiv. Participants discussed further assistance measures, including the provision of defensive weapons and economic aid, while reaffirming their commitment to Ukraine’s sovereignty. The meeting follows the latest wave of Ukrainian strikes, highlighting the broader international response to the ongoing conflict.
author: France 24

title: Wildfire in southern Spain kills 13, leaves 10 missing
content:
A wildfire that erupted in the Almería region of southern Spain has claimed at least 13 lives and left ten people still missing, authorities said. The blaze, which ignited in early August, spread across roughly 7,000 hectares of forest and scrubland before firefighters were able to bring it under control. Emergency services evacuated hundreds of residents from the affected municipalities, but the fire’s intensity has now subsided enough for many to return to their homes.

Officials continue to assess the full extent of the damage while search and rescue teams work to locate the missing. The incident follows a season of heightened fire risk across the Iberian Peninsula, prompting heightened alert levels and the deployment of additional firefighting resources. FRANCE 24’s Sarah Morris reported from Madrid on the ongoing response and the community’s efforts to recover from the disaster.
author: France 24

title: Macron says France has fulfilled its rearmament commitment
content:
French President Emmanuel Macron announced that France has met its “commitment to rearm” during his annual address to the armed forces on Monday, ahead of the nation’s July 14 Bastille Day celebrations. In the speech, he highlighted the country’s recent investments in defense capabilities, including new aircraft, naval vessels, and advanced cyber‑security systems, underscoring the government’s focus on maintaining strategic autonomy.

Macron’s remarks followed a series of budgetary increases and procurement programs aimed at modernising the French military. He noted that the rearmament effort is part of a broader European security strategy, aligning with NATO objectives and responding to evolving geopolitical threats. The president also reaffirmed France’s dedication to international cooperation while emphasizing the importance of self‑reliance in defense matters.

Concluding his address, Macron urged the armed services to continue adapting to contemporary challenges and to uphold France’s role as a leading global security actor. The statement was received as a reaffirmation of France’s commitment to safeguarding national interests and reinforcing its position within the international community.
author: France 24

title: Former Spanish PM Rajoy Faces Backlash Over Racist Remark About French Football Team
content:
Former Spanish Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy has drawn sharp criticism after claiming that France’s national football team fielded “no French players.” The remark, made during a televised discussion about the recent international match, was quickly denounced by Spain’s current prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, who called the statement “misinformed” and “disrespectful to the French squad.” Spanish media outlets amplified the backlash, highlighting the inconsistency of the claim given the team’s roster of home‑grown talent.

The controversy extended beyond Spain’s borders, with French officials and commentators labeling Rajoy’s comment as “unfounded” and an affront to French football. Social media platforms saw a surge of responses from French fans and sports analysts defending the national team’s composition. The episode underscores the sensitivity surrounding cross‑border sports commentary and has prompted calls for public figures to verify facts before speaking on international matters.
author: France 24

title: World Cup final to feature Super Bowl‑style halftime show supporting FIFA education fund
content:
For the first time in history, the FIFA World Cup final will feature a halftime performance modeled on the entertainment format of the U.S. Super Bowl. Organizers said the spectacle is designed to draw a global audience and to promote the tournament’s charitable component, the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which aims to raise $100 million for children’s education and welfare projects worldwide during the competition.

The halftime show will be produced in partnership with Global Citizen and will include musical acts, visual displays and interactive segments intended to highlight the fund’s objectives. FIFA officials explained that proceeds from sponsorships, merchandise and viewer donations linked to the event will be directed to the education fund, which supports initiatives ranging from school construction to digital learning resources in low‑income regions. In an interview with France 24, Hugh Evans, CEO of the Global Citizen Education Fund, emphasized the importance of leveraging the World Cup’s massive viewership to generate both awareness and financial support for the $100 million target.

The integration of a Super Bowl‑style halftime show marks a new approach for FIFA in combining sport, entertainment and philanthropy on the world stage. If successful, the model could become a recurring feature of future tournaments, linking the excitement of the final match with a sustained effort to improve educational outcomes for children around the globe.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine Announces New Prime Minister Amid Cabinet Reshuffle
content:
Kyiv – President Volodymyr Zelensky announced a new political strategy accompanied by a reshuffle of the Ukrainian government, stating that Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko will leave her post. Zelensky said he has offered Svyrydenko a new position centered on managing relations with a key international partner, and called for a “renewal of the Cabinet of Ministers” as part of the broader reform agenda.

The president also indicated that changes will be made among the heads of law‑enforcement agencies, though no specific reasons for the shake‑up were provided. The announced adjustments signal an effort to reorganize the executive branch and align it with the president’s strategic priorities.
author: France 24

title: EU Ministers Approve New Air Passenger Rights Package
content:
EU transport ministers have formally approved a new package of air‑passenger rights reforms that aim to make compensation claims more accessible for travelers across the bloc. The measures, which update the existing Regulation (EC) No 261/2004, introduce a streamlined, EU‑wide online portal for filing claims and lower the administrative thresholds that have previously hindered passengers from pursuing compensation. Under the revised rules, airlines will be required to provide clearer information about passenger entitlements and to process valid claims within a set timeframe, with stronger penalties for non‑compliance.

The reforms, the result of several years of negotiations between the European Commission, the Parliament and member states, are intended to reduce bureaucratic obstacles and improve enforcement of passenger rights. Once the legislation is ratified by the European Parliament, the new procedures are expected to take effect next year, offering a more uniform and efficient system for travelers seeking redress for delays, cancellations or denied boarding.
author: DW World

title: US-Iran conflict escalates, Gulf nations face heightened risks
content:
Washington’s recent air strikes against Iranian facilities have been met with a rapid Iranian response that has focused on the United States’ regional partners. Within hours of the attacks, Iranian forces launched a series of missile and drone operations aimed at military installations and logistical hubs belonging to U.S. allies in the Gulf, including Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.

Iranian officials have emphasized that the retaliation is directed at U.S. strategic assets rather than at the governments or civilian populations of neighboring states. Nevertheless, the escalation raises concerns for Gulf nations, whose economies and security frameworks are closely tied to stable oil exports and maritime trade routes. Analysts note that any broadening of hostilities could jeopardize critical infrastructure, disrupt energy markets and compel regional powers to divert resources toward defense measures.

The developing confrontation underscores the heightened risk of a wider conflict in the Middle East. Diplomatic channels remain active as regional and international actors seek to contain the violence, but the situation remains fluid, with Gulf states facing significant potential losses should the fighting intensify.
author: DW World

title: Iran's IRGC attacks US-linked sites in Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman after US strike
content:
Tehran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced on Tuesday that it had launched attacks against facilities it described as “linked to the United States military” in Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman. The statement came in response to what the IRGC called the “latest U.S. bombardment” of Iranian targets, a reference to a series of airstrikes the United States carried out earlier this week in retaliation for attacks on American interests in the region. According to the IRGC, the strikes were coordinated by its Quds Force and were intended to neutralize surveillance and communication sites used by U.S. forces operating from the three Gulf states.

The IRGC did not provide specific details on the weapons employed or the extent of damage inflicted, but it claimed the operations were “precise” and caused “significant disruption” to U.S. military capabilities in the area. U.S. officials have not yet confirmed or denied the attacks, and regional governments in Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman have called for investigations while urging calm. The exchange of fire marks a further escalation in the already strained U.S.-Iran relationship, raising concerns among international observers about the potential for broader conflict in the Gulf.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Welsh artist embroiders names of Gaza infants on christening gown
content:
Diana Williams, an American textile artist, has completed a hand‑stitched gown bearing the names of 300 infants who died in the Gaza conflict. The piece, which lists each child in small, red embroidery, is intended as a visual memorial and a call for awareness of the civilian toll of the war between Israel and Hamas. Williams began the project in early 2024 after reviewing United Nations reports that documented the deaths of more than 300 babies in Gaza since the conflict escalated in October 2023.

The artist plans to exhibit the gown in New York City later this summer, seeking placement in a gallery or museum that can accommodate the work’s size and emotional impact. She has already displayed photographs of the garment at several virtual forums and has shared the images on social media, where they have been viewed by thousands. Organizers of upcoming human‑rights exhibitions have expressed interest, and Williams hopes the piece will become part of broader discussions on war casualties and civilian protection.

If the gown reaches a public venue in New York, it will join a series of artistic responses to the Gaza war that aim to document personal loss and foster dialogue. Williams’ project underscores the use of textile art as a medium for collective remembrance, adding a tangible record of the conflict’s youngest victims to the historical archive.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran launches third Gulf strike as US‑Iran tensions rise
content:
Iran launched a series of missile and drone strikes against several Gulf states on Thursday, marking the third retaliatory episode in a week of escalating hostilities between Tehran and the United States. The attacks were directed at military installations in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar, and were described by Iranian officials as a response to what they termed “unprovoked American aggression” following a U.S. drone shoot‑down over Iranian airspace earlier in the week. The strikes, which reportedly involved short‑range ballistic missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles, caused limited structural damage and no confirmed fatalities, according to local authorities.

U.S. Central Command condemned the actions as “unjustified aggression” and pledged to defend its regional partners, while diplomatic channels in Washington and Tehran exchanged warnings of further escalation. Regional security analysts noted that the rapid succession of attacks underscores a heightened risk of broader conflict in the strategically vital Persian Gulf corridor, where shipping lanes and energy supplies are critical to the global economy. Both sides appear to be testing each other’s resolve, leaving neighboring states and international observers closely monitoring developments for signs of de‑escalation or further confrontation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukrainian attacks spark explosions and fires in Russia
content:
Explosions and extensive fires erupted in Russia’s Belgorod region on Tuesday after a series of Ukrainian strikes targeted several settlements near the border. Local authorities reported multiple blasts that ignited residential and industrial structures, prompting emergency services to deploy fire‑fighting units and rescue teams across the affected areas. The Russian Ministry of Defense confirmed that the attacks involved a combination of missile and drone munitions, though it did not disclose the exact number of projectiles used.

Preliminary assessments indicated that dozens of homes and a small manufacturing facility suffered severe damage, with several injuries reported among civilians and first responders. Russian officials condemned the strikes as a violation of international law and announced plans to reinforce border defenses, while Ukrainian officials claimed the operations were aimed at “neutralizing military infrastructure” in the region. No immediate claims of responsibility were made by either side, and the situation remained under close monitoring by regional security agencies.

The incidents have heightened tensions along the Russia‑Ukraine frontier, prompting both governments to issue statements warning of further escalations. International observers called for restraint and urged both parties to avoid actions that could endanger civilian populations. Investigations into the cause of the explosions and the extent of the damage are ongoing.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Syria's electricity supply improves but costs remain high
content:
Damascus residents have reported a noticeable improvement in the reliability of state‑supplied electricity over the past few weeks, marking a shift from the frequent outages that have plagued the capital for years. The enhancement follows recent upgrades to the national grid and the commissioning of additional power generation capacity, which officials say are part of a broader effort to stabilize the country’s energy infrastructure.

Despite the gains in service, households and businesses continue to voice concerns over the rising cost of electricity, which they say places a growing financial burden on consumers already coping with economic challenges. Energy analysts note that higher tariffs reflect the government’s attempt to offset the expenses of importing fuel and maintaining the upgraded network, while also reducing subsidies. The mixed response underscores the delicate balance between improving service delivery and managing affordability for the population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Wildfires near Paris cause evacuations and disrupt train and motorway services
content:
Wildfires have engulfed more than 800 hectares of forest and scrubland on the outskirts of Fontainebleau, a town south of Paris, prompting the deployment of two water‑bombing aircraft by French authorities on Saturday. The aerial units were dispatched by the Prefecture of Seine‑et‑Marne in coordination with the national fire service to contain the rapidly spreading flames that ignited earlier in the day.

Ground crews from the departmental fire brigade and the National Gendarmerie have been engaged in direct suppression, establishing firebreaks and protecting nearby residential zones. Weather conditions, including strong winds and high temperatures, have hampered containment efforts, while officials have issued precautionary alerts to residents in the affected communes. No casualties have been reported, and the cause of the blaze remains under investigation.

The operation continues with both aerial and terrestrial resources focused on fully extinguishing the fire and preventing further expansion. Authorities will maintain heightened surveillance of the area and provide updates as the situation evolves, emphasizing that the priority remains the safety of the local population and the preservation of the surrounding natural environment.
author: Al Jazeera

title: France meets Spain in World Cup semifinal
content:
France, led by veteran striker Kylian Mbappé, will meet a youthful Spanish side captained by prodigy Lamine Yamal in the semifinal of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The match, scheduled for Thursday at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, pits the defending European champions against a Spain team that advanced to the knockout stage after topping Group C with victories over Brazil, Nigeria and Japan. Mbappé, who has scored 12 goals in the tournament, will look to guide Les Bleus back to the final after a 2‑1 win over England in the quarter‑finals, while Yamal, the youngest player ever to start a World Cup match, has already contributed two assists and one goal in Spain’s run.

Both teams arrive with contrasting narratives: France seeks to capitalize on Mbappé’s experience and a balanced midfield anchored by Paul Pogba and Antoine Griezmann, whereas Spain relies on the pace and creativity of Yamal alongside established forwards Ansu Fati and Ferran Torres. Tactical analysts note that France’s compact defense, marshaled by Raphaël Varane, will be tested by Spain’s high‑pressing style. The winner will move on to face the victor of the other semifinal, with the World Cup title at stake. A victory for either side would set up a historic final, underscoring the tournament’s blend of seasoned stars and emerging talent.
author: Al Jazeera

title: EU countries discuss sanctions on trade from Israeli settlements
content:
Pressure from European Union member states to adopt punitive measures against Israel has grown markedly in recent months, driven by a surge in violence perpetrated by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. Diplomats note that a coalition of countries, including Sweden, Ireland and the Netherlands, have formally called on the European Commission to consider targeted sanctions aimed at individuals and entities linked to settlement expansion and attacks on Palestinian civilians.

The escalation of settler activity, which has included reports of property destruction, physical assaults and the use of firearms against residents of Palestinian villages, has intensified scrutiny from the EU. In response, the European Parliament’s foreign affairs committee has organized hearings to assess evidence of human‑rights violations, while the European Commission’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs has indicated that any sanctions would need to be consistent with EU legal frameworks and coordinated with member states. Meanwhile, Israel’s government has rejected the prospect of sanctions, arguing that they would undermine bilateral cooperation and regional stability.

As the debate continues, EU officials emphasize that any decision will balance the need to uphold international law with the diplomatic complexities of the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict. The outcome is expected to shape the Union’s broader policy toward the Middle East and could set a precedent for future actions against settlement‑related activities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Infantino hints at 64‑team World Cup 2026 expansion
content:
The final week of the 2026 FIFA World Cup is now in full swing, with teams preparing for the knockout rounds as the tournament’s climax approaches. Amid the on‑field action, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has reiterated plans to expand the competition to 64 teams for future editions, a proposal that has generated significant discussion among football authorities, clubs, and national associations.

The expansion would eliminate the current third‑place qualification mechanism, thereby reducing the number of matches that determine elimination and streamlining the tournament’s structure. Proponents argue that a larger field would broaden participation, allowing more nations to compete and potentially enriching the global football experience. Critics, however, point to the increased complexity of qualification, the need for additional venues, and the logistical demands on host cities—including stadiums, accommodation, training facilities, and media infrastructure—that could strain resources and planning capacities.

As FIFA weighs the benefits of a cleaner, more inclusive format against the practical challenges of scaling the event, the debate continues to shape discussions about the future of the World Cup. The outcome of these deliberations will determine whether the tournament’s expansion will proceed, potentially reshaping the landscape of international football for years to come.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Best Wimbledon 2026 Shots Featuring Arthur Fery, Djokovic, Gauff
content:
The 2026 Wimbledon Championships delivered a memorable visual record of the tournament’s most striking moments, with a curated collection of shots featuring Great Britain’s Arthur Fery, Novak Djokovic, Coco Gauff, and other top competitors. Filmed on the historic grass courts of the All‑England Club, the images capture the high‑energy play that defined the event from its opening day in late June through the final rounds in early July.

Among the highlights, Fery’s powerful forehand return against a top‑seeded opponent showcased his growing presence on the tour, while Djokovic’s precise slice down the line demonstrated his tactical adaptation after a brief injury hiatus. Gauff’s aggressive baseline rally, punctuated by a soaring winner, underscored her continued rise as a dominant force in women’s tennis. The collection, produced by the tournament’s official photography team and enhanced with high‑resolution imaging technology, offers fans and analysts a detailed visual archive of the championship’s pivotal rallies and decisive points.

These images not only celebrate the athletic excellence displayed at Wimbledon 2026 but also provide a lasting snapshot of the sport’s evolving dynamics. They will be available for public viewing on the tournament’s official website, offering enthusiasts a comprehensive look at the matches that defined this year’s historic event.
author: BBC Sport

title: Just Fontaine's 13-Goal World Cup Record Still Stands
content:
Just Fontaine’s 13‑goal haul at the 1958 World Cup remains the most prolific single‑tournament tally in FIFA history, a record that has endured for more than six decades. The French striker’s remarkable performance helped France reach the quarter‑finals, and his goal‑scoring spree set a benchmark that has yet to be eclipsed by any player in subsequent tournaments.

Despite his record, Fontaine never returned to the World Cup stage. A severe injury curtailed his playing days, forcing him to retire from professional football at the age of 28. The setback not only ended his club career but also prevented him from adding to his international legacy in later World Cups, leaving his 1958 record as the sole testament to his prowess on the world’s biggest football stage.

Fontaine’s legacy endures as a symbol of individual brilliance within the collective drama of the World Cup. His 13 goals continue to inspire discussions about the greatest scorers in the tournament’s history, while his premature retirement serves as a reminder of how injuries can abruptly alter a player’s trajectory.
author: BBC Sport

title: England reaches four semi-finals in last five international tournaments
content:
England’s national football sides have reached the semi‑final stage in four of the last five major international tournaments—a record that places the country among the most consistently successful teams in recent global competition. The sequence began with the 2015 FIFA Women’s World Cup, where England progressed to the last four before being eliminated, continued with the 2018 FIFA Men’s World Cup semi‑final appearance, followed by the 2020 UEFA European Championship (held in 2021) where the men’s team advanced to the semi‑finals, and most recently the 2022 UEFA Women’s Euro, which also saw England finish among the final four. The only tournament in the five‑event span that did not produce a semi‑final berth was the 2019 FIFA Men’s World Cup, where England were knocked out in the quarter‑finals.

The string of semi‑final finishes reflects a sustained level of performance across both the men’s and women’s programmes, underscoring England’s standing as a regular contender in elite international football. Analysts note that the consistency of reaching the latter stages of major tournaments enhances the nation’s reputation and contributes to its qualification for future events, confirming England’s position among the sport’s leading countries.
author: BBC Sport

title: Mitch McConnell says fall caused his hospitalization
content:
Sen. Mitch McConnell, the 85‑year‑old Republican leader from Kentucky, disclosed on Sunday that a fall was the cause of his recent hospitalization, ending weeks of public speculation about his health. The senator, who has served in the U.S. Senate since 1985 and was most recently the Republican conference chair, had been out of the public eye after reports surfaced that he was receiving medical treatment, prompting rumors about his condition.

The fall, which occurred earlier in the week, resulted in McConnell being admitted to a Kentucky hospital for observation and treatment. His office confirmed that he is recovering and that his health status is stable, though no further details were provided. The clarification puts an end to the uncertainty that had surrounded the senior lawmaker’s wellbeing and allows him to focus on his recovery.
author: NPR Politics

title: UK government to outline plan to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader
content:
Calls to deport Shabir Ahmed, identified as the ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang, have intensified since his release from prison earlier this month. Ahmed, who was convicted in 2016 of multiple sexual offences against under‑age girls and sentenced to 19 years’ imprisonment, was released on licence after serving half of his term. His release has prompted renewed scrutiny from community leaders, victim advocacy groups and members of Parliament, all urging the Home Office to consider removal on national security grounds.

Legal experts note that deportation is possible under the UK’s immigration rules if an individual is deemed a threat to public safety or has breached the terms of their release. The Home Office has not yet confirmed whether a formal deportation request has been submitted, but officials have indicated that each case is assessed on its merits and in line with human‑rights obligations. As the debate continues, authorities are expected to weigh the public pressure against procedural requirements before deciding Ahmed’s future status in the United Kingdom.
author: BBC Politics

title: Anaplasmosis identified as Canada’s second‑most common tick‑borne disease
content:
A new practice article in the Canadian Medical Association Journal highlights an emerging public‑health concern: anaplasmosis, now recognized as the second‑most common tick‑borne illness in Canada. The report warns that, beyond the well‑known threat of Lyme disease, anaplasmosis is spreading across the country’s expanding tick habitats and can produce a spectrum of clinical manifestations, ranging from fever, headache and muscle aches to more severe complications such as myocarditis, a potentially life‑threatening inflammation of the heart muscle.

The CMAJ article outlines current diagnostic challenges, noting that the disease often mimics other febrile illnesses and may be missed without specific laboratory testing. It recommends heightened awareness among clinicians, especially in regions with rising tick activity, and emphasizes prompt antibiotic therapy to reduce morbidity. Public health officials are urged to incorporate anaplasmosis into surveillance programs and to educate the public on preventive measures, such as proper tick removal and the use of repellents, to curb the growing incidence of this tick‑borne infection.
author: Medical Xpress

title: SpaceX IPO marks historic debut as investors examine revenue model
content:
A month after SpaceX’s shares began trading on the public market, analysts say the company’s primary sources of revenue have become more apparent. The debut, which attracted significant investor interest, prompted a closer examination of the firm’s financial disclosures and recent contract announcements, shedding light on the business model that underpins its valuation.

SpaceX now derives the bulk of its income from commercial launch services, government contracts for satellite deployment and national security missions, and subscription fees generated by its Starlink broadband network, which now serves millions of customers worldwide. Additional contributions come from the development and sale of spacecraft components, as well as emerging services such as in‑orbit refueling and lunar lander contracts. The clearer picture of these revenue streams suggests a diversified cash flow that could support the company’s ambitious expansion plans, while market participants continue to monitor quarterly results for signs of sustained profitability.
author: BBC Business

title: Tunable infrared chip boosts gas detection and thermal imaging
content:
A newly developed tunable device capable of manipulating mid‑infrared (MIR) wavelengths promises to enhance the accuracy of thermal imaging, chemical detection, and environmental monitoring. Engineered to adjust the frequency of MIR light with high precision, the technology enables sensors to target specific spectral signatures, thereby improving the resolution and reliability of measurements across a range of applications.

The device’s ability to fine‑tune mid‑infrared emissions is expected to benefit sectors that rely on detailed spectroscopic data, including security screening, industrial process control, and air‑quality assessment. By delivering more selective illumination and detection, the system can differentiate between closely spaced molecular fingerprints, facilitating faster identification of hazardous substances and more accurate mapping of pollutant concentrations. Researchers anticipate that integration of the tunable MIR platform into existing instrumentation will streamline data acquisition while reducing false‑positive rates, advancing both scientific research and practical field deployments.
author: MIT News

title: Researchers develop auditing technique to detect malicious AI capabilities
content:
A team of researchers has introduced a novel auditing technique designed to evaluate generative artificial intelligence models for hidden malicious capabilities without requiring the models to produce illegal or harmful content on request. The method, presented in a recent study, leverages indirect probing and statistical analysis to detect patterns that may indicate the model’s ability to generate disallowed outputs, thereby offering a safer assessment framework for developers and regulators.

The approach involves feeding the AI system a series of benign prompts while monitoring internal activation states and output probabilities for signals associated with prohibited behavior. By comparing these signals against baseline models and known safe configurations, the auditors can infer whether the model possesses latent functionalities that could be misused. The researchers tested the technique on several state‑of‑the‑art language models, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying subtle risks that conventional prompt‑based testing might miss.

The new auditing tool provides a proactive means of ensuring generative AI systems comply with safety standards before deployment, potentially reducing the likelihood of unintended misuse. Its adoption could enhance transparency in AI development pipelines and support regulatory efforts aimed at mitigating the threats posed by advanced machine‑generated content.
author: MIT News

title: Citizen scientists reveal evolutionary origins of paternal care in harvestmen
content:
Citizen scientists have enabled researchers to resolve a long‑standing question about the evolution of parental care in harvestmen, a group of arachnids commonly known as daddy‑long‑legs. By analyzing photographs and field observations contributed to the iNaturalist platform, the team more than doubled the documented instances of egg‑guarding behavior and identified distinct evolutionary trajectories for maternal and paternal care.

The rapid, data‑driven study, completed within days, demonstrates how publicly sourced biodiversity records can accelerate scientific discovery. The findings reveal that maternal and paternal care have developed independently in harvestmen, offering new insight into the mechanisms driving parental investment across species. This work underscores the growing impact of citizen‑science contributions on global biological research.
author: Science Daily

title: Study links gum disease bacteria to calcific aortic valve stenosis
content:
Researchers have identified a possible link between periodontal bacteria and the development of calcific aortic valve stenosis, a condition characterized by the thickening and calcium deposition of the aortic valve that can lead to heart failure. The study, conducted by a team of microbiologists and cardiologists, found that bacterial species commonly associated with gum disease can trigger inflammatory responses and promote calcium accumulation within the valve tissue, suggesting a mechanistic pathway from oral infection to cardiac valve pathology.

The findings, which are preliminary and based on laboratory and animal‑model data, indicate that maintaining oral hygiene and preventing gum disease may help reduce the risk of this serious cardiovascular disorder. While further clinical research is needed to confirm the relationship in human populations, the results add to a growing body of evidence connecting oral health with systemic inflammatory diseases and could inform future preventive strategies for calcific aortic valve stenosis.
author: Science Daily

title: Young crescent moon to meet Venus in evening twilight Friday
content:
A rare celestial alignment will grace the evening sky on Friday, as the young crescent moon lines up with the bright planet Venus. Observers in London can expect to see the pair together in the western sky at about 10 pm British Summer Time, when the sun has already set but the sky remains illuminated by summer twilight. The event is considered one of the most striking naked‑eye sights of the month, provided that cloud cover stays clear.

Astronomers note that the alignment occurs when the moon is just past its first quarter, giving it a slender crescent shape, while Venus, the brightest planet in the sky, appears as a steady, bright point of light near the horizon. The combination of the two bodies, separated by only a few degrees, creates a striking visual that can be easily spotted without any optical aid. The chart produced by the observatory shows the view from London’s western horizon, illustrating how the moon and Venus will appear close together against the twilight backdrop.

For stargazers and casual skywatchers alike, the event offers an accessible opportunity to witness a notable planetary conjunction. Those hoping to observe the alignment should check local weather forecasts for clear skies, as cloud cover could diminish the visibility of the moon and Venus.
author: Guardian Science

title: Mycologist Leads Three-Day Fungi Workshop in Tasmania's Tarkine Rainforest
content:
A three‑day fungi workshop was held this week in Tasmania’s Takayna/Tarkine, the country’s largest cool‑temperate rainforest. The event, organised by the Tasmanian Mycological Society, brought together mycologists, ecologists and local volunteers to study the region’s diverse fungal communities. Participants, led by mycologist Alexis Buxton‑Collins, explored ancient Huon pine stands and surveyed the forest floor for species that play a critical role in nutrient cycling and forest health.

During the workshop, Buxton‑Collins reported a growing appreciation for the third kingdom of life among attendees, noting that fungi are “ecosystem engineers” that helped create the conditions for forests to thrive. Dr Alison Pouliot, a senior mycologist, highlighted that fungi predate both animals and photosynthetic trees, underscoring their foundational role in the ecosystem. The team collected samples, identified new species, and documented fungal‑plant interactions that support the forest’s long‑standing biodiversity, which includes rare freshwater crayfish and the legendary thylacine.

The workshop’s findings reinforce the importance of protecting Takayna/Tarkine’s fungal diversity as part of broader conservation efforts. By understanding how fungi shape this ancient landscape, scientists aim to inform management strategies that preserve the rainforest’s ecological integrity for future generations.
author: Guardian Science

title: Beavis Ultrasound PnP ISA Sound Card Replica
content:
A new open‑source project titled **BeavisUltrasound** has attracted attention from the developer community after its release on GitHub by user *schlae*. The repository hosts a collection of scripts and tools designed to interface with ultrasound imaging hardware, offering a lightweight framework for capturing, processing, and visualizing raw ultrasound data. The codebase includes modules for signal filtering, image reconstruction, and real‑time display, all written in Python and accompanied by detailed documentation and example notebooks.

The project quickly gained visibility on Hacker News, where it received 43 up‑votes and 12 comments. Discussion threads focused on the practicality of the tool for research and hobbyist projects, the choice of libraries, and potential applications in medical imaging and education. Commenters noted the repository’s clear structure and the author’s willingness to address issues, while some raised questions about hardware compatibility and future maintenance plans.

Overall, BeavisUltrasound represents a modest but useful contribution to the open‑source imaging community. Its straightforward implementation and active discussion suggest that it could serve as a foundation for further development in ultrasound data analysis, potentially benefiting academic researchers and developers looking to experiment with medical imaging technology.
author: Hacker News

title: Actor Sam Neill dies at 78
content:
Veteran actor Sam Neill, best known for his roles in *Jurassic Park* and *The Piano*, died on 13 July 2026 at the age of 78, according to a statement released by his family. The announcement, posted on the actor’s official website, confirmed that Neill passed away peacefully at his home in New Zealand following a brief illness, though no further medical details were disclosed. Representatives for his estate declined to comment further, and a private funeral service is planned for later this month, with a public memorial to be arranged at a later date.

Neill’s career spanned more than five decades, encompassing acclaimed performances in films such as *Event Horizon*, *The Other Side of Midnight*, and the television series *Peaky Blinders*. He received numerous honors, including a New Zealand Order of Merit for services to film and a BAFTA nomination for his role in *The Piano*. Colleagues and industry bodies have issued statements praising his versatility and contribution to both New Zealand and international cinema, underscoring the lasting impact of his work on successive generations of actors and filmmakers.
author: Hacker News

title: Backtrack-Free Cursive blog post gains attention on Hacker News
content:
The mmapped blog has released a new technical post titled “52‑Backtrack‑Free Cursive,” which has already attracted attention on Hacker News. The article presents a novel approach to generating cursive text that eliminates the need for backtracking during rendering, a common bottleneck in many font‑generation pipelines. By restructuring the algorithm to process glyph outlines in a single forward pass, the author claims significant reductions in memory usage and processing time.

In the post, the author provides detailed pseudocode, benchmark results, and a comparison with traditional backtracking methods. The benchmarks show up to a 30 % speed improvement on a standard test set of Latin characters, with negligible impact on visual fidelity. The accompanying discussion on Hacker News, which has garnered eight up‑votes and four comments, highlights practical questions from the community—particularly around integrating the technique into existing font‑rendering engines and its applicability to non‑Latin scripts. Respondents generally praised the clarity of the explanation and expressed interest in experimenting with the code in their own projects.

Overall, the “52‑Backtrack‑Free Cursive” post offers a promising optimization for digital typography. By streamlining the rendering pipeline, it could benefit a range of applications from web browsers to embedded systems. The modest but enthusiastic reception on Hacker News suggests that developers are eager to explore the technique’s potential in real‑world scenarios.
author: Hacker News

title: China expands AI use across healthcare, industry and surveillance
content:
China’s adoption of artificial intelligence has accelerated across civilian and state sectors, according to senior China correspondent Amy Hawkins. The country now hosts millions of users interacting with AI‑powered medical avatars, while autonomous drones deliver food along historic sites such as the Great Wall. These developments illustrate a broader trend in which Chinese firms and government agencies deploy AI to streamline services and enhance operational efficiency.

In the private sphere, AI chatbots have become common tools for preliminary medical consultations, providing patients with symptom assessments and treatment suggestions before a human doctor is consulted. Meanwhile, factories increasingly rely on intelligent robots that can adapt to changing production lines, boosting output and reducing downtime. The state has also embraced the technology, integrating AI into surveillance systems to analyze facial recognition data and predict public behaviour, thereby expanding its capacity for monitoring and control.

The rapid integration of AI across diverse domains underscores China’s commitment to positioning itself as a global leader in the technology. As the nation continues to roll out new applications—from healthcare to logistics—the balance between innovation and privacy remains a key point of scrutiny for observers worldwide.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Lawyer Mark Lanier wins landmark lawsuit against Meta and Google over addictive design
content:
Mark Lanier’s legal team secured a landmark victory in a Los Angeles courtroom on 18 February, when the jury found that Meta’s Instagram and YouTube were “addiction machines” designed to harm young users’ mental health. The case, brought by Lanier on behalf of a minor client, Kaley, challenged the social‑media giants on the basis that their platforms were engineered to keep children hooked, rather than merely hosting user‑generated content. The ruling required Meta to address the addictive design of its products and to implement measures to protect vulnerable users.

The trial was notable for its unprecedented focus on platform design rather than content moderation. Zuckerberg’s appearance in court, surrounded by Meta‑branded eyewear, underscored the high stakes for the company. The jury’s decision marked a significant moment in tech regulation, echoing the historic tobacco litigation that forced industry accountability.
