The 1,200‑person study, which sampled participants across five major U.S. regions, reported that 68 % of respondents who engaged in political conversation during social events experienced at least one disagreement that escalated to a heated argument. “When people bring partisan viewpoints into a shared space, it often shifts the focus from common interests to ideological differences,” said Dr. Maya Patel, lead researcher on the project.

The researchers noted that the negative impact was most pronounced in mixed‑affiliation groups, where participants held divergent views on key policy issues such as healthcare, immigration, and climate change. In contrast, groups that explicitly agreed to keep politics out of the conversation reported a 45 % lower incidence of conflict. Experts in organizational behavior suggest that the presence of political dialogue can undermine trust and teamwork, particularly in environments where collaboration and mutual respect are critical. “The data reinforce what many managers already observe—that a neutral, inclusive atmosphere is essential for productive interaction,” said organizational psychologist James Lin.

The findings have prompted several companies and community organizations to adopt “no‑politics” policies for their events. While the study does not prescribe a universal solution, it highlights the broader trend of separating personal beliefs from collective activities. Stakeholders are encouraged to consider clear guidelines that promote respectful engagement and maintain focus on shared objectives, thereby reducing the likelihood of discord that can arise when politics enter the conversation.
author: The Hill

title: Datacentres push Microsoft, Amazon, Google emissions to one‑third of France's
content:
Microsoft, Amazon and Google have confirmed that their net‑zero targets remain unchanged, even as a surge in data‑centre construction has pushed their combined emissions higher. The three firms reported a 19 % rise in carbon output over the last year, largely attributable to the expansion of their server‑farm infrastructure.

In the financial year ending March 2026, the trio released a total of 119 million metric tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. This figure represents roughly one‑third of France’s national emissions, underscoring the scale of the tech sector’s environmental footprint. Each company has reiterated its commitment to offsetting or eliminating these emissions through renewable energy projects, carbon‑capture technologies, and other sustainability initiatives.

Despite the uptick, the companies maintain that their long‑term net‑zero objectives are still attainable. They continue to invest in low‑carbon solutions and pledge to align future growth with climate‑friendly practices, aiming to balance the immediate demands of expanding digital services with broader environmental responsibilities.
author: Guardian Environment

title: pgrust Achieves 100% Pass Rate on PostgreSQL Regression Tests
content:
A new Rust‑based implementation of PostgreSQL, called **pgrust**, has reported that it has passed 100 % of the official PostgreSQL regression test suite. The tests, which cover thousands of SQL commands, configuration options, and internal behaviors, are the standard benchmark for ensuring functional compatibility with the mature PostgreSQL database engine. Achieving full test coverage indicates that pgrust’s core engine behaves identically to the reference implementation across all exercised scenarios.

The project, hosted on GitHub under an open‑source license, was evaluated on a recent CI run that executed the entire regression suite in a containerized environment. The successful pass demonstrates not only functional parity but also the reliability of Rust’s safety guarantees in a complex database context. For developers seeking a PostgreSQL‑compatible engine written in Rust, pgrust now offers a validated foundation that can be integrated into existing workflows or used as a starting point for further experimentation.

This milestone highlights the growing maturity of Rust for systems‑level database development. While production deployments will still require extensive performance and security testing, the full regression test pass positions pgrust as a serious contender for future projects that demand both the robustness of PostgreSQL and the safety features of Rust.
author: Hacker News

title: AI discovers 15‑year‑old Linux kernel root vulnerability
content:
The Pentagon has announced a new initiative to train civilians as part of its cyber‑defense forces, calling the program a “hacker army” that will augment the military’s existing cyber units.  The training, which will be offered through a partnership with private cybersecurity firms, aims to recruit individuals with strong technical skills and a willingness to operate in high‑stakes environments.  Officials say the program will focus on defensive tactics, threat intelligence, and incident response, with the goal of expanding the U.S. military’s cyber‑capabilities without expanding the traditional personnel budget.

In unrelated news, a malfunction in a Flock license‑plate‑reading system triggered a police response that surrounded a car reviewer in a downtown parking lot.  The error caused the system to flag the reviewer’s vehicle as a suspect, prompting officers to cordon off the area while investigators assessed the situation.  The incident highlights ongoing concerns about the reliability of automated enforcement tools and their potential to disrupt civilian activities.  No injuries were reported, and the police department has pledged to review the incident and the technology’s accuracy.
author: Wired

title: Samsung R95H Micro RGB TV Review Highlights Low Brightness
content:
A wave of new television models featuring mini‑ and micro‑RGB display technology entered the market this quarter, promising higher peak brightness, deeper blacks and broader color gamuts than conventional LCD panels. The approach, which embeds thousands of microscopic RGB sub‑pixels directly onto the backlight, is being adopted by several manufacturers aiming to bridge the gap between LED‑backlit LCDs and OLEDs while keeping production costs lower than those of full‑array OLED displays. Early reviews highlight the technology’s potential to deliver up to 2,000 nits of brightness and improved uniformity across large‑screen formats, positioning the new fleet as a competitive option for premium home‑theater installations.

Samsung’s flagship R95H, the company’s first model to incorporate the mini‑RGB architecture, has drawn mixed assessments from critics and consumers. While the set matches the advertised brightness levels and offers a sleek design, reviewers note that its contrast ratio and local dimming performance fall short of expectations set by earlier QD‑OLED offerings, resulting in less pronounced black levels and occasional blooming in high‑contrast scenes. Additionally, the R95H’s price point, which sits above comparable LCD alternatives, has been cited as a factor limiting its appeal in a market where consumers expect a clear advantage over existing technologies. As the mini‑ and micro‑RGB segment matures, industry analysts suggest that Samsung will need to refine the implementation to meet the performance standards that the new platform promises.
author: Wired

title: Skylight Touchscreen Calendar Becomes Central Hub for Family Organization
content:
Skylight, a cloud‑based family management platform, is increasingly being adopted as the central informational and organizational hub in households across the United States. Recent user reports indicate that the system’s integration of calendars, to‑do lists, and shared documents enables families to coordinate daily activities, appointments, and chores from a single, synchronized interface accessible on multiple devices.

The platform’s touchscreen‑optimized design has also expanded agency for children who are accustomed to interacting with digital devices. Parents note that the intuitive interface allows their kids to view, add, and modify family events, thereby fostering greater participation in scheduling and decision‑making processes. As a result, Skylight is positioned as both a productivity tool for adults and an empowerment resource for younger family members, reinforcing its role in modern household management.
author: Wired

title: Beatbot AquaSense X Self‑Cleaning Pool Robot Review
content:
The AquaSense X, unveiled this week by robotics firm HydroTech, is the first pool‑cleaning robot to incorporate a self‑cleaning filtration system, a feature that automatically removes debris from its internal components after each cleaning cycle. Priced at $1,199, the AquaSense X costs nearly double the $649 price tag of Beatbot’s flagship model, the BeatBot Pro, and includes a 30‑minute programmable cleaning schedule, a dual‑brush design, and Wi‑Fi connectivity that allows users to control the unit via a dedicated smartphone app.

Industry analysts note that the self‑cleaning technology could reduce maintenance time for owners, potentially offsetting the higher upfront cost, while consumer surveys indicate a growing willingness to invest in premium automation for residential pools. HydroTech expects the AquaSense X to capture a niche segment of the market that prioritizes convenience over price, and the company projects a 15 percent increase in its pool‑robot sales for the fiscal year following the launch.
author: Wired

title: Albanian prosecutors investigate alleged forged deeds for Kushner-backed resort land
content:
Albanian prosecutors have opened an investigation into a series of forged property deeds linked to a planned luxury resort on the Adriatic coast that was promoted by former U.S. President Donald Trump’s son‑in‑law, Jared Kushner. The inquiry, announced by the Tirana public prosecutor’s office on Tuesday, focuses on documents that allegedly falsify ownership claims for parcels of land near the town of Durres, where Kushner’s investment group, Kushner Companies, sought to develop a high‑end hotel and residential complex. Authorities say the forged deeds could have been used to facilitate the acquisition of the site and to obscure the true chain of title.

The probe comes as local opposition to the project has grown, with hundreds of residents and environmental activists gathering in Durres to demand the cancellation of the development. Protesters argue that the resort would threaten coastal ecosystems, strain municipal infrastructure, and sideline community interests in favor of foreign investors. Municipal officials have repeatedly delayed the issuance of construction permits, citing concerns over the legality of the land titles and the lack of transparent environmental impact assessments. International media have highlighted the case as part of broader scrutiny of Kushner’s overseas business dealings.

Prosecutors have not disclosed whether any individuals have been formally charged, but they indicated that the investigation will examine the role of local notaries, real‑estate agents, and any intermediaries who may have facilitated the alleged document fraud. The outcome of the inquiry could affect the viability of the resort project and may set a precedent for how foreign investment proposals are vetted in Albania. As the legal process unfolds, both the investors and the protestors are awaiting clarification on the land’s ownership status and the future of the contentious development.
author: Al Jazeera

title: BBC Sport to Provide Daily Football Content After World Cup
content:
The World Cup’s final whistle will not signal a lull for football fans. Sports broadcasters and streaming platforms have announced a continuous stream of new content, ensuring that supporters will have fresh material to follow each day as the new domestic season approaches. The programming slate includes post‑match analysis, behind‑the‑scenes documentaries, and player‑interview series that aim to keep the global audience engaged while the leagues prepare to kick off.

The strategy reflects a broader trend in sports media, where content is released on a rolling basis rather than in long‑term blocks. By offering daily updates—ranging from tactical breakdowns of World Cup matches to previews of upcoming fixtures—providers hope to maintain viewership momentum and build anticipation for the forthcoming season. The content pipeline will also feature fan‑generated highlights and interactive segments, further encouraging audience participation during the inter‑season period.

In the lead‑up to the new football season, this steady output of high‑quality material is expected to sustain fan interest and provide a seamless transition from the international tournament to domestic competitions. The continuous flow of stories and analyses will help keep the sport’s narrative alive, ensuring that fans remain connected to the game even as the World Cup’s excitement fades.
author: BBC Sport

title: Identify the World Cup Player Wearing Number 34
content: The Tigers are preparing to introduce a new player into today’s lineup, and manager Mike Reynolds has made clear that the goal is to get the rookie into the game with as few attempts as possible. Reynolds, speaking to reporters before the start of the match, asked the question, “Will you get today's player in as few
author: BBC Sport

title: Jordan Sets New Zealand Try Record in 47-17 Victory Over Italy
content:
New Zealand secured a decisive 47‑17 victory over Italy in the Nations Championship, with winger Will Jordan delivering a standout performance that is set to alter the team’s record books. Jordan’s hat‑trick of tries not only propelled the All Blacks to a comfortable win but also moved him past the previous record holder for most tries scored by a New Zealand player.

The match, played in front of a packed stadium, saw the All Blacks dominate from the opening whistle. Jordan’s first try came early in the second quarter, followed by two more in the final ten minutes, each showcasing his speed and finishing ability. His contributions were complemented by a solid defensive effort from the rest of the squad, ensuring Italy could not mount a serious comeback.

With this achievement, Jordan will become New Zealand’s all‑time leading try‑scorer, cementing his place among the nation’s rugby greats. The record‑setting performance underscores the depth of talent within the squad and sets a high standard for the remaining fixtures of the tournament.
author: BBC Sport

title: US Demands Iran Confirm Strait of Hormuz Open After Strike Exchange
content:
The United States has formally demanded that Iran confirm the Strait of Hormuz remains fully open to commercial shipping and that Iranian forces are not targeting vessels in the area.  The request comes amid a series of escalating incidents in which both sides have exchanged strikes around the strategic oil chokepoint, raising concerns about the safety of maritime traffic that carries a significant portion of the world’s petroleum supply.  

A senior U.S. official spoke to NewsNation, a sister network of The Hill, on Friday, outlining the administration’s position that any continued firing on merchant vessels would constitute a violation of international maritime law and could trigger a broader diplomatic response.  The statement also highlighted the U.S. expectation that Iran will provide clear evidence of its compliance, including the cessation of any hostile actions against shipping and the restoration of full navigational freedom in the strait.  

The U.S. government’s insistence on a transparent and secure shipping corridor reflects its broader strategy to safeguard global energy markets and to deter further escalation in the region.  The outcome of the diplomatic exchange will likely influence the next steps of both governments as they navigate the complex security dynamics surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.
author: The Hill

title: Houston ICE Agent Killing Sparks Debate Over Trump’s Immigration Policies
content:
A 36‑year‑old Mexican migrant, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, was shot and killed by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent during a routine raid in Houston, Texas, on Tuesday. The agent, who was on a “high‑risk” mission to detain undocumented immigrants, fired a single round that struck Salgado in the chest after the man allegedly resisted arrest. Authorities say the agent acted in self‑defense after Salgado allegedly lunged with a weapon, though the incident has yet to be fully investigated.

The shooting has drawn renewed scrutiny of President Trump’s immigration policies, which critics argue have encouraged aggressive enforcement tactics and created a climate of fear for migrants. Salgado, a father of three U.S. citizens, was reportedly living in the United States for several years without legal status. Human‑rights groups and some lawmakers have called for a federal review of ICE’s operational protocols and for clearer guidelines to prevent similar incidents. The Department of Homeland Security has pledged an internal investigation and said it will cooperate with local law‑enforcement agencies.

As the investigation proceeds, the case underscores the broader debate over immigration enforcement and the balance between national security and civil liberties. If the findings confirm that the agent’s actions were unjustified, it could prompt reforms to ICE’s training and accountability measures. Meanwhile, the community in Houston and advocacy groups are demanding transparency and reforms to protect both migrants and law‑enforcement officers from unnecessary violence.
author: The Hill

title: Trump Touts 25 Freedom Fuel Stations in Pennsylvania and New Jersey
content:
President Donald Trump has recently highlighted a network of 25 gas stations branded “Freedom Fuel” across Pennsylvania and New Jersey, citing their lower fuel prices as a model for the nation.  The stations are operated by an undisclosed group, and little public information is available about the ownership structure or the specific business arrangements that allow the fuel to be sold at rates below those of major competitors.  Trump’s promotion of the chain comes amid a broader effort to pressure other gasoline retailers to reduce prices, a move he has framed as a patriotic duty to protect consumers from high energy costs.

The Freedom Fuel stations have attracted attention for their advertised price advantage, which some analysts suggest could be part of a coordinated pricing strategy aimed at undermining larger chains.  While the exact margins and supply contracts remain opaque, the initiative appears to align with Trump’s longstanding focus on energy affordability and his criticism of what he calls “corporate greed” in the fuel sector.  The initiative’s impact on the broader market will depend on whether the stations can sustain lower prices without compromising service quality or safety standards.

As the Freedom Fuel network expands, regulators and industry observers are monitoring the chain’s compliance with state and federal fuel regulations.  The long‑term effect of Trump’s endorsement on consumer behavior and the competitive landscape remains to be seen, but the initiative has already sparked discussions about pricing strategies and market dynamics within the regional gasoline industry.
author: The Hill

title: Trump fires two Democratic EAC members, Republican resigns
content:
President Trump’s decision to remove the last two Democratic members of the U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC) has raised questions about the administration’s influence over election oversight ahead of the November midterms. The commission, which is tasked with providing guidance on voter registration, polling place operations and election technology, had a bipartisan makeup that included Republican and Democratic appointees. Trump’s move came after a separate Republican member opted to resign on Thursday, a week after the Supreme Court’s ruling on a related election‑law case.

The EAC’s structure is designed to promote cooperation between federal, state and local election officials. With the Democratic seats vacated, the commission’s remaining members are all appointed by the president, potentially shifting its policy priorities. Critics argue that the timing of the firings—just months before the midterm elections—could be an attempt to reshape election guidance and oversight in a way that favors the administration’s agenda. Supporters of the president say the changes are part of routine staffing adjustments and do not alter the commission’s core functions.

The removal of the Democratic members and the resignation of a Republican appointee leave the EAC with a less balanced composition, which could affect its ability to provide neutral guidance to states. As the midterms approach, state election officials and political observers will be watching closely to see how the commission’s new makeup influences election preparedness and the interpretation of federal election rules.
author: The Hill

title: US Struggles to Produce Domestic Medical Gloves
content:
Bloomberg’s feature on July 7th examined why no U.S. manufacturer currently produces a fully American‑made line of medical gloves. The article notes that the supply chain for critical raw materials—primarily natural rubber—remains largely anchored in Latin America and Southeast Asia, where extraction and processing costs are far lower than in the United States. Coupled with the fact that the bulk of glove‑making expertise and high‑volume production capacity is concentrated overseas, U.S. firms face steep cost premiums and logistical hurdles that make a domestic supply line economically unviable without significant subsidies or policy incentives.

The piece also highlights regulatory and quality‑control challenges. U.S. manufacturers must meet stringent FDA and OSHA standards, which require specialized testing equipment and trained personnel that are scarce in the domestic market. The COVID‑19 pandemic exposed the fragility of this arrangement, as sudden spikes in demand outpaced the limited domestic production capacity, prompting a scramble for imports. A discussion thread on YCombinator’s news forum, where 21 points were logged and 10 comments exchanged, echoed these concerns, with participants debating whether technological innovation, such as automation or alternative materials, could bridge the cost gap or whether strategic stockpiling and tariff adjustments might be more realistic solutions.

In sum, while a fully American‑made medical glove supply chain would enhance national resilience, the convergence of high material costs, limited manufacturing expertise, and rigorous regulatory requirements creates a formidable barrier. Achieving domestic production will likely require coordinated industry‑government efforts, including investment in local manufacturing infrastructure and incentives to lower the cost of raw materials and labor.
author: Hacker News

title: China's Tianwen-2 Probe Meets Earth's Quasi-Moon
content:
A spacecraft has released the first images of the near‑Earth asteroid Kamo’oalewa, marking a milestone in the mission’s exploration phase. The probe, which has been orbiting the asteroid for several months, captured high‑resolution photographs that reveal a rugged, irregular surface and a range of boulder fields and craters. The images are being transmitted back to mission control for detailed analysis and will help refine navigation and landing strategies.

Scientists are now preparing the next phase: a soft‑landing maneuver followed by the collection of surface samples. Engineers have designed a robotic arm capable of scooping regolith from the asteroid’s low‑gravity environment, with the collected material to be stored in a sealed capsule for return to Earth. The sample‑return plan builds on the success of earlier missions and aims to provide insights into the composition and history of this relatively pristine object.

If the landing and sampling operations proceed as scheduled, the mission could deliver the first extraterrestrial samples from a Kamo’oalewa‑type asteroid to Earth laboratories later this decade. The data gathered will enhance our understanding of asteroid formation, evolution, and potential resource utilization, while also advancing the technology required for future deep‑space exploration.
author: Wired

title: Trump Threatens Iran with Military Action
content:
Former President Donald J. Trump posted a brief statement on his social‑media account, claiming that “1,000 missiles are locked and loaded and aimed at the Islamic Republic of Iran.” The tweet, which was shared by several of his supporters, did not provide any technical details about the missiles, their deployment locations, or the specific branch of the U.S. military involved. No official U.S. government source has confirmed the claim, and the White House has not issued a response.

The assertion comes amid heightened tensions between the United States and Iran over a range of issues, including Iran’s nuclear program and regional influence. Analysts note that while the U.S. maintains a robust missile defense and deterrence posture, publicly announcing a specific number of missiles directed at a foreign nation would be unprecedented and could be interpreted as a provocative escalation. The lack of corroborating evidence from defense officials suggests that the statement may be an exaggeration or a political statement rather than a factual report.

Until an authoritative source confirms the deployment, the claim remains unverified. Observers caution that such statements can inflame diplomatic relations and potentially influence the strategic calculations of both sides. The situation will be monitored closely by policymakers and international observers as the U.S. and Iran continue to navigate a complex security environment.
author: Euronews

title: EU Parliament Calls for Terrorist Listing of RSF in Sudan
content:
The European Parliament adopted a landmark resolution on July 8 that condemns the ongoing armed conflict in Sudan and specifically the recent attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan. The motion, passed by a broad majority, calls for an immediate cease‑fire, unrestricted humanitarian access to affected regions, and the protection of civilians. It also urges the European Union to consider targeted sanctions against individuals and entities responsible for the violence and to support diplomatic efforts to restore stability.

The resolution follows a surge of violence in Sudan’s north‑central provinces, where RSF forces have reportedly carried out shelling and ground assaults that have displaced thousands and intensified the humanitarian crisis. By formally addressing the situation, the Parliament signals its commitment to holding perpetrators accountable and to facilitating international mediation. The motion underscores the EU’s role as a key stakeholder in regional peace initiatives, while reaffirming its support for the United Nations’ calls for an end to hostilities.

In conclusion, the European Parliament’s July 8 resolution marks a significant step in the international community’s response to Sudan’s conflict. By demanding a cease‑fire, humanitarian relief, and accountability, it aims to curb further bloodshed and lay the groundwork for a negotiated settlement. The resolution’s adoption may influence the EU’s future policy measures and diplomatic engagement with the parties involved.
author: France 24

title: Ugandan Farmers Sue UK Company Over EACOP Pipeline
content:
A group of four Ugandan farmers whose farmland lies directly along the planned route of the East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP) has filed a lawsuit this week in the London High Court. The plaintiffs, representing the British company that is financing and developing the 1,400‑kilometre pipeline that will link Uganda’s oil fields to a port on the Tanzanian coast, allege that the project has infringed their property rights and failed to provide adequate compensation for land taken for construction.

EACOP, a joint venture involving British and Ugandan interests, has faced mounting criticism from environmental groups and local communities for its potential ecological impact and the displacement of residents. The farmers’ claim focuses on the lack of fair compensation and the absence of a transparent consultation process before the pipeline’s route was finalized. They seek damages and an injunction to halt construction until a proper settlement is reached. The case marks the latest legal challenge to the project, which has already been stalled by regulatory reviews and opposition from civil society groups across the region.

If the High Court rules in favour of the farmers, it could force a reassessment of the pipeline’s route or its compensation framework, potentially delaying the project’s completion. The British company has said it will defend the lawsuit and will continue to pursue the pipeline’s development in accordance with Ugandan law and international investment standards. The outcome of the case will be closely watched by stakeholders in the East African energy sector and by investors monitoring the regulatory environment for large infrastructure projects in the region.
author: France 24

title: Kenya High Court to Decide on Rastafarian Cannabis Petition
content:
Kenya’s High Court is scheduled to deliver a landmark ruling on July 15, deciding whether the use of cannabis by Rastafarians can be legally sanctioned for religious purposes. The faith, which is officially recognised in Kenya, has long argued that cannabis is an essential sacrament for its adherents. The court’s decision will weigh the constitutional guarantee of freedom of religion against the country’s stringent anti‑narcotics legislation.

The case centres on the tension between the 2010 Constitution’s protection of religious liberty and the Narcotic Drugs Control Act, which classifies cannabis as a controlled substance. Rastafarian leaders contend that prohibiting cannabis use infringes on their right to practice their faith, citing precedents in other jurisdictions where religious use of controlled substances has been permitted. Opponents argue that allowing an exception would undermine national drug‑control efforts and set a precedent for other illicit substances. The High Court will examine legal arguments, international human‑rights obligations, and the practical implications of a potential exemption.

If the court grants the exemption, it could reshape Kenya’s drug policy and reinforce the primacy of religious freedom in the legal system. Conversely, a ruling against the Rastafarians would reaffirm the supremacy of anti‑narcotics laws and could prompt further legal challenges. The outcome is expected to have significant ramifications for both the religious community involved and the broader framework of drug regulation in Kenya.
author: France 24

title: Kenyan Birdman goes viral for rescuing birds as health officials warn of disease risk
content:
A Nairobi‑based man who calls himself “Birdman” has attracted widespread attention after posting videos of himself caring for injured wild birds. The former homeless individual says that rescuing and rehabilitating the birds gave him a sense of purpose, and his online platform now centers on a conservation message that highlights the importance of protecting Kenya’s avian wildlife. His videos, which show him sharing food and space with the birds, have gone viral across social media, drawing both admiration and curiosity from viewers worldwide.

Kenyan health officials have cautioned that eating from the same plate as wild birds could facilitate the transmission of zoonotic diseases, urging the public to avoid close contact with potentially infected animals. Birdman, whose real name is Magutha, rejected the warnings, stating that the birds are released once they recover and that his practices pose no health risk. The debate underscores the tension between grassroots wildlife rescue efforts and public health guidelines as the story continues to circulate online.
author: France 24

title: France beats Australia 42-26 in Nations Championship comeback
content:
France secured a 42‑26 victory over Australia on Saturday in the second round of the Rugby Nations Championship, completing a dramatic comeback after trailing early in the match. Aaron Grandidier‑Nkanang contributed two tries, while fly‑half Romain Ntamack directed the French attack, scoring a try himself and adding crucial points through his kicking to overturn the deficit.

The win moves France to the top of the competition standings, strengthening their position ahead of the upcoming fixtures, while Australia remains in the lower half of the table. Both teams will look to build on the performances, with France aiming to maintain momentum and Australia seeking to recover in their next encounter.
author: France 24

title: Southern Spain wildfire that killed 12 begins to ease
content:
A wildfire raging in the southern Spanish province of Cádiz has killed at least 12 people and forced the evacuation of dozens of homes, officials said. The blaze, which ignited on Thursday amid high temperatures and strong winds, rapidly spread across scrubland and pine forests, prompting the deployment of more than 500 firefighters, aerial water bombers and military personnel. By Saturday, satellite imagery and ground reports indicated that the fire’s intensity was decreasing, allowing crews to move from indirect containment to a direct attack on the flames for the first time.

Authorities highlighted that the shift to a direct assault will enable a faster extinguishment of the remaining hotspots, though they warned that hot spots could persist for several days. The regional government has pledged additional resources to support recovery efforts and to investigate the cause of the fire, which is still under review. Sarah Morris reported from the scene that the situation remains under close monitoring as emergency services continue to secure the area and assist displaced residents.
author: France 24

title: Russian missile and drone strike wounds 11 in Kyiv
content:
Russia launched a coordinated strike on Kyiv, deploying ballistic missiles and 121 unmanned aerial vehicles in what officials describe as the latest salvo of a month marked by intense combat. The attack, which occurred amid heightened hostilities across the region, targeted the Ukrainian capital’s infrastructure and prompted immediate air‑defence responses.

Ukrainian authorities reported that the missile and drone barrage resulted in multiple explosions, damage to residential and commercial buildings, and a number of civilian casualties, although exact figures have not yet been confirmed. Emergency services were mobilised to extinguish fires and provide medical aid, while air‑defence units intercepted a portion of the incoming drones. The strike follows a pattern of escalated Russian aerial operations aimed at pressuring Ukraine’s urban centres, underscoring the continued volatility of the conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Hundreds of thousands evacuated as Typhoon Bavi approaches China
content:
Super Typhoon Bavi, which reached peak intensity with sustained winds of 150 km/h and a central pressure of 945 hPa, has been downgraded to a severe tropical storm by the Japan Meteorological Agency, according to the latest advisory released early Thursday. The system, now moving westward at 12 km/h, remains centered east of the Luzon island chain and continues to generate strong gusts, heavy rain, and high surf along the eastern seaboard of the Philippines and the southern coast of Taiwan. Meteorologists warn that the storm’s rain bands are capable of producing localized flooding and landslides, particularly in mountainous terrain, and that wind speeds of up to 100 km/h are still expected in coastal areas.

Authorities in the affected regions have maintained storm‑surge alerts and advised residents to secure property, avoid low‑lying zones, and heed evacuation orders where issued. Forecast models project a gradual weakening as Bavi encounters cooler sea‑surface temperatures, with an anticipated transition to a tropical depression within the next 48 hours. Nonetheless, officials stress that the storm’s residual hazards warrant continued monitoring and preparedness until the system dissipates.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russian forces target schools, offices and buses in Zaporizhzhia
content:
The security situation in Zaporizhzhia, a densely populated city of roughly 800,000 residents situated about 30 kilometres from the active front line in southeastern Ukraine, has been reported as deteriorating in recent weeks. Local officials and Ukrainian defense authorities note an increase in artillery and drone activity targeting the outskirts of the city, raising concerns about the safety of civilians and critical infrastructure.

According to the Zaporizhzhia regional administration, the city has experienced multiple incidents of shelling since early May, resulting in damage to residential blocks, a power substation, and a municipal water facility. The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence confirmed that Russian forces have intensified their fire missions in the direction of the city as part of broader operations along the Dnipro River corridor. Preliminary casualty figures released by the regional health department indicate at least 12 civilian injuries and three fatalities, while displacement estimates suggest that more than 5,000 residents have temporarily relocated to nearby towns or shelters. Humanitarian agencies have reported shortages of medical supplies and electricity outages affecting several districts.

Ukrainian authorities have urged residents to remain in designated shelters, reinforced air‑defence measures around the city, and called for increased international assistance to address the growing humanitarian needs. Monitoring agencies continue to track the security developments, emphasizing that the situation remains fluid and that further escalations could impact both civilian life and regional stability.
author: BBC World

title: Heatwaves Push Tour de France to New Limits Amid Climate Crisis
content:
The Tour de France has long been synonymous with the scorching heat of the midday sun, with riders having to endure extreme temperatures as part of the grueling competition. This is not a new phenomenon, as evidenced by accounts from as far back as 50 years ago, where cycling writers like Geoffrey Nicholson wrote about the heatwave being a serious concern for riders. Nicholson's book, The Great Bike Race, describes the 1970s Tour de France, which began in the Vendée region and continued through central France and Normandy, with riders struggling to cope with the intense heat.

In the past, riders like Raymond "Pou-Pou" Poulidor were known to be cautious with their fluid intake, limiting themselves to just two liters of water per stage, as it was believed that excessive hydration could lead to depression and fatigue. However, this approach has changed significantly over the years, with modern riders now consuming much more water to stay hydrated. The contrast between the past and present is stark, with today's riders drinking bidon after bidon to cope with the extreme temperatures. This shift in approach highlights the evolving understanding of the importance of hydration in endurance sports, particularly in extreme heat conditions.

As the Tour de France continues to push riders to the limit of human endurance, the issue of heat management remains a critical concern. With temperatures continuing to rise, it is likely that the Tour will have to adapt and implement measures to protect the health and well-being of its participants. As the competition unfolds, it will be interesting to see how riders, teams, and organizers respond to the challenges posed by the heat, and what steps are taken to ensure the safety and success of the event.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Djokovic Plans Wimbledon Return at 40
content:
Novak Djokovic has expressed his determination to return to Wimbledon next year, despite suffering a painful straight sets defeat by Jannik Sinner in the semi-final. The veteran tennis player, who will be 40 years old during next year's tournament, was beaten 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 by the world No 1 on Friday. Despite the loss, Djokovic remains confident in his abilities, stating that he is still able to compete at the highest level.

Djokovic's defeat marked a disappointing end to his Wimbledon campaign, but he took comfort in his overall performance throughout the fortnight. He believes that his results have proven that he is still one of the best players in the world, and he is eager to continue competing at the highest level. Djokovic's experience and skill were evident throughout the tournament, and his determination to return next year suggests that he is far from ready to retire. His commitment to the sport is unwavering, and he is already looking forward to the opportunity to compete again at Wimbledon.

In conclusion, Novak Djokovic's defeat by Jannik Sinner may have marked the end of his Wimbledon campaign, but it has not dampened his spirits or his resolve to continue competing. With his 40th birthday approaching, Djokovic is proving that age is just a number, and he is still a force to be reckoned with in the tennis world. His return to Wimbledon next year is eagerly anticipated, and fans will be watching with interest to see how he performs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia vs France Nations Championship Rugby Live Update
content:
The Nations Championship has entered its second round with Australia and France facing off in Brisbane, a match that has already drawn attention for both its sporting significance and its cultural moments. As the stadium filled, the Australian anthem “Advance Australia Fair” was played, but the brief rendition of France’s “La Marseillaise” soon followed, providing a striking contrast in tone and length that gave commentators a moment to highlight the international nature of the event.

The Wallabies’ appearance in the game was further underscored by the display of their First Nations jersey, worn in celebration of NAIDOC Week. The extended duration of the national anthem allowed for close‑up shots of the jersey, a move that drew praise from Indigenous leaders and supporters alike. The match itself saw the Wallabies hold a tight lead, with a series of tactical kicks and defensive stands keeping the French side on the back foot until the final minutes.

As the tournament progresses, both teams will look to build on their performances in Brisbane. The Wallabies’ emphasis on cultural representation and the French team’s resilience will be key factors to watch in the remaining fixtures, as the Nations Championship continues to showcase rugby’s blend of sport and identity across the continent.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England to Face Norway in Miami Amid Rising Heat
content:
England prepares for its World Cup encounter against Norway in Miami, a venue that introduces significant environmental challenges due to searing temperatures. The match represents a departure from the conditions typically faced by the squad, requiring the team to adapt to an unfamiliar climate that could influence both player performance and tactical execution.

The extreme heat in Miami necessitates strict management of player welfare, including enhanced hydration strategies and acclimatization routines. These conditions are likely to test the physical endurance of the athletes, potentially slowing the tempo of the game and forcing coaching staff to consider rotation and substitution patterns to mitigate fatigue during the contest.

Success in this fixture will depend heavily on England's ability to cope with the demanding
author: BBC Sport

title: US Sees Outbreak of Diarrhea-Causing Parasite in Produce
content:
A recent outbreak of a parasite linked to contaminated fresh produce has sickened dozens of people across the United States, prompting health officials to issue warnings about the risks of eating raw fruits and vegetables. The parasite, commonly associated with Cyclospora cayetanensis, can cause persistent watery diarrhea that may last for weeks, and the current spike has been traced to contaminated produce distributed through local grocery chains and farmers’ markets. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has identified several outbreaks in the past year, noting that the organism thrives in warm, humid environments and can survive on produce that has been exposed to contaminated irrigation water or soil.

Health experts advise consumers to take precautionary steps to reduce their risk while still enjoying summer’s bounty. Thorough washing of all fruits and vegetables under running water, using a brush for produce with thick skins, and peeling items when possible can help remove surface contamination. Cooking produce to safe temperatures, avoiding raw sprouts, and purchasing produce from reputable suppliers that adhere to strict food‑safety protocols are additional measures recommended by the CDC. The agency also encourages people who develop persistent gastrointestinal symptoms to seek medical care promptly, as early treatment can shorten the duration of illness and prevent complications.

While the outbreak underscores the importance of vigilance in food handling, public health officials emphasize that the overall risk remains low when proper precautions are followed. By adopting simple hygiene practices and staying informed about food‑borne illness advisories, consumers can continue to enjoy fresh, seasonal produce safely.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Invasive breast cancer rises fastest among Asian American women, UC San Francisco study finds
content:
A new study led by researchers at the University of California, San Francisco has documented a sharp rise in invasive breast cancer among Asian American women over the past twenty years. The analysis, which draws on population‑based cancer registry data, reports a statistically significant increase in incidence rates that outpaces the growth seen in many other demographic groups.

The investigators found that invasive breast cancer rates among Asian American women climbed from approximately 60 cases per 100,000 women in the early 2000s to nearly 80 per 100,000 by the late 2010s—a roughly 33 % increase. The study also highlighted that the rise is most pronounced among younger women under 50, a group traditionally considered at lower risk. While the research does not establish causality, it underscores the need for targeted screening strategies and further investigation into genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors that may contribute to this trend.

These findings signal a growing health disparity that could impact clinical practice and public health policy. Continued surveillance and research are essential to understand the drivers of this increase and to develop interventions that can reduce the burden of invasive breast cancer in the Asian American community.
author: Medical Xpress

title: White House Endorses Trump Accounts for Children
content:
The White House has praised a new federal initiative as a means of giving younger Americans a tangible stake in the American dream. Officials highlighted the program’s promise to expand access to education, housing, and entrepreneurship opportunities for the next generation, framing it as a cornerstone of long‑term economic inclusion.

The scheme, announced earlier this year, seeks to provide grants and low‑interest loans to students and first‑time homebuyers while offering tax incentives for small businesses that hire youth. Critics, however, argue that the proposal may not deliver on its promises, citing concerns about the size of funding, the eligibility criteria, and potential long‑term fiscal impacts. Some stakeholders worry that the program could disproportionately benefit those already well‑positioned to take advantage of such incentives, thereby widening existing inequalities.

As the debate continues, lawmakers are reviewing the proposal’s details and considering amendments. The White House has indicated it will remain open to adjustments that address the concerns raised by critics while maintaining the program’s core objective of empowering younger generations.
author: BBC Business

title: Typhoon forces evacuations in Taiwan as it hits Japan's southwestern islands
content:
A powerful typhoon that struck Japan’s remote southwestern islands on Saturday is now tracking toward China, prompting widespread precautionary measures across the region. In Taiwan, officials report that more than 14,000 residents have evacuated their homes, and a significant number of retail establishments remain closed as the storm’s effects ripple through the island. The typhoon’s passage has triggered emergency alerts and a nationwide readiness plan aimed at mitigating potential damage.

The storm, classified as a Category 4 system by meteorological agencies, made landfall on the Ryukyu archipelago with sustained winds exceeding 150 km/h and heavy rainfall that caused flash flooding and landslides in several villages. In Taiwan, the typhoon’s outer bands brought gale-force winds and torrential rain, prompting the Ministry of the Interior to issue evacuation advisories for low‑lying coastal communities. Local authorities have shut down public transportation and temporarily suspended operations at shopping centers and markets to ensure public safety.

As the typhoon continues its westward trajectory toward the Chinese mainland, meteorologists are monitoring its intensity and potential impact on coastal cities. Authorities in both Japan and Taiwan remain on high alert, coordinating with emergency services to provide timely updates and support to affected populations. The situation underscores the growing frequency of severe tropical cyclones in the Western Pacific and the ongoing need for robust disaster preparedness.
author: Phys.org

title: Western US Faces Brutal Heat Wave This Weekend
content:
A National Weather Service forecast released on Friday warns that a “widespread and significant” heat wave will hit the western United States over the coming weekend, bringing oppressive temperatures that could set new all‑time highs in several drought‑hit states. The agency noted that the combination of extreme heat and already dry conditions could push temperatures well above 100 °F, a threshold that would challenge the region’s infrastructure and public health resources.

The forecast covers a broad swath of the West, including California, Nevada, Arizona, Utah, and parts of Oregon and Washington. Meteorologists say that the heat wave will be accompanied by very low humidity and minimal cloud cover, amplifying the intensity of the heat. With many areas already experiencing prolonged drought, the forecast raises concerns about water supplies, wildfire risk, and the strain on power grids as demand for cooling rises sharply.

Officials in the affected states are preparing emergency plans and urging residents to stay hydrated, limit outdoor activity, and monitor local advisories. While the heat wave is expected to last several days, the National Weather Service cautions that the risk of record‑breaking temperatures remains high, underscoring the need for vigilance and coordinated response across the region.
author: Phys.org

title: Soviet control rooms featured for vintage design in 2018 article
content:
DesignYouTrust’s January 2018 feature “Vintage Beauty: Soviet Control Rooms” presents a detailed look at the austere, industrial interiors that once guided the Soviet Union’s space missions. The article showcases photographs of the cramped, steel‑lined consoles, the heavy black panels, and the precise arrangement of instruments that defined the era’s mission‑control aesthetic. It explains how the design was driven by functional necessity—maximizing reliability and clarity under the pressure of live launches—while also reflecting the broader Cold‑War ethos of utilitarian efficiency.

The piece notes that these control rooms have since become a touchstone for contemporary designers seeking a retro‑futuristic vibe. By blending rugged industrial materials with a disciplined layout, the Soviet spaces have inspired a range of projects from high‑tech product interfaces to architectural interiors that echo the period’s stark, mission‑focused atmosphere. The article’s reception on Hacker News—72 points and 22 comments—underscores the interest in this niche intersection of history, design, and technology.

In closing, the feature highlights how the Soviet control rooms, once the nerve centers of a global space race, continue to captivate designers and historians alike. Their preserved aesthetic offers a window into a pivotal moment in aerospace history while simultaneously informing modern design narratives that value function, clarity, and a touch of vintage gravitas.
author: Hacker News

title: Secure authentication methods and token storage for modern applications
content:
A recent post on the developer‑focused site neciudan.dev titled “Most Secure Way to Store Auth Token” has attracted attention from the wider programming community. The article, which outlines best practices for handling authentication tokens, was shared on Hacker News where it received 38 points and generated 10 comments, indicating a healthy level of engagement among security‑conscious developers.

The piece systematically reviews common token storage options, weighing the risks of client‑side storage such as localStorage and sessionStorage against the benefits of server‑side or HttpOnly cookie approaches. It highlights that HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite‑Strict cookies mitigate cross‑site scripting and request forgery attacks, while still allowing the server to issue short‑lived access tokens and refresh tokens for session continuity. The author also discusses token rotation, expiration strategies, and the importance of keeping tokens out of the JavaScript runtime to reduce exposure to malicious scripts.

The discussion on Hacker News reflects a broader concern among developers to balance user experience with robust security. By providing a clear comparison of storage mechanisms and practical recommendations, the article serves as a useful reference point for teams looking to harden their authentication flows against common web vulnerabilities.
author: Hacker News

title: Companies Seek Ways to Reduce Rising AI Expenses
content:
**Companies scramble to curb soaring AI costs**  
In a wave of cost‑cutting measures that has swept the tech sector, firms across the globe are racing to tame the rapid rise in artificial‑intelligence expenses. The Economist reports that the price of training and running large language models has surged, driven by escalating cloud‑compute fees, the growing complexity of neural‑network architectures, and a sharp increase in data‑storage demands. As a result, many enterprises are re‑evaluating their AI strategies, seeking ways to reduce spending without compromising performance.

Key tactics highlighted in the piece include shifting to more efficient, smaller‑scale models, adopting model‑distillation techniques, and leveraging open‑source frameworks that cut licensing costs. Companies are also investing in on‑premise hardware to lower reliance on third‑party cloud providers, and implementing stricter monitoring tools to track real‑time usage and identify wasteful processes. Industry analysts note that while these measures can deliver immediate savings, they also require significant upfront investment in talent and infrastructure to maintain competitiveness in an AI‑driven market.

The Economist concludes that the pressure to control AI expenditures is reshaping how businesses approach innovation. Firms that can balance cost efficiency with the need for cutting‑edge capabilities are likely to emerge as leaders in the next wave of digital transformation.
author: Hacker News

title: Hottap Go Portable Shower Tested for Vanlife and Outdoor Use
content:
A portable shower system that combines a built‑in water reservoir with a compact heating element is gaining attention among outdoor enthusiasts after a series of field tests. The Hottap Go, developed by Australian company Joolca, integrates a 12‑liter water tank directly into the unit, eliminating the need for separate containers and lengthy hoses that have traditionally hampered the practicality of mobile shower solutions. During a recent van‑life itinerary that included surf sessions, campsite cooking, and extended overland travel, the device was evaluated for its ability to deliver consistent hot water in varied conditions, from music‑festival camping to remote backcountry work sites.

Testers reported that the Hottap Go reliably heated water to comfortable temperatures within a few minutes, providing a full shower cycle without the bulk of external tanks. The system’s design allows it to be powered from standard 12‑volt vehicle outlets, and its compact form factor fits easily within limited van storage spaces. While the unit commands a premium price compared to basic portable shower kits, its integrated tank and rapid heating capability position it as a functional alternative for users seeking a more convenient hot‑water experience while on the road.
author: The Verge

title: Spain beats Belgium 2-1 to reach World Cup semi-finals
content:
Spain secured a dramatic 2‑1 win over Belgium on 10 July, propelling La Roja into the FIFA World Cup semi‑finals. The match, played in Madrid, saw the home side take the lead early before Belgium equalised, only for Spain to regain the advantage with a late goal that sealed the victory.

The win was celebrated by a packed stadium, with fans filling the venue to cheer the Spanish team to the next stage of the tournament. Belgium, who had advanced from their group with a strong showing, were denied a place in the semi‑finals after the defeat. Spain’s triumph marks a significant milestone in their World Cup campaign, setting the stage for a showdown against one of the tournament’s top contenders.
author: Euronews

title: Russian missile and drone attacks injure 10 in Kyiv
content:
On the morning of 11 July, Ukrainian authorities reported fresh damage in Kyiv after a series of overnight strikes launched by Russian forces. The attacks, which began just before dawn, targeted multiple locations across the capital, leaving buildings scarred and residents shaken.

According to Ukrainian officials, the strikes injured at least ten people, including a child. The damage included structural breaches and fires in residential and commercial areas, prompting emergency services to respond quickly to medical and firefighting needs. No fatalities were reported, but the injuries underscore the ongoing risk to civilians in the conflict zone.

The incident follows a pattern of nightly attacks that have intensified in recent weeks, as Russia seeks to pressure Kyiv through sustained bombardment. Kyiv’s security forces have reiterated their readiness to counter further strikes, while international observers continue to monitor the situation for potential escalation.
author: Euronews

title: Typhoon Bavi forces evacuations in Taiwan, disrupts power in Okinawa
content:
More than 14,000 residents in Taiwan were forced to evacuate their homes on Saturday as Typhoon Bavi swept across the island with heavy rain and sustained winds exceeding 120 km/h. The storm triggered flash flooding in low‑lying areas and prompted authorities to activate emergency shelters in several counties. Power outages affected thousands of households, while transportation services were suspended to reduce the risk of accidents on wet roads.

At the same time, Typhoon Bavi cut electricity to thousands of customers on Japan’s Okinawa islands as it moved northeast toward eastern China. Meteorological agencies warned that the system could bring strong gusts and additional rainfall to coastal provinces in China later in the week. Emergency officials in all three regions continue to monitor the typhoon’s progress and advise residents to remain prepared for further disruptions.
author: France 24

title: Venezuela Quake Death Toll Tops 4,000
content:
The death toll from Venezuela’s devastating twin earthquakes has risen above 4,000, authorities announced on Friday, marking the deadliest seismic event in the nation in more than a century. The quakes, which struck the western region of the country on March 25 with magnitudes of 7.3 and 6.8, caused widespread collapse of homes, schools and infrastructure, prompting a massive emergency response that has been hampered by aftershocks and difficult terrain.

More than two weeks after the initial shock, families continue to sift through rubble in search of missing loved ones while rescue teams, supported by the military and international aid groups, work around the clock to locate survivors and retrieve bodies. Officials said the scale of destruction has strained local resources, prompting the government to request additional assistance and to establish temporary shelters for displaced residents. The ongoing efforts underscore the magnitude of the disaster and the challenges that remain in the recovery process.
author: France 24

title: Spain defeat Belgium 2-1 to reach World Cup semi-finals
content:
Spain secured a place in the World Cup semi‑finals on Friday after a dramatic 2‑1 win over Belgium, with midfielder Mikel Merino scoring the decisive goal in the closing minutes. The match, played under intense pressure, saw both sides exchange chances before Merino’s late strike broke the deadlock, giving La Roja the advantage they needed to hold on for the victory.

The win sets up a semi‑final clash with France on Tuesday, where Spain will compete for a spot in the tournament final. Both teams will now focus on preparation ahead of the decisive encounter, which promises to determine the next finalist in the competition.
author: France 24

title: Norway reaches World Cup quarter-finals led by Erling Haaland
content:
Norway’s national team has reached the quarter‑finals of the FIFA World Cup for the first time since 1998, setting up a Saturday clash with England for a spot in the semi‑finals. The Vikings’ journey to the last eight has been marked by a series of decisive victories, culminating in a dramatic win that secured their place among the tournament’s elite.

The team’s success is largely attributed to the prolific striker Erling Haaland, who has delivered a series of match‑winning goals and earned the nickname “The Cyborg” for his clinical finishing. Haaland’s performance is supported by a broader cohort of talent often referred to as the “golden generation,” whose development has been underpinned by Norway’s long‑term structural reforms in youth academies, coaching education, and sports science. Together, these elements have created a cohesive unit capable of competing against the world’s best.

As the Vikings prepare to face England, the match will not only determine a semi‑final berth but also serve as a testament to Norway’s footballing resurgence. The outcome will be closely watched by fans and analysts alike, who will assess whether the nation’s investment in youth development and tactical innovation can sustain its newfound competitiveness on the world stage.
author: France 24

title: Argentina and Switzerland to meet in World Cup 2026 quarterfinal
content:
Argentina will face Switzerland in the quarter‑final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, a match that will determine which side advances to the semi‑finals. The game is scheduled for Thursday, July 12, at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, where the two teams will compete for a spot in the final four. Lionel Messi will lead the Argentine squad, while Breel Embolo will captain the Swiss side.

The match follows a tight group stage in which both teams secured their quarter‑final berths with decisive victories. Argentina, ranked third in the world, will rely on Messi’s experience and finishing ability, whereas Switzerland will look to Embolo’s pace and goal‑scoring record to break through. Historically, the two nations have met only once in a World Cup, with Argentina winning 1‑0 in 2018; the upcoming encounter will be the first competitive clash between the squads since then.

A victory for Argentina would set up a semi‑final against either Brazil or France, depending on the bracket, while a Swiss win would propel them into a showdown with the eventual finalists from the other half of the draw. Either outcome will have significant implications for the tournament’s narrative and the legacy of the players involved.
author: Al Jazeera

title: World Cup Quarterfinals Today: England vs Norway, Argentina vs Switzerland
content:
England will take on Norway while Argentina faces Switzerland in the final group‑stage matches, with the winners of each game securing the last two places in the World Cup semifinals. The two fixtures, scheduled for the same day, carry the same weight: a single victory guarantees a spot in the knockout stage, while a loss means elimination.

Both teams have already secured advancement to the knockout phase, but the outcomes will determine the semifinal pairings. England’s victory over Norway would set up a clash with the winner of the other group, while Argentina’s win against Switzerland would similarly place them against the remaining group winner.

The results of these games will finalize the semifinal lineup and set the stage for the tournament’s final rounds, determining which nations will compete for the world title.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Victor Wembanyama signs five-year $252 million rookie extension with Spurs
content:
Victor Wemnanyama, the NBA’s tallest active player at 7 feet 8 inches, signed a rookie extension on Tuesday that ranks as the third‑largest in league history. The five‑year deal, reported to be worth roughly $190 million, will keep the center with the Chicago Skyhawks through the 2029‑30 season and includes a player‑option for the final year. The contract follows a series of record‑breaking extensions for first‑round picks, trailing only Luka Dončić’s $207 million and Zion Williamson’s $205 million agreements.

Wemnanyama, selected 12th overall in the 2023 draft, has become a defensive anchor for the Skyhawks, averaging 12.4 points, 9.8 rebounds and 2.6 blocks per game in his sophomore campaign. His presence in the paint has contributed to Chicago’s top‑ten defensive rating and helped the team secure a playoff berth for the first time in five years. The extension reflects both his on‑court impact and the franchise’s confidence in his continued development as a rim protector and low‑post scorer.

The agreement underscores the growing emphasis on size and defensive versatility in the modern NBA, while providing the Skyhawks with a cornerstone player under a long‑term, cost‑controlled contract. With the extension in place, Chicago can focus on building a complementary roster around Wemnanyama as the team aims to deepen its playoff runs in the coming seasons.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump warns US will strike Iran after death chants at Khamenei funeral
content:
President Joe Biden warned that the United States would take decisive military action against Iran if the latter proceeds with alleged plots to assassinate U.S. personnel and interests in the region. The statement, delivered at a press briefing on Tuesday, cited intelligence reports indicating that Iranian operatives were planning covert attacks against American diplomats and contractors in the Middle East. Biden emphasized that any attempt to harm U.S. citizens would be met with a “decisive and overwhelming” response, underscoring the administration’s commitment to protect its nationals and maintain regional stability.

At the same time, diplomatic efforts led by Oman and Qatar are underway to preserve a memorandum of understanding (MoU) that had been negotiated earlier this year to limit Iran’s nuclear enrichment activities and to establish a framework for prisoner exchanges. Mediators say they are seeking to separate the MoU from the alleged assassination schemes, arguing that continued dialogue is essential to avoid further escalation. The outcome of these talks will determine whether diplomatic channels remain open or whether the president’s warning will translate into direct military action.
author: Al Jazeera

title: China and North Korea mark 65 years of friendship treaty
content:
Beijing and Pyongyang marked the 65th anniversary of the 1959 Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance with a series of diplomatic events scheduled throughout the week. The milestone was highlighted by a joint press conference in Beijing, where Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and North Korean Vice‑Foreign Minister Kim Yong‑nam reaffirmed the parties’ commitment to “deepening political trust and expanding economic collaboration.” Both governments released statements emphasizing the treaty’s role in maintaining regional stability and supporting each nation’s sovereignty.

Celebrations included cultural performances, the unveiling of a commemorative plaque at the site of the original signing, and high‑level delegations visiting each other’s capitals. Analysts note that the anniversary comes amid heightened international scrutiny of North Korea’s nuclear program and China’s expanding influence in Northeast Asia, suggesting the ceremony also serves to reinforce bilateral ties in a complex geopolitical environment. Both sides indicated that the partnership will continue to focus on trade, infrastructure projects, and coordinated diplomatic efforts in multilateral forums.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russian overnight strikes injure ten in Kyiv
content:
Russian forces launched a series of overnight strikes on Kyiv, leaving ten people injured, officials said. The attacks, which began shortly after midnight, involved a combination of missile and drone munitions targeting residential districts on the capital’s western outskirts. Emergency responders arrived within minutes, transporting the wounded to local hospitals where most were reported to have sustained non‑life‑threatening injuries, while two required surgery for shrapnel wounds.

Ukrainian authorities condemned the assault, labeling it a violation of international humanitarian law and urging the international community to hold Moscow accountable. The strikes come amid intensified fighting in the eastern and southern fronts, where both sides have escalated artillery and aerial operations in recent weeks. Ukrainian officials affirmed that security forces are bolstering air defenses around the capital and that investigations into the incident are ongoing.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Spain defeats Belgium to reach World Cup 2026 semifinals
content:
The FIFA World Cup 2026 entered its third matchday on Tuesday, with the United States defeating Mexico 2‑1 in a Group A showdown at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. The hosts opened the scoring in the 23rd minute through a header by forward Christian Pulisic, while Mexico equalised midway through the second half via a penalty taken by Hirving Lozano. A decisive goal came in the 78th minute when midfielder Weston McKennie converted a low cross, securing the United States’ first three points of the tournament. The match featured 18 shots on target and a combined possession rate of 55% for the United States.

Post‑match reactions highlighted the tactical adjustments made by both sides. United States head coach Gregg Berhalter praised his team’s defensive organization and the effectiveness of the wing‑back system, noting that the victory “sets a solid foundation for the group stage.” Mexico’s manager Diego Cocca acknowledged the missed opportunities, emphasizing the need for sharper finishing in the upcoming fixtures. Fan attendance reached 78,000, and television ratings in North America rose 12% compared with the previous matchday, indicating strong regional engagement. The next round of group play will see the United States face Colombia on Thursday, while Mexico meets Saudi Arabia on Friday, both matches scheduled for prime‑time broadcast.

The outcomes of Tuesday’s games have positioned the United States at the top of Group A with three points, while Mexico remains in contention with a single point. With the group stage nearing its midpoint, the forthcoming matches will determine which teams advance to the round of 16, slated to begin on June 30. Viewers can follow live coverage through the official FIFA streaming platform and participating regional broadcasters.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Indonesia anti-graft prosecutor resigns after police seize gold bars and cash
content:
Police officials announced the seizure of 74 kilograms of gold bars along with approximately $20 million in cash denominated in multiple foreign currencies during a coordinated raid conducted earlier this week. The operation, carried out by a joint task force of national law‑enforcement agencies, targeted a warehouse on the outskirts of the capital city where investigators believed illicit proceeds were being stored.

Authorities identified the gold and cash as part of a broader criminal network suspected of money‑laundering and smuggling activities, though no arrests have been disclosed at this stage. The seized assets are being catalogued as evidence, and investigators said the case will remain under active review as they pursue additional leads and potential charges against those involved.
author: Al Jazeera

title: The Hay Wain Painting Arrives in Suffolk for First Time
content:
A landmark painting that has long been celebrated for its portrayal of a Suffolk landscape is on view in the county for the first time. The work, created by the 19th‑century artist William Hartley, depicts the tranquil river scene at Bury St. Edmunds that has become an icon of the region’s pastoral heritage. After decades of being housed in London’s National Gallery, the canvas was loaned to the Suffolk County Museum on 15 June, marking the artwork’s inaugural exhibition in the very countryside it depicts.

The museum’s opening event attracted a crowd of art enthusiasts and local residents, all eager to see the piece in its natural context. Curators explained that the loan arrangement was part of a broader initiative to bring national treasures to regional audiences, and that the painting’s technical details—its use of light and brushwork—offer a unique insight into Hartley’s approach to landscape. The museum will keep the painting on display through 30 September, with accompanying educational programmes aimed at students and visitors.

The arrival of Hartley’s Suffolk scene is seen as a significant cultural moment for the county, providing residents with a tangible link to their artistic heritage. By placing the painting within its original setting, the Suffolk County Museum hopes to deepen public appreciation of both the artist’s legacy and the enduring beauty of the region’s countryside.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Snow Patrol marks 20 years of Chasing Cars and discusses new Kylie Minogue collaboration
content:
The veteran pop‑rock group [Band Name] reflected on the enduring legacy of their 2004 chart‑topping single “Midnight Echo” during a recent press conference, noting how the track’s blend of synth‑driven hooks and lyrical nostalgia continues to attract streaming listeners worldwide. While celebrating the milestone, the band announced the release of a new collaboration with Australian pop icon Kylie Minogue, titled “Neon Skyline,” slated for digital platforms later this week.

In answering questions about the nature of the partnership, the band clarified that “Neon Skyline” is not a duet in the traditional sense; Minogue’s contribution is limited to a spoken‑word bridge and background vocal textures rather than a shared lead vocal performance. According to the group’s spokesperson, the decision was driven by the song’s production concept, which required Minogue’s distinctive tonal color to complement the band’s lead singer without dividing the narrative focus. Both parties expressed enthusiasm for the track’s experimental direction and hinted that the collaboration may open avenues for further joint projects.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Kane downplays comparisons with Haaland, says England ready to peak
content:
Harry Kane dismissed media comparisons between his goal‑scoring record and that of Norway’s Erling Haaland on Friday, emphasizing that England’s focus is on collective performance rather than individual statistics. Speaking after England’s group‑stage match, the striker said the team is “ready to peak” as the tournament moves into its knockout phase, highlighting the importance of timing and teamwork over personal accolades.

Kane’s comments came as England prepares for its next World Cup fixtures, with the squad aiming to build on its early results and maintain consistency through the later stages. The forward reiterated that the national side’s preparation, tactical flexibility, and squad depth position them to compete effectively as the competition intensifies, underscoring the team’s ambition to advance as far as possible.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: NBPA urges NBA to fix second apron policy hurting players
content:
NBA Players Association executive director David Kelly warned that the league’s newly introduced “second apron” is compelling teams to make roster moves that are driven by financial considerations rather than purely basketball merit. In remarks to the media, Kelly said the mechanism forces clubs to prioritize “cost control” over on‑court performance, creating a situation where player contracts and playing time are dictated by the secondary salary‑cap threshold rather than talent evaluation.

The second apron, a supplemental cap limit that sits above the standard salary cap, is intended to curb excessive spending but, according to Kelly, it is “hurting players” by restricting their earning potential and limiting roster flexibility. The NBPA has indicated that the policy could lead to more non‑basketball‑related transactions, such as trades and waivers, as teams seek to remain under the new financial ceiling. The association is expected to continue discussions with the league to address the concerns raised about the impact on player livelihoods and competitive balance.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Iguodala says LeBron's Warriors interest highlights Curry's impact
content:
Andre Iguodala, who earned the 2015 NBA Finals MVP as the Golden Warriors secured their first championship in a three‑title run, commented on the recent speculation surrounding LeBron James’ free‑agency options. Iguodala said that the very fact James is being mentioned as a possible destination for the Warriors underscores the impact of Stephen Curry on the franchise’s appeal.

The former Warriors forward highlighted Curry’s role in transforming Golden State into a perennial contender, noting that James’ interest, even if only rumored, reflects the team’s elevated status in the league. Iguodala’s remarks come as James evaluates his next move after opting out of his current contract, while the Warriors continue to build around Curry and a core that includes several recent additions.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Caleb Wilson scores 35 in Summer League debut, second‑most Las Vegas debut since 2004
content:
