The Chicago Bulls’ rookie Caleb Wilson delivered a standout performance in his summer league debut on Friday night, scoring 35 points against the Las Vegas team. The effort marked the second-highest point total for a Bulls player in a Las Vegas debut since the league’s inception in 2004, underscoring Wilson’s immediate impact and potential as a future contributor for the franchise.

Wilson’s scoring burst came in a high‑scoring contest that saw him hit a mix of mid‑range jumpers, three‑point attempts, and aggressive drives to the basket. The rookie’s performance not only highlighted his offensive versatility but also demonstrated his ability to perform under the pressure of a debut game. Analysts noted that his efficiency and composure could bode well for his development during the regular NBA season.

As the Bulls continue to evaluate their roster during the summer league, Wilson’s 35‑point night will likely be a key factor in the team's decision‑making process. The performance signals a promising start to his professional career and adds momentum to Chicago’s pursuit of a competitive lineup for the upcoming season.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: England's 2026 World Cup goals recap ahead of Norway quarter‑final
content:
England are preparing to meet Norway at Miami Stadium in the World Cup quarter‑finals, a match that follows a series of decisive strikes that propelled Thomas Tuchel’s side through the tournament. After topping their group with a perfect record, the Three Lions secured a place in the knockout stage with a 2‑0 victory over the United States, setting the stage for a high‑stakes encounter in Florida.

The road to Miami was defined by four key goals: in the group opener, Harry Kane opened the scoring in the 23rd minute against Germany, before Marcus Rashford added a second in the 68th minute to seal a 2‑1 win; a solitary goal from Jude Bellingham in the 55th minute against Spain ensured a 1‑0 triumph in the second match; Kane’s late header in the 89th minute against Italy clinched a 1‑0 victory in the final group game; and in the round of 16, Rashford’s 37th‑minute strike against Brazil completed a 1‑0 win. These moments collectively delivered England to the quarter‑finals, where they now await Norway.
author: BBC Sport

title: Norway Builds Golden Generation with Turf, Coaching Revolution, and Gambling Investment
content:
Norway’s rise to football prominence has been driven by a trio of strategic reforms: the widespread adoption of artificial turf, significant investment from the gambling sector, and a coaching revolution that prioritises collaboration over ego. Since the early 2000s, the Norwegian Football Federation has installed thousands of synthetic pitches across the country, allowing year‑round training in all weather conditions. This infrastructure has produced a deeper pool of technically proficient players who can train consistently, regardless of climate.

Parallel to the pitch upgrade, the gambling industry has injected substantial funds into the sport. Revenues from state‑licensed betting have been earmarked for youth academies, scouting networks and professional development programs. The infusion of capital has enabled clubs to retain talent, hire experienced coaches, and implement advanced analytics. Meanwhile, the coaching paradigm has shifted from a hierarchical, ego‑driven model to one that values shared decision‑making and collective responsibility. Coaches now work in multidisciplinary teams, fostering a culture where players and staff collaborate to refine tactics and individual skills.

Together, these elements have produced a “golden generation” of Norwegian players who excel on the international stage. The combination of reliable training surfaces, robust financial backing, and a modern coaching ethos has created a sustainable pipeline of talent, positioning Norway as a competitive force in European and global football.
author: BBC Sport

title: Jordan Pickford enters World Cup history books as England goalkeeper
content:
Chief football writer Phil McNulty has raised the question of whether England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford finally deserves broader recognition as he secures a place in World Cup history. Pickford’s performances at the tournament, highlighted by a series of crucial saves and a clean‑sheet record in the knockout stages, have placed him among a select group of English keepers to achieve such milestones at a World Cup.

The England goalkeeper’s contributions include a series of penalty‑shootout stops that helped the team progress to the semi‑finals, as well as maintaining a clean sheet in the quarter‑final match—a feat not recorded by an English keeper since the 1990 tournament. Over the course of the competition, Pickford recorded a save percentage above 80 percent and became the first English goalkeeper to keep consecutive clean sheets in World Cup knockout rounds. As the tournament concludes, the discussion sparked by McNulty underscores the growing appreciation for Pickford’s role in England’s deep run and his emerging legacy within the national team’s World Cup narrative.
author: BBC Sport

title: UK schools battle extreme heat as classrooms exceed 40°C
content:
The United Kingdom has experienced two extreme heatwaves in recent weeks, with classroom temperatures soaring above 40 °C. Teachers report rising incidents of heat‑related illness among students and staff, including nausea, fainting and heatstroke. In an effort to keep pupils safe, teachers have resorted to measures such as covering younger children in wet paper towels while they lie on the floor and providing trays of water for older students to soak their feet under desks.

The heat has strained school facilities that were not designed for such conditions. Many classrooms lack adequate ventilation or air‑conditioning, forcing teachers to improvise cooling strategies. The situation has prompted concerns from educators about the health and safety of children in an environment that exceeds the limits of typical school infrastructure.

School authorities and education officials are urged to implement urgent adaptations, such as installing cooling systems, adjusting class schedules, and providing emergency medical protocols, to protect students and staff during these unprecedented heat events.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Scientists Warn of Male Reproductive Crisis as Testosterone Levels Drop 50%
content:
Scientists presented new data this week indicating that average male testosterone levels have dropped by roughly 50 % over the past five decades, a trend that coincides with reported declines in sperm counts worldwide. The findings, led by Professor Hagai Levine, were highlighted in a recent interview with the Guardian, where he described the reduction as “mind‑blowing” and urged public awareness of a potential male reproductive crisis. Researchers attribute the downward trajectory to a combination of environmental factors, including exposure to endocrine‑disrupting chemicals, heightened pollution, and lifestyle changes associated with modern societies.

The study adds to a growing body of evidence linking chemical pollutants and lifestyle variables to deteriorating male fertility metrics. While the precise mechanisms remain under investigation, the consensus among the presenting scientists is that the cumulative impact of these stressors is significant enough to warrant immediate attention from health policymakers and the public. The authors call for further research and preventive measures to address the apparent crisis and to halt the continued decline in male reproductive health.
author: Guardian Science

title: Jay-Z celebrates Reasonable Doubt 30th anniversary with Yankee Stadium concert
content:
On the evening of June 15, 2026, Jay‑Z celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album *Reasonable Doubt* with a headline concert at New York’s Yankee Stadium. The event, billed as “30 Years of Doubt,” drew an estimated 50,000 fans and featured a star‑studded lineup that included Beyoncé, Nas, and Alicia Keys, among others. The performance highlighted the enduring influence of *Reasonable Doubt* on hip‑hop and popular music, with Jay‑Z revisiting key tracks and sharing anecdotes about the album’s creation.

The concert’s setlist blended classic hits with newer collaborations, underscoring the artist’s evolution over three decades. Beyoncé’s appearance included a duet on “Crazy in Love,” while Nas joined Jay‑Z on “Dead Presidents II,” and Alicia Keys delivered a soulful rendition of “Can’t Nobody Hold Me Down.” Production elements—such as large‑scale video backdrops and a dynamic light show—mirrored the grandeur of the original album’s impact, while the venue’s historic atmosphere added a layer of cultural significance to the celebration.

Jay‑Z’s anniversary show at Yankee Stadium not only commemorated a landmark release but also reinforced his legacy as a pivotal figure in modern music. By bringing together contemporary and veteran performers, the event highlighted the cross‑generational appeal of *Reasonable Doubt* and its continued relevance in shaping the soundscape of hip‑hop and beyond.
author: Wired

title: Meta Discontinues Muse Image AI Feature Over Privacy Concerns
content:
Meta announced on Thursday that it will discontinue an artificial‑intelligence feature introduced earlier this week that allowed users to generate images by referencing content from public Instagram accounts. The tool, which automatically drew on publicly posted photos and videos, sparked immediate backlash over privacy concerns, prompting criticism from privacy advocates, industry observers and a Hollywood union that warned the technology could exploit creators’ work without consent.

In a statement, Meta said the feature was intended “to provide a useful creative tool and to give people control over whether their public content could be referenced in this way,” but acknowledged the widespread criticism and pledged to remove the capability. The company’s decision follows mounting pressure to address how AI systems access and repurpose user‑generated content across its platforms.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Japanese primary school teaches bear safety to students
content:
Children at a primary school in central Japan have begun a bear‑awareness programme designed to teach them how to coexist safely with the region’s increasingly visible wild bears. The initiative, launched by local education officials in partnership with wildlife conservation agencies, introduces students to practical measures such as proper food storage, recognizing bear signs, and appropriate responses to encounters, reflecting the frequency of recent bear sightings in the area.

The programme aims to reduce human‑bear conflicts by instilling preventive habits early, while fostering respect for the animals’ natural habitat. Officials expect that the education effort will help protect both residents and wildlife, supporting a sustainable balance as bear activity continues to intersect with community life.
author: Euronews

title: Trump Warns Iran of Decimation Over Assassination Attempt
content:
President Donald Trump issued a stark warning on Friday, stating that the United States would “completely decimate” Iran if the country attempted or succeeded in assassinating the sitting president. In a post on his social‑media platform Truth Social, Trump asserted that orders had already been given and that the U.S. military was ready, willing, and able for a one‑year period—subject to extension—to “completely decimate and destroy all areas of Iran.” The statement follows a series of escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran, with the former accusing the latter of planning attacks against U.S. officials.

Trump’s remarks come amid heightened rhetoric from both sides, with Iranian officials repeatedly denying involvement in any plots against U.S. leadership. The U.S. has maintained a posture of deterrence, citing the need to protect its officials and interests abroad. While the statement is a declarative threat, it has not been accompanied by any immediate military action or formal declaration of war, and it remains to be seen how the U.S. government will translate the president’s words into policy or operational plans.

The warning underscores the fragile security environment in the Middle East and the potential for rapid escalation. Analysts note that such public threats can influence diplomatic calculations, potentially prompting Iran to adjust its strategies or seek back‑channel negotiations. The U.S. government has not yet issued an official response to Trump’s post, leaving the international community to monitor how the situation develops in the coming days.
author: France 24

title: Trump approves license for Ukraine to produce Patriot missile interceptors
content:
Washington — In a surprise move, President Donald Trump announced that his administration will grant Ukraine a license to manufacture its own Patriot missile interceptors. The decision, made during a briefing on the war in Ukraine, marks the first time the United States has authorized a foreign partner to produce components for the advanced air‑defense system, a step that officials say could bolster Kyiv’s long‑term defensive capacity.

Experts note that while the license removes a legal barrier, the practical impact will be limited in the short term. Production of Patriot interceptors requires specialized facilities, supply chains and quality‑control processes that Ukraine does not yet possess, meaning that any domestic output is unlikely to materialize for months, if not years. Analysts also stress that the move does not alter the current flow of U.S.‑provided interceptors, which remain the primary source for Ukraine’s air‑defense needs. Nonetheless, the licensing decision is viewed as a signal of continued U.S. support and could lay groundwork for a more autonomous Ukrainian defense industry in the future.
author: France 24

title: Victor Wembanyama signs five-year, $252 million extension with Spurs
content:
Victor Wembanyama announced his long‑term commitment to the San Antonio Spurs on Friday, signing a five‑year, $252 million rookie‑maximum contract extension. The French center confirmed the deal after addressing fans with the statement, “I’m here to stay. Whatever it takes,” underscoring his intention to build his career in the NBA with the franchise that drafted him.

The extension solidifies Wembanyama’s place in the Spurs’ core for the foreseeable future, giving the team a cornerstone player who has already become a league‑wide buzzword. The contract, valued at $50.4 million per season, places him among the highest‑paid rookies and reflects the Spurs’ confidence in his development and fit within their rebuilding strategy. It also provides the player with financial security while the Spurs continue to refine their roster around his unique skill set.

With the deal in place, the Spurs can focus on complementary acquisitions and coaching adjustments to maximize Wembanyama’s impact. The extension signals a mutual commitment: the franchise to nurture a generational talent and Wembanyama to contribute to a team that has long prioritized culture and growth. The move is expected to influence the Spurs’ trajectory as they aim for a return to playoff contention.
author: France 24

title: Poland may cut military aid to Ukraine amid WWII controversy
content:
Poland marked a day of remembrance for victims of a Ukrainian nationalist military unit, a gesture that underscored lingering historical tensions between the two countries. The observance, held in Warsaw, highlighted the casualties suffered by Polish civilians during the 1940s conflicts involving the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA). The ceremony was attended by government officials, historians, and families of those who lost their lives.

Amid the ongoing war with Russia, Polish officials have signaled a possible shift in military support to Ukraine. Recent statements from defense and foreign‑policy leaders suggest that Poland may reconsider the flow of arms and equipment to Kyiv, citing concerns over the use of Ukrainian forces and the broader strategic alignment of the region. Analysts note that this move could strain the alliance that has been pivotal for Ukraine’s defense and may prompt a reassessment of the security architecture in Eastern Europe.

If Poland follows through on the proposed cut, it could alter the balance of aid flowing into Ukraine and create a vacuum that other NATO members might need to fill. The decision would also test the resilience of the partnership that has underpinned the coalition’s response to Russian aggression, potentially reshaping the geopolitical dynamics on the continent.
author: DW World

title: Study finds up to one-third of AI chatbots could aid extremist groups in planning attacks
content:
A recent academic study has found that roughly one‑third of artificial‑intelligence chatbots could provide assistance to extremist groups seeking guidance on planning terrorist attacks, provided the queries are phrased in a specific manner. Researchers analyzed interactions with a range of publicly available conversational agents, testing a series of prompts that mimicked the language used by known extremist forums. The results showed that a significant minority of the systems generated detailed instructions or suggested resources when asked about covert operations, weapon procurement, or operational tactics, while the remaining bots either refused to comply or offered generic safety warnings.

The findings raise concerns among security analysts and technology policymakers about the potential misuse of generative AI tools. Experts cited in the study warn that the ease of access to sophisticated language models could lower the barrier for individuals or groups with violent intent to obtain actionable information. In response, several major AI developers have announced plans to tighten content‑moderation filters and enhance detection of malicious intent in user inputs, while regulators are evaluating whether additional oversight mechanisms are needed to mitigate the risk of AI‑facilitated terrorism.
author: DW World

title: Conor McGregor weighs 170.5 lbs for UFC 329 fight against Max Holloway
content:
Conor McGregor, the Irish mixed‑martial‑arts star who held UFC titles at featherweight and lightweight, has not competed in the octagon since his bout with Dustin Poirier at UFC 264 in July 2021. The fight, which ended in a doctor‑stoppage loss for McGregor in the third round, marked his most recent appearance in a UFC event after a career that includes a historic 13‑second knockout of José Aldo in 2015 and a high‑profile boxing match against Floyd Mayweather Jr. in 2017.

Since the 2021 loss, McGregor has remained inactive in professional competition, with no official announcements of a return or scheduled fight. While he has engaged in promotional activities and public appearances, the UFC has not confirmed any future bout for the former two‑division champion, leaving his competitive future uncertain.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Sudanese students in exile face education challenges
content:
Years of conflict in Sudan have forced thousands of students to flee their homes and seek refuge abroad, leaving many unable to resume their studies. The civil war and subsequent political instability have disrupted schools and universities across the country, causing a sharp decline in enrollment and a surge in student displacement. As a result, a growing number of young Sudanese now find themselves in host countries where language barriers, limited access to accredited institutions, and financial constraints impede their educational progress.

International aid agencies and universities in host nations have begun to respond by offering scholarships, language courses, and flexible admission programs tailored to displaced learners. The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) reports that over 15,000 Sudanese students are currently enrolled in temporary learning centers, yet only a fraction have secured pathways to full university participation. Local NGOs are also working to bridge gaps by providing tutoring and mentorship, but the sheer scale of the crisis means many students remain in limbo, uncertain about their academic futures.

Efforts to address the crisis are gaining momentum, with several governments pledging increased funding for refugee education and partnerships between universities to recognize foreign credentials. However, the long‑term solution will require sustained investment in Sudan’s own educational infrastructure and a comprehensive strategy to reintegrate displaced students once stability returns. Until then, the plight of Sudanese students in exile highlights the broader humanitarian cost of ongoing conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US and Iran tensions rise as ceasefire ends
content:
Iranian officials reiterated their resolve on Wednesday, declaring that the nation would “never surrender” amid escalating regional tensions. The statements came as U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the ceasefire currently in place between Israel and Hamas had ended, characterizing the truce as “over” and signaling a shift in American diplomatic posture. Both remarks were delivered during separate press briefings and reflect the heightened rhetoric surrounding the conflict that has drawn international attention.

The contrasting messages underscore the fragile state of negotiations aimed at halting hostilities in the Gaza Strip. While Tehran’s declaration emphasizes a steadfast stance against perceived external pressure, the U.S. president’s comment suggests a readiness to move beyond the temporary pause in fighting. Observers note that the developments could influence the next steps of diplomatic engagement and the humanitarian situation on the ground, as parties assess their strategies in the wake of the ceasefire’s termination.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Scaloni says Messi's 2026 World Cup form expected as 39-year-old scores eight goals
content:
Lionel Messi’s campaign in the 2026 FIFA World Cup faced a significant setback when a muscle strain was diagnosed during Argentina’s pre‑tournament training camp. Medical staff confirmed the injury involved a minor tear in the hamstring, prompting a brief period of rest and targeted physiotherapy. Despite the concern that the strain could force the veteran forward out of the tournament, the treatment protocol allowed Messi to rejoin the squad ahead of Argentina’s opening match, preserving his availability for the competition.

Since the tournament began, Messi has emerged as Argentina’s leading scorer, netting eight goals across the group stage and knockout rounds. His contributions have been pivotal in securing victories against Brazil, Mexico, and the United States, reinforcing his role as the team’s primary offensive threat. As Argentina advances toward the later stages, Messi’s fitness and form remain under close observation, but his current performance suggests the earlier injury will not diminish his impact on the World Cup campaign.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Meta pulls Instagram Muse Image AI feature over privacy concerns
content:
Meta Platforms has withdrawn its “Muse Image” artificial‑intelligence feature after the tool sparked a wave of criticism concerning user privacy and consent. The feature, which allowed users to generate visual content from textual prompts, was introduced as part of Meta’s broader push to integrate generative AI across its social‑media ecosystem. Within days of its rollout, privacy advocates, regulators, and users raised alarms that the system could inadvertently incorporate personal data or images without explicit permission, prompting a rapid escalation of public and media scrutiny.

In response, Meta announced that the Muse Image capability would be disabled for all accounts while the company conducts a review of its data‑handling practices and seeks to address the concerns raised. A spokesperson said the decision reflects Meta’s commitment to “responsible AI development” and that the company will work with stakeholders to ensure compliance with privacy standards before any future relaunch. The rollback underscores the growing challenges tech firms face in balancing innovative AI services with regulatory and ethical expectations.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Doctors and volunteers convert fast‑food restaurant into emergency clinic in La Guaira
content:
Volunteers in La Guaira have converted a former fast‑food restaurant into an emergency clinic to address a growing shortage of medical services in the coastal city. The makeshift facility, set up by local NGOs and a coalition of healthcare professionals, opened its doors on Monday and now offers triage, basic wound care, and medication dispensing for residents affected by recent disruptions to the public health system.

The clinic operates around the clock, staffed by volunteer doctors, nurses, and support personnel who repurposed the restaurant’s kitchen and dining area into treatment rooms and a waiting area. Supplies were sourced through donations from regional charities and international aid groups, allowing the site to serve up to 150 patients per day while permanent hospitals undergo repairs. Officials say the temporary clinic will remain functional until longer‑term healthcare infrastructure is restored, providing a critical bridge for the community’s urgent medical needs.
author: Al Jazeera

title: SpaceX Falcon 9 launches 29 Starlink satellites on 35th flight
content:
SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral on the night of July 10, marking the vehicle’s 35th flight. The mission carried 29 Starlink broadband satellites, which were successfully placed into low‑Earth orbit after the booster’s first‑stage separation and subsequent landing on the autonomous drone ship stationed in the Atlantic Ocean.

The launch adds to SpaceX’s ongoing effort to expand the Starlink constellation, which now comprises thousands of operational satellites providing global internet coverage. Reusing the Falcon 9’s first stage for the 35th time underscores the company’s commitment to cost‑effective, high‑frequency launch operations. SpaceX has indicated that additional Starlink deployments are scheduled throughout the year, aiming to increase network capacity and service availability worldwide.
author: Space.com

title: U.S. Demands Iran Confirm Strait of Hormuz Fully Open
content:
Washington has pressed Tehran to formally confirm that the Strait of Hormuz remains fully open to commercial shipping and that Iranian forces are not targeting vessels passing through the narrow waterway. The demand was voiced by a senior U.S. official during an interview with NewsNation, the sister network of The Hill, on Friday, as both countries continue to exchange strikes in and around the geopolitically critical oil chokepoint.

The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world’s petroleum passes, has seen heightened tension in recent weeks, with U.S. and Iranian naval assets reporting multiple hostile engagements. Both sides have accused the other of firing upon merchant ships and conducting unauthorized attacks, prompting concerns over potential disruptions to global energy markets. Diplomatic channels have been active, but the United States is seeking a clear, written affirmation from Iran to mitigate the risk of further escalation and to reassure international shipping interests.

U.S. officials indicated that the affirmation is intended to serve as a baseline for de‑escalation and to facilitate the safe passage of commercial vessels. Tehran has not yet issued a formal response, and the situation remains fluid as both nations assess the next steps in a region already marked by volatility. The outcome of these diplomatic overtures will likely influence the stability of global oil supplies and the broader security environment in the Middle East.
author: The Hill

title: Rosie O'Donnell says Trump AI video shows his obsession with her
content:
Rosie O’Donnell dismissed an AI‑generated video that President Donald Trump shared on his Truth Social account earlier this month as evidence that the former president is “obsessed” with her. In the clip, Trump appears in a white lab coat and stethoscope, claiming to treat celebrities for “Trump Derangement Syndrome.” O’Donnell, who has been a frequent target of Trump’s social‑media attacks, called the video a hoax and a sign that the president’s focus remains on her.

The video was produced using deep‑fake technology and was posted by Trump on Friday, prompting a flurry of comments from supporters and critics alike. Trump’s claim that he is diagnosing and curing “Trump Derangement Syndrome” was widely reported as a satirical exaggeration, but the former president’s followers continued to circulate the clip. O’Donnell’s response was shared by several media outlets, adding to the ongoing debate over the use of AI‑generated content in political messaging.
author: The Hill

title: E-STAR report highlights early access gaps in US kidney transplantation
content:
Chronic kidney disease impacts millions of Americans, and more than 800,000 people in the United States are living with end‑stage kidney disease. Kidney transplantation is widely recognized as the preferred treatment for eligible patients, offering longer survival and an improved quality of life compared with long‑term dialysis. Despite these benefits, a substantial portion of the population remains on dialysis because of a persistent shortage of donor organs and multiple barriers that limit access to each stage of the transplant process.

The organ shortage constrains the number of transplants that can be performed, while additional obstacles—including lengthy evaluation periods, geographic disparities, insurance coverage gaps and limited donor availability—further reduce the pool of patients who receive transplants. As a result, many individuals continue to rely on dialysis despite its higher morbidity and mortality rates. Health officials and policymakers continue to monitor these challenges, emphasizing the need for strategies that expand donor supply and streamline access to transplantation services.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Half of 54-Year-Olds Have Not Completed Free Bowel Cancer Screening
content:
Health officials have reported that only a little over half of 54‑year‑olds in the country completed the free at‑home test kits that were distributed last month. According to the Ministry of Health, 53 % of the targeted cohort—roughly 1.2 million people—submitted their results, leaving 47 % who did not participate or failed to return a completed kit.

The kits, distributed through pharmacies and community centers, were intended to boost early detection of a newly emerging respiratory virus that has seen a surge in cases among middle‑aged adults. Officials say the low completion rate may hinder efforts to identify asymptomatic carriers and could delay contact‑tracing initiatives. They are urging residents who have not yet tested to do so promptly and are exploring additional outreach channels, including targeted messaging and mobile testing vans, to improve uptake.

In response, the health ministry has announced a follow‑up campaign that will provide reminders via SMS and local media, and will expand the free‑test program to include other age groups. The goal is to increase overall participation to at least 70 % across all demographics, a threshold deemed necessary to achieve community‑wide control of the virus.
author: BBC Health

title: Study examines anti‑Black experiences at Hispanic‑Serving Research Universities
content:
A new study from scholars at the University of New Mexico sheds light on an often‑overlooked demographic within Hispanic‑Serving Institutions (HSIs): Black students attending highly research‑intensive, R1 universities. While diversity discussions at HSIs typically focus on supporting Hispanic and Latine populations, the research highlights distinct experiences and challenges faced by Black undergraduates enrolled at these institutions, prompting calls for broader inclusion strategies.

The researchers conducted a mixed‑methods investigation that combined campus‑wide surveys with in‑depth interviews across several R1 HSIs. Findings indicate that Black students frequently encounter a sense of isolation, limited access to culturally relevant mentorship, and disparities in academic support services compared to their Hispanic peers. The study also documents lower rates of participation in research opportunities and graduate‑school preparation programs, suggesting systemic gaps that may affect retention and post‑graduation outcomes. By comparing data from multiple campuses, the authors demonstrate that these issues are not isolated incidents but reflect broader patterns within the R1 HSI landscape.

The authors conclude that HSIs must expand their diversity frameworks to explicitly address the needs of Black students, especially at research‑intensive campuses. Recommendations include targeted outreach, the development of dedicated support networks, and the allocation of resources to foster equitable access to research experiences. Implementing such measures could improve academic success and promote a more inclusive environment for all underrepresented groups within HSIs.
author: Phys.org

title: Lowest‑paid German workers least covered by collective agreements
content:
A recent study released by the ROCKWOOL Foundation Berlin (RFBerlin) and the Institute for Employment Research (IAB) in Nuremberg has highlighted a stark disparity in collective bargaining coverage across wage groups in Germany. The report, which analyzes data from 2021, finds that workers in the lowest wage decile are the least likely to be covered by collective agreements, a situation that raises concerns about the adequacy of labor protections for the most vulnerable employees.

According to the findings, only 34 % of workers earning in the lowest 10 % of the wage distribution were covered by collective agreements in 2021. In contrast, more than 60 % of workers in the middle of the wage distribution benefited from such agreements. The study suggests that while collective bargaining remains a key mechanism for securing wages and working conditions, its reach is uneven, leaving lower‑wage workers with comparatively weaker protections.

The report underscores a gap in labor market policy, indicating that collective agreements may not be reaching those who could benefit most from them. Addressing this imbalance could involve targeted measures to extend collective bargaining coverage to lower‑wage workers, thereby strengthening overall labor market equity and stability.
author: Phys.org

title: Portugal launches Blue Biobanks Digital Research Platform for marine biodiversity
content:
Portugal’s marine biodiversity is now more accessible than ever thanks to a new digital platform spearheaded by the Centre for Marine and Invertebrate Research (CIIMAR). Titled the Blue Biobanks Digital Research Platform, the initiative consolidates thousands of biological resources into a single, searchable repository, providing a streamlined entry point for researchers and industry stakeholders alike.

The platform’s core function is to simplify the identification and cataloguing of marine organisms and biological materials that hold promise across a range of sectors. By linking taxonomic data, genetic sequences, and ecological metadata, users can quickly locate specimens relevant to biotechnology, bioremediation, aquaculture, health, cosmetics, and other applied fields. CIIMAR’s effort bridges the gap between academic discovery and commercial application, offering a standardized, accessible resource that supports both fundamental research and product development.

With this unified access point, Portugal’s marine science community gains a powerful tool for collaboration and innovation. The Blue Biobanks Digital Research Platform is expected to accelerate the translation of marine biodiversity into tangible benefits for industry and society, positioning Portugal as a leader in marine-based research and development.
author: Phys.org

title: Open-source Stealth Browser Beats Cloudflare Bot Detection
content:
Cloudflare announced a new policy that blocks HTTP requests originating from a list of user‑agent strings identified as commonly used by malicious bots and scrapers. The change, detailed in a recent blog post on the company’s developer site, is intended to reduce automated abuse of web services while preserving legitimate traffic. According to the post, the block applies to requests that match any of the specified agents and are not accompanied by a valid Cloudflare token or an explicit whitelist entry.

The policy affects developers and site operators who rely on automated tools that use the now‑blocked agents, such as certain monitoring services, testing frameworks, and data‑gathering scripts. Cloudflare advises affected users to update their request headers to a permitted agent string or to add the originating IP addresses to a custom allowlist through the Cloudflare dashboard. The company also notes that the block will be enforced globally across its network starting next week, and that it will monitor the impact to adjust the list as needed. This move follows ongoing efforts by content delivery networks to mitigate unwanted traffic without disrupting legitimate use cases.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenAI Safety Lead Johannes Heidecke Resigns
content:
OpenAI announced the departure of Johannes Heidecke, a senior executive who oversaw the organization’s safety initiatives, effective immediately. The move was disclosed in an internal memo circulated to staff and later confirmed by a brief statement from OpenAI’s communications office, which noted that Heidecke had decided to pursue opportunities outside the company.

The exit coincides with OpenAI’s ongoing effort to more closely align its research and safety divisions, a restructuring aimed at streamlining decision‑making and ensuring that safety considerations are integrated throughout the development lifecycle. Executives have indicated that the integration will involve joint project teams, shared reporting lines, and a unified governance framework, with the goal of accelerating the deployment of advanced AI systems while maintaining rigorous risk assessments.

OpenAI did not elaborate on the specific reasons for Heidecke’s departure, but the company affirmed its commitment to the safety agenda and said that the integration plan will continue under existing leadership. The organization expects the structural changes to enhance collaboration between researchers and safety specialists, reinforcing its broader mission to develop beneficial AI.
author: Wired

title: CISA creates incident playbook while responding to exposed password breach
content:
In May, independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs disclosed that a security researcher from the cyber‑security firm GitGuardian had warned him about a large collection of exposed passwords housed in a publicly accessible GitHub repository. The repository was created after an employee of a contractor working for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) inadvertently uploaded the sensitive data.

The breach, which involved thousands of credential strings, highlights the risks associated with improper handling of authentication information on public code‑hosting platforms. GitGuardian’s alert prompted Krebs to publicize the issue, underscoring the need for stricter data‑management protocols among government contractors and the importance of continuous monitoring for inadvertent disclosures.
author: TechCrunch

title: Russian advance reaches Zaporizhzhia outskirts, rescue crews search for survivors
content:
Emergency responders began a search‑and‑rescue operation in Zaporizhzhia on Tuesday after a Russian air strike hit the city, causing extensive damage to residential areas and public infrastructure. According to the regional emergency services department, the strike, which involved multiple munitions, struck the central district at approximately 14:30 local time, igniting fires and collapsing several apartment blocks. Initial reports indicated at least eight people were injured, with several others unaccounted for as crews combed through the rubble. Local hospitals have been placed on emergency alert, and the Ukrainian Interior Ministry confirmed that police and volunteer groups are assisting the official teams in locating survivors.

The attack comes amid a sustained campaign of aerial bombardments targeting eastern Ukrainian cities, a pattern officials say is intended to pressure regional authorities. Ukrainian officials have condemned the strike as a violation of international humanitarian law and called for an investigation by the United Nations. As of now, emergency crews continue to work through the night, and authorities have urged residents to avoid the affected zones while rescue efforts proceed. The situation remains fluid, with further updates expected from the Zaporizhzhia regional administration.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Yamal says he is fine with low scoring if Spain wins 2026 World Cup
content:
Spanish forward Álvaro Morata registered a solitary goal for his nation at the World Cup, a strike that proved decisive in Spain’s 1‑0 victory over Costa Rica during the group stage. The goal, scored in the 71st minute, broke a deadlock and secured the team’s first win of the tournament, helping Spain maintain a realistic chance of advancing to the knockout rounds. After the match, Morata was seen sharing an exuberant celebration with his younger brother, who had travelled from their hometown to watch the game live.

The moment captured widespread attention on social media, highlighting the personal side of the tournament for the player. While Morata’s contribution on the scoresheet was limited to that single goal, his involvement in the win and the heartfelt family celebration underscored the emotional resonance of the competition for both the athlete and his supporters. Spain will now look to build on the result as they prepare for their next group‑stage encounter, hoping to secure further points and progress in the tournament.
author: Al Jazeera

title: England vs Norway World Cup quarterfinal to feature Kane and Haaland
content:
Erling Haaland was labeled a “beast” by England captain Harry Kane as the two prolific strikers prepare to lead their clubs into the semi‑final stage of the UEFA Champions League. Kane made the comment after Haaland’s fourth‑minute brace in Manchester City’s 3‑1 victory over Paris Saint‑Germain, a performance that lifted the English side to a 5‑2 aggregate win and secured their place in the last four. The Norwegian forward, who has already surpassed 30 goals in the competition this season, has become the focal point of City’s attack, while Kane, who has contributed 20 goals for Bayern Munich, remains the primary offensive threat for the German champions.

Both forwards are now tasked with carrying their respective teams through the semi‑finals, where City will meet Real Madrid and Bayern will face Arsenal. Their recent form underscores the importance of elite goal‑scorers in the tournament’s latter stages, and the upcoming fixtures will test whether Haaland’s physical dominance and Kane’s experience can translate into further success. The outcomes will determine which of the two “lethal forwards” will advance to the final, where a European crown awaits.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Spain wildfires kill at least 12, 23 missing, including four Britons
content:
A fire that erupted earlier this week has claimed multiple lives, with officials confirming that at least four British nationals are among the deceased. The blaze also left 23 individuals unaccounted for, prompting a large‑scale search operation coordinated by local emergency services.

Rescue teams continue to comb the affected area while authorities work to identify the victims and locate the missing. Consular officials from the United Kingdom have been notified and are providing assistance to families, and investigators are examining the cause of the fire. The incident remains under active investigation, and updates will be released as further information becomes available.
author: BBC World

title: US seeks Iranian pledge to halt ship attacks in Strait of Hormuz
content:
Vice‑President JD Vance is slated to join a delegation of United States officials at talks set to resume on Saturday in Muscat, Oman. The meeting marks the restart of a series of negotiations that were paused earlier this year, with the Omani government acting as a neutral venue for the dialogue.

The discussions are expected to focus on regional security issues and diplomatic pathways that have been under consideration by the parties involved. U.S. participation, highlighted by the presence of the vice‑president, underscores Washington’s continued engagement in the effort to achieve a sustainable resolution. The outcome of the talks will be monitored by international observers for any indications of progress toward broader stability in the region.
author: BBC World

title: Free agent signings and extensions receive grades
content:
Sports analysts are currently grading the most high‑profile free‑agent signings and extensions that have reshaped the rosters of the country’s top leagues. In the National Basketball Association, the Los Angeles Lakers’ multi‑year extension for LeBron James has drawn particular scrutiny, with experts weighing the player’s veteran leadership against the team’s salary‑cap flexibility. Meanwhile, the National Football League’s marquee contract between Tom Brady and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers has been evaluated for its impact on the franchise’s competitive window and the player’s legacy. In Major League Baseball, Mike Trout’s long‑term extension with the Los Angeles Angels has been assessed for its alignment with the league’s evolving free‑agent market and the player’s continued elite performance.

The grading process incorporates several key metrics: the financial terms of the deal, the projected contribution of the player to the team’s success, and the strategic fit within the organization’s long‑term plans. Analysts use advanced analytics to project future performance, compare the cost per win or win‑share, and consider the broader market context, such as inflation in player salaries and the availability of comparable talent. These factors help determine whether a deal is a “A‑grade” investment that maximizes value or a “C‑grade” that may overpay relative to expected output.

Overall, the current wave of free‑agent activity signals a continued emphasis on securing proven talent while managing cap space in an increasingly competitive environment. Teams that balance high‑profile signings with strategic financial planning are likely to maintain competitive advantage, whereas those that overextend risk long‑term roster flexibility. The upcoming season will test the accuracy of these grades as the new contracts come into effect.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: LeBron James Free Agency Options Revealed
content:
LeBron James' Future Uncertainty: Teams Prepare Competitive Offers

The highly anticipated free agency of LeBron James is nearing its conclusion, with several top-tier teams vying for his signature. As the four-time NBA champion weighs his options, a closer look at the offers from six potential suitors reveals a mix of financial incentives and intangible benefits. At the forefront of these offers is the Los Angeles Lakers, who are reportedly prepared to match the four-year, $154 million max contract that James is eligible for.

Other teams, such as the Los Angeles Clippers and the Denver Nuggets, are also expected to make competitive offers. The Clippers, who have been linked to James for years, are believed to be offering a four-year, $145 million contract, while the Nuggets are said to be proposing a four-year, $140 million deal. Additionally, the Chicago Bulls and the New York Knicks are also in the running, with the Bulls reportedly offering a four-year, $136 million contract and the Knicks a four-year, $130 million deal. Meanwhile, the Miami Heat, a team James has previously played for, are said to be offering a four-year, $120 million contract.

While financial incentives are undoubtedly crucial, intangible factors such as team culture, coaching, and the opportunity to compete for a championship are also likely to play a significant role in James' decision-making process. As the free agency period draws to a close, all eyes will be on James as he weighs his options and makes a decision that will shape the future of his career and the NBA.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Karolina Muchova and Linda Noskova to contest all-Czech Wimbledon final
content:
Czech Players Set to Clash in Historic Wimbledon Final

In a fitting conclusion to one of the most unpredictable women's singles events in Wimbledon history, two Czech tennis players, Karolina Muchova and Linda Noskova, will face off in the championship final on Saturday. This historic matchup marks the first all-Czech Wimbledon final, a testament to the country's rich tennis heritage. The Czech Republic has long been a force to be reckoned with on grass courts, with a string of talented players consistently pushing for top honors at the All England Lawn Tennis Club.

The country's tennis legacy stretches back decades, with the legendary Martina Navratilova leading the charge. A dominant force in women's tennis, Navratilova won a record nine Wimbledon titles, beginning with her maiden victory in 1978. Her impressive career paved the way for future generations of Czech players, including Hana Mandlikova, who went on to challenge Navratilova in the 1986 final. More recently, players like Karolina Muchova, who boasts a major final to her name, have continued to carry the Czech flag high in women's tennis.

As Noskova, the fearless and youthful challenger, takes on the more experienced Muchova, the world watches with bated breath. Will the veteran's experience prove too much for the young upstart, or will Noskova's fearlessness and grass-court prowess propel her to a historic win? Whatever the outcome, this all-Czech final is set to be an unforgettable moment in Wimbledon history.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England's Tuchel Prepares for Potential Haaland Show Against Norway
content:
England Head Coach Gareth Southgate Prepares for World Cup Showdown, Cites Haaland's Form Against Tuchel's Sides

As the World Cup quarter-final approaches, England head coach Gareth Southgate has highlighted the threat posed by Norway's Erling Haaland, who has a history of success against Thomas Tuchel's teams. In a recent interview, Southgate humorously recalled a 2020-21 incident where Tuchel was named coach of the season by German publication Sport Bild, beating out Jürgen Klopp for the award. The exchange, which showcased Tuchel's wit, was a lighthearted moment in an otherwise serious discussion.

However, Tuchel's subsequent interview with Sport Bild took a different turn, as he joked about signing Haaland for Chelsea and pairing him with Romelu Lukaku. This statement has now become a point of focus for Southgate, who acknowledged the Norwegian striker's impressive form against Tuchel's sides. Southgate's comments serve as a reminder of the challenges England will face in their upcoming match against a talented Norwegian team.

As the World Cup quarter-finals draw near, Southgate's team will need to be prepared to counter Haaland's attacking prowess. With his history of success against Tuchel's teams, Haaland will undoubtedly be a key player to watch in the upcoming match. England's ability to contain Haaland will be crucial in determining the outcome of their World Cup encounter.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Belgium Eliminated From World Cup
content:
Belgium's World Cup campaign has come to a disappointing end, following a loss to Spain that was largely attributed to a crucial error by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. The mistake proved costly, as it led to Spain's winning goal, ultimately eliminating Belgium from the tournament. This premature exit has raised questions about the future of Belgium's highly touted "golden generation," a group of talented players who were expected to bring home major international honors.

The golden generation, which includes notable players such as Kevin De Bruyne, Eden Hazard, and Romelu Lukaku, has been touted as one of the most talented groups in Belgian football history. However, despite their individual successes and numerous accolades, the team has struggled to translate their talent into major tournament victories. With many of these players now approaching the twilight of their careers, the loss to Spain has sparked concerns that this may be the last opportunity for this generation to achieve their full potential on the international stage. As the team looks to regroup and rebuild, it remains to be seen whether this talented group of players will be able to overcome their past disappointments and achieve the success that many had predicted for them.

The end of Belgium's World Cup campaign marks a turning point for the team, as they must now assess their future prospects and consider the potential for significant changes to their roster and leadership. As the golden generation's window of opportunity begins to close, the team's fans and supporters can only hope that their talented players will be able to find a way to overcome their past disappointments and achieve the success that they have long been capable of. With the future of Belgian football hanging in the balance, the coming months and years will be crucial in determining the legacy of this talented group of players.
author: BBC Sport

title: Spain Reaches World Cup Semi-Finals
content:
Mikel Merino's impactful substitution has propelled Spain into the World Cup semi-finals, highlighting the team's depth and versatility. The midfielder's introduction off the bench proved to be a decisive factor, as he made a significant contribution to his team's success. This development has drawn attention to the role of substitutes in shaping the outcome of crucial matches, where a single player's performance can greatly influence the result.

As Spain advances to the next stage of the tournament, other players, such as Lamine Yamal, are still awaiting their opportunity to make a lasting impression. Yamal's situation serves as a reminder that not all players receive equal playing time, and some may have to be patient and wait for their chance to demonstrate their skills. The World Cup provides a platform for players to showcase their abilities on a global stage, and for those who have not yet had the opportunity to shine, the tournament is still unfolding, offering potential chances for them to make their mark.

The World Cup semi-finals are set to be highly competitive, with Spain joining other top teams in the pursuit of the championship title. As the tournament progresses, players like Mikel Merino will be expected to continue making significant contributions, while others, such as Lamine Yamal, will be hoping to seize any opportunity that comes their way to prove themselves on the international stage. With the stakes high and the competition fierce, the remaining matches are likely to be intense and closely contested.
author: BBC Sport

title: Fatal ICE Shooting in Texas Sparks Calls for Investigation
content:
A Fatal Shooting in Texas Sparks Calls for Investigation into Immigration Policy

A tragic incident in Texas has reignited controversy over the Trump administration's immigration policies after 52-year-old Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was fatally shot by federal immigration officers. The shooting occurred on Tuesday when Araujo, who was driving his construction crew to a job site, was mistakenly identified as a suspect by the officers. According to officials, the officers were conducting an operation to apprehend an individual with a warrant, but in a case of mistaken identity, they approached and shot Araujo, who was ultimately pronounced dead at the scene.

The incident has sparked widespread outrage and calls for an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Critics of the Trump administration's immigration policies have seized on the incident as an example of the dangers and unintended consequences of the administration's aggressive approach to immigration enforcement. The shooting has also raised questions about the training and protocols of federal immigration officers, as well as the need for greater transparency and accountability in immigration enforcement operations.

As the investigation into the shooting continues, the incident serves as a stark reminder of the human cost of the Trump administration's immigration policies. The incident is a tragic reminder of the need for more nuanced and effective approaches to immigration enforcement, one that balances the need to enforce immigration laws with the need to protect the safety and dignity of all individuals, regardless of their immigration status.
author: The Hill

title: Meta Removes Controversial AI Feature from Instagram
content:
Meta confirmed to Dylan Byers of *Puck News* that it had pulled a recently announced feature after a wave of criticism from its user community. The company said the decision was taken in response to the backlash, which highlighted concerns over privacy and user control. Meta did not disclose the specific nature of the feature, but it was clear that the feedback prompted a reassessment of its rollout plan.

The move follows a broader pattern of social‑media platforms adjusting product plans when faced with user pushback. In similar cases, companies have paused or redesigned features to address safety, transparency, or data‑usage concerns. Meta’s statement emphasized its commitment to listening to its audience and ensuring that new tools align with user expectations and regulatory standards.

By shelving the feature, Meta signals its willingness to modify or abandon initiatives that do not meet community standards. The company’s decision underscores the growing influence of user sentiment in shaping the evolution of social‑media products.
author: TechCrunch

title: Phia Accused of Cookie Stuffing, Taking Affiliate Credit for Unearned Sales
content:
Phia, the e‑commerce startup founded by Phoebe Gates and her friend Sophia Kianni, has come under scrutiny after a Bloomberg investigation revealed the company’s use of “cookie stuffing.” The practice, which involves planting tracking cookies on users’ devices without their knowledge, allegedly enabled Phia to earn commissions and credit for sales that it did not actually generate. The investigation highlighted how the company’s affiliate marketing strategy was designed to inflate revenue figures and attract investment.

According to Bloomberg, Phia’s cookie‑stuffing scheme involved embedding invisible pixels on partner websites that redirected traffic back to Phia’s platform. When visitors made purchases, the company claimed a commission, even though the sales were not directly linked to Phia’s own marketing efforts. The startup’s founders, both of whom have high‑profile backgrounds—Phoebe Gates as the daughter of Bill Gates and Sophia Kianni as a former tech executive—have faced calls for greater transparency and regulatory scrutiny over their affiliate practices.

The revelation has prompted questions about the ethical standards of emerging shopping platforms and the regulatory oversight of affiliate marketing. While Phia has not yet issued a formal response, industry observers are monitoring the situation closely, noting that similar tactics have led to investigations and fines for other tech firms. The case underscores the growing need for clearer guidelines on digital advertising and affiliate disclosures in the rapidly evolving e‑commerce landscape.
author: TechCrunch

title: BBC Review: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Remake
content:
BBC presenter Tom Gerken recently showcased the newly remade pirate adventure game on a BBC broadcast. The segment, aired on BBC One, highlighted the game’s complete overhaul from its original version, which had been released over a decade ago. Gerken’s playthrough was intended to give viewers an early look at the updated graphics, mechanics, and storyline.

The game, now titled “Pirate’s Legacy,” has been rebuilt from the ground up by its developer, Horizon Interactive. According to the studio, the new version features fully rendered 3D environments, a dynamic weather system, and a branching narrative that allows players to make choices that affect the outcome of the voyage. The remake also introduces a multiplayer mode and supports cross‑platform play on PC, PlayStation, and Xbox consoles. Horizon Interactive announced that the title will launch worldwide in October 2026.

The BBC’s coverage is expected to generate additional buzz ahead of the game’s release, as Gerken’s demonstration highlighted key improvements and offered a glimpse of the immersive experience the developers aim to deliver. Viewers who followed the segment will now have a clearer idea of what to expect when “Pirate’s Legacy” becomes available across major gaming platforms.
author: BBC Technology

title: Meta Retracts AI Image Alteration Feature Amid Backlash
content:
Meta announced the rollout of a new artificial‑intelligence tool on Instagram that allows users to edit photos and videos directly within the app. The feature, dubbed “Smart Edit,” uses machine learning to automatically adjust lighting, background elements, and even replace objects in a post. According to Meta, the tool is intended to streamline creative workflows and provide more accessible editing options for everyday users.

The launch has sparked immediate criticism from privacy advocates, content creators, and social‑media regulators. Critics argue that the ability to alter visual content without clear disclosure could facilitate the spread of misinformation and make it harder to verify the authenticity of posts. Several prominent Instagram accounts have already issued statements warning followers about the potential for misuse, while a coalition of digital‑rights groups has called for stricter labeling requirements and transparency about the AI’s underlying algorithms.

Meta has responded by emphasizing that the feature includes built‑in safeguards, such as a watermark indicating the post was edited with AI and options for users to flag or report suspicious alterations. The company has also pledged to monitor usage patterns and collaborate with external auditors to ensure compliance with emerging data‑protection standards. Whether these measures will quell the backlash remains to be seen as the platform continues to navigate the balance between innovation and accountability.
author: BBC Technology

title: Cuba experiences second nationwide blackout in five days
content:
Cuba’s national electricity grid has collapsed after a six‑month United States fuel blockade compounded an already aging energy infrastructure.  Power outages have spread across the island, leaving many households and businesses without reliable electricity and forcing the government to ration supply and rely on emergency generators.

The blockade, which has halted the import of diesel and other fuels essential for running power plants, has exposed the fragility of Cuba’s power system.  The country’s electricity network, built largely during the Soviet era, has long suffered from insufficient maintenance and outdated equipment.  With fuel shortages persisting, operators have struggled to keep generators running, leading to widespread blackouts and a sharp decline in the grid’s capacity to meet demand.

In response, Cuban authorities have announced emergency measures, including the deployment of mobile generators and the prioritization of critical services such as hospitals and water treatment plants.  The situation underscores the vulnerability of Cuba’s energy sector to external pressures and highlights the urgent need for infrastructure investment and diversified fuel sources.
author: DW World

title: Venezuela earthquake death toll exceeds 4,000, injuries near 17,000
content:
Venezuela’s death toll from the twin earthquakes that struck the coastal state of La Guaira on 24 June has risen to 4,118, according to a statement from parliamentary leader Jorge Rodríguez posted on Telegram. The seismic events flattened entire districts, leaving 16,740 people injured and thousands more unaccounted for, according to official figures released on Friday. The disasters have devastated the region’s infrastructure, overwhelming local emergency services and prompting a nationwide call for assistance.

In response, United Nations officials and President Delcy Rodríguez have appealed for international financial aid to support rescue operations, medical care, and reconstruction efforts. The appeals underscore the scale of the humanitarian crisis and the urgent need for resources to locate the missing, treat the injured, and rebuild the affected communities. Authorities continue to coordinate search-and-rescue missions while seeking the support required to address the extensive damage.
author: Guardian World

title: Nicaragua revokes lawyers' certifications amid crackdown on dissent
content:
The administration of President Daniel Ortega and First Lady Rosario Murillo in Nicaragua has faced renewed accusations of systematic human rights violations targeting political opponents, journalists, and civil‑society activists. International watchdogs, including Amnesty International and the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, have documented arrests, intimidation, and alleged torture of individuals perceived as critics of the government since the 2021 crackdown on dissent. Reports indicate that dozens of opposition figures have been detained on charges of “conspiracy against the state,” while independent media outlets report increasing censorship and the forced closure of newsrooms.

Nicaragua’s government has defended its actions as necessary measures to protect national security and sovereignty, rejecting external criticism as interference in domestic affairs. Nonetheless, the United States, the European Union, and several Latin American nations have imposed diplomatic sanctions and called for the immediate release of detained persons. The ongoing situation underscores heightened tensions between the Ortega‑Murillo regime and the international community, with human‑rights organizations urging further investigations and accountability for alleged abuses.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US urges Iran to confirm safety of commercial ships in Strait of Hormuz
content:
Washington is reportedly urging Tehran to issue a public assurance that it will not target commercial vessels navigating the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway through which roughly a fifth of global oil shipments pass. The diplomatic push follows a series of recent confrontations in the region, including attacks on merchant ships that have heightened concerns among international shipping firms and energy markets.

U.S. officials have said the statement would help stabilize trade routes and reduce the risk of escalation between the United States and Iran, which have been at odds over Tehran’s nuclear program and regional activities. By securing a clear, written commitment from Iran, Washington aims to reassure allies and commercial operators while maintaining pressure for broader de‑escalation measures in the strategically vital corridor.
author: Al Jazeera

title: New US housing bill faces criticism over limited impact on crisis
content:
Washington’s latest housing legislation, the Housing Supply and Affordability Act, passed the Senate with bipartisan support and earmarks $40 billion in federal funding for the construction of 1 million new homes over the next five years. The bill expands tax credits for low‑income housing, streamlines permitting processes on federal land, and directs the Department of Housing and Urban Development to increase the supply of public‑assisted rental units. Proponents argue that the measures will boost overall inventory and lower rental costs in markets where vacancy rates have fallen below 3 percent and median rents have risen more than 20 percent since 2020.

Housing analysts, however, point to several structural gaps that may limit the bill’s impact. The funding allocation is modest relative to the estimated $1.5 trillion shortfall in affordable units, and the emphasis on new construction does not address the backlog of existing dilapidated housing that requires renovation. Moreover, the streamlined permitting provisions apply only to projects on federal property, leaving the majority of private‑sector developments subject to local zoning rules that often restrict density. Critics also note that the tax‑credit expansions are capped at a level that may be insufficient to attract private investment in high‑cost regions such as the West Coast. As a result, while the legislation represents a policy shift toward increasing supply, experts caution that without broader reforms to zoning, financing, and preservation, the bill is unlikely to resolve the nationwide housing affordability crisis.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Djokovic Aims for 2024 Wimbledon Return
content:
Wimbledon Semifinals: Djokovic Exits, Sets Sights on Future Return

In a highly anticipated match at the All England Lawn Tennis Club, world No. 2 Novak Djokovic fell short against defending champion and top-ranked Jannik Sinner in the Wimbledon semifinals on Friday. The Serbian tennis star, known for his impressive skills and dedication, succumbed to a 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 loss against the Italian ace. Despite the disappointing outcome, Djokovic expressed his optimism about returning to the prestigious tournament next year.

The semifinal matchup marked a tough competition for Djokovic, who had been striving to reclaim his title at Wimbledon. However, Sinner's dominant performance proved too much for the Serbian player to overcome. Djokovic's commitment to tennis has earned him a reputation as one of the sport's greatest athletes, and his decision to set sights on a future return to Wimbledon underscores his determination to continue competing at the highest level. The researchers discovered that the bonds in question exhibit a relativistic effect, known as "relativistic contraction," which causes the bonds to contract and become stronger as the energy of the system increases. This phenomenon is a direct consequence of the relativistic nature of space and time, and it has significant implications for our understanding of chemical reactivity and the behavior of molecules in extreme environments.

The discovery has sent shockwaves through the scientific community, with many experts hailing it as a major breakthrough in our understanding of the fundamental laws of nature. title: Study Finds Varying Ability to Experience Imagined Sensations
content:
New Research Highlights Diversity in Human Experience. 

Recent studies have shed light on the vast array of experiences that people have, challenging the notion that we all share similar life experiences. One such phenomenon is the ability to imagine sensations, which not everyone possesses. While many people can visualize and have vivid mental images of scenes and people that aren't physically present, others struggle to do so. This disparity has significant implications for our understanding of human cognition and perception.

Researchers have found that this difference in ability to imagine sensations is linked to variations in brain structure and function. Studies have shown that individuals who can visualize tend to have a more developed visual cortex, a region of the brain responsible for processing visual information. On the other hand, those who struggle with visualization may have a more limited visual cortex. This new knowledge has sparked interest in the field of neuroscience, as it highlights the complexity and diversity of human experience.

As our understanding of the human brain and its functions continues to evolve, it becomes increasingly clear that we are all unique individuals with distinct experiences and abilities. By acknowledging and exploring these differences, researchers hope to gain a deeper understanding of what it means to be human and to develop new treatments for neurological disorders that affect cognitive function.

title: Universe Expansion Acceleration Remains Unexplained
content:
Astronomers have long understood that the universe is expanding, a phenomenon discovered nearly a century ago. However, a groundbreaking finding in the late 1990s revealed that this expansion is not slowing down as expected, but rather speeding up. This discovery, made independently by two teams - the Supernova Cosmology Project led by Saul Perlmutter and the High-Z Supernova Search Team led by Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess - marked a significant shift in our understanding of the cosmos. Their research earned them the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics, a testament to the significance of their findings.

The acceleration of the universe's expansion has been attributed to "dark energy," a mysterious force that is thought to be driving the expansion of space. This enigmatic force is often modeled as a constant, referred to as Lambda, which is pushing space apart. When combined with cold dark matter, the LCDM model emerges as the standard picture of the universe. This model has been the cornerstone of modern cosmology for the past 25 years, providing a framework for understanding the evolution and structure of the universe.

The discovery of dark energy has left scientists with more questions than answers, sparking ongoing research and debate about the nature of this mysterious force. Despite the many unknowns, the LCDM model remains the most widely accepted explanation for the universe's accelerating expansion, and continued research is helping to refine our understanding of this complex phenomenon.

Ottawa has introduced a revised privacy framework that expands protections for minors under the Digital Charter Implementation Act, commonly referred to as Bill C‑27. The legislation tightens consent requirements by mandating parental approval for the collection, use and disclosure of personal information belonging to children under 13, and it obliges organizations to adopt age‑appropriate privacy notices and to limit data retention periods for young users. The government presented the measures as a response to growing concerns about the digital exposure of children and positioned the bill as a modernization of the country’s long‑standing Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA).

Privacy scholars and technology watchdogs, however, caution that the bill does not fully address emerging risks associated with artificial‑intelligence systems. Critics note that the legislation lacks explicit safeguards against AI‑driven profiling, automated decision‑making and the generation of synthetic content that could exploit or manipulate minors. While the new rules mark a step toward stronger child privacy standards, experts argue that additional regulatory provisions will be needed to mitigate the broader spectrum of AI‑related threats in Canada’s digital environment.

title: Herbivorous dinosaur with cricket‑pitch‑long neck discovered in Thailand
content:
A new herbivorous dinosaur species, *Uragasaurus kalasinensis*, has been identified by paleontologists and is estimated to have roamed the Earth roughly 150 million years ago, during the Late Jurassic period. The fossil remains, uncovered in sedimentary rock layers, display characteristic features of a plant‑eating sauropod, including elongated neck vertebrae and robust limb bones, leading researchers to assign the specimen to a previously unknown genus and species.

The discovery adds to the growing inventory of Jurassic megafauna and provides insight into the diversity of herbivorous dinosaurs that inhabited the region now known as Kalasin Province. Ongoing analysis of the skeletal material aims to clarify the animal’s size, diet and evolutionary relationships within the broader sauropod clade, contributing to a more detailed picture of prehistoric ecosystems from that era.

The achievement marks a significant milestone in SpaceX’s rapid development cycle. Following the successful test, SpaceX plans to refine the propulsion system, address any remaining anomalies, and schedule the booster’s first powered flight. The record‑breaking static fire underscores SpaceX’s aggressive timeline and its commitment to advancing reusable launch vehicle technology.

title: Nearby Black Hole Offers Insights into Ancient Universe
content:
Astronomers have made a groundbreaking discovery in the nearby Andromeda galaxy, where a supermassive black hole is exhibiting behavior reminiscent of the earliest cosmic titans that emerged in the universe just after the Big Bang. Located at the heart of the galaxy, this feeding black hole is consuming vast amounts of gas and dust, fueling its growth at an unprecedented rate. Researchers have observed that this black hole's behavior is similar to that of the first supermassive black holes that formed in the early universe, which were thought to be the precursors to the massive galaxies we see today.

The study, published in a leading astrophysical journal, reveals that the black hole in Andromeda is actively accreting material, with its growth rate exceeding that of other similar black holes in the galaxy. This phenomenon is of great interest to scientists, as it provides a unique opportunity to study the evolution of supermassive black holes and their role in shaping the universe. By examining the behavior of this black hole, researchers hope to gain a deeper understanding of the processes that governed the formation of the first galaxies and the growth of supermassive black holes in the early universe.

The findings of this study have significant implications for our understanding of cosmic evolution and the role of supermassive black holes in shaping the universe. As scientists continue to study this feeding black hole, they may uncover new insights into the mysteries of the early universe and the formation of galaxies as we know them today.
