Meteorological agencies, including the Japan Meteorological Agency and the China Meteorological Administration, have upgraded the storm to a super‑typhoon, projecting sustained winds of 150–170 km/h (93–106 mph) and gusts exceeding 200 km/h (124 mph). The storm is expected to make landfall within the next 48 hours, prompting the issuance of the highest-level typhoon warnings for Taiwan’s eastern coast and China’s Fujian and Zhejiang provinces. Authorities have ordered evacuations of coastal communities, suspended ferry services, and mobilized emergency response teams to reinforce flood defenses and prepare shelters.

Bavi is being described as one of the strongest storms to affect the region in several decades, comparable in size and intensity to the 1999 Typhoon Lekima and the 2009 Typhoon Morakot. Forecast models indicate a rapid intensification as the system moves over warm sea‑surface temperatures, raising concerns about heavy rainfall, landslides, and storm surge that could threaten densely populated areas. Residents have been advised to secure property, avoid low‑lying zones, and stay tuned to official updates. The combined preparedness measures aim to mitigate potential loss of life and infrastructure damage as Bavi approaches landfall later this week.
author: BBC World

title: China Lands Rocket After Orbital Launch
content:
A significant milestone was achieved in the field of space exploration on Friday, July 10, as a Chinese Long March 10B rocket successfully completed its maiden launch. The rocket, which is a crucial component of China's ambitious space program, performed flawlessly, sending a satellite into orbit and paving the way for future missions. This achievement marks a major step forward for China's space agency, demonstrating its capabilities in designing and launching advanced rockets.

The Long March 10B rocket's successful launch and subsequent landing at sea are particularly noteworthy. The ability to recover rockets after launch is a complex and challenging task, requiring precise calculations and advanced technology. By achieving a controlled landing at sea, China has demonstrated its mastery of this complex process, which is essential for reducing the cost of access to space and increasing the efficiency of launch operations. The satellite deployed by the Long March 10B rocket is expected to play a vital role in supporting various applications, including communication, navigation, and Earth observation.

The successful debut of the Long March 10B rocket is a testament to China's growing presence in the global space industry. As the country continues to push the boundaries of space exploration and development, it is likely to have a significant impact on the future of space travel and research. With this achievement, China has reaffirmed its commitment to advancing its space program and expanding its capabilities in this critical area. The success of the Long March 10B rocket is a significant step forward, and it will be interesting to see how China's space agency builds on this momentum in the months and years to come.
author: Space.com

title: Bellingham and Haaland meet as England faces Norway in World Cup quarter‑final
content:
The 2026 World Cup has shifted its spotlight from the long‑dominated Messi–Ronaldo era to a new generation of stars. England’s quarter‑final against Norway on Saturday night will feature the first international clash between Jude Bellingham of Manchester City and Erling Haaland of Real Madrid. The two players, who have met on three Champions League stages over the past three seasons, are now set to face each other for the first time on a national team.

Bellingham and Haaland’s friendship began two years ago while both were at Borussia Dortmund. Their time together at BVB forged a bond that has been highlighted by the media, and the pair have continued to collaborate in the Champions League, exchanging goals and assists for their respective clubs. Their upcoming World Cup encounter is being framed by tabloids as the start of a new “superstar rivalry,” a narrative that could define the tournament in ways distinct from the likes of Mbappé or Yamal.

With the Ballon d’Or debate already on the horizon, the England–Norway match offers a fresh storyline: the clash of two young, world‑class forwards whose careers have intersected in club football but not yet on the international stage. The game will not only decide a quarter‑final spot but also set the tone for how the next generation of football stars will be perceived in the global arena.
author: Guardian Sport

title: France Beats Morocco in World Cup Match
content:
The French national team has undergone a significant transformation under the guidance of head coach Didier Deschamps, as evident in their recent World Cup knockout performance against Morocco. In contrast to their match against the same opponents four years ago in Qatar, France's current style of play is vastly superior, with a notable emphasis on a freeform attacking line. This shift in approach has been a deliberate effort by Deschamps, who has sought to reinvent his team's tactical strategy over the course of a single tournament cycle.

The results of this new approach were on full display as France advanced to the semi-final, thanks in large part to the dynamic duo of Kylian Mbappé and Ousmane Dembélé. The pair's one-two punch proved to be the decisive factor in the match, showcasing the effectiveness of Deschamps' tactical reinvention. The scoreline may have been identical to the previous encounter between the two teams, but the difference in style and overall performance was stark. France's ability to adapt and evolve under Deschamps' guidance has been a key factor in their success, and their current form suggests that they will be a formidable opponent in the semi-final.

The success of Deschamps' new approach is a testament to his ability to evolve and adapt as a coach, and France's continued progress in the tournament will be closely watched by fans and pundits alike. With their semi-final berth secured, the team will look to build on their momentum and make a deep run in the competition. As the tournament unfolds, it will be interesting to see how France's new style of play continues to develop and whether they can ultimately achieve their goal of winning the World Cup.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Arthur Fery Faces Alexander Zverev in Wimbledon Semi-Finals
content:
In a stunning turn of events, wildcard Arthur Fery has defied expectations to reach the semi-finals of Wimbledon, leaving the tennis world in awe. Despite being considered the underdog in most of his matches, Fery has demonstrated remarkable resilience and skill to overcome his opponents, including a notable win against Grigor Dimitrov in the fourth round and Flavio Cobolli in the quarter-finals. His impressive run has been a highlight of the tournament, with many now eager to see how he will fare against his next opponent.

As Fery prepares to face French Open champion Alexander Zverev in the semi-finals, he will need to excel in specific areas to topple the highly skilled opponent. Zverev's experience and expertise on the court will undoubtedly pose a significant challenge for Fery, requiring him to elevate his game to new heights. To reach the Wimbledon final, Fery will need to leverage his strengths and capitalize on any weaknesses Zverev may exhibit, all while maintaining his focus and composure under pressure. The match promises to be an exciting and closely watched encounter, with Fery's determination and skill pitted against Zverev's formidable talent.

The outcome of the semi-final match remains uncertain, but one thing is clear: Arthur Fery's remarkable run to the semi-finals has already made this Wimbledon tournament one to remember. Regardless of the result, Fery's achievement is a testament to his hard work and dedication to the sport, and his performance will undoubtedly be closely watched by tennis fans around the world. As the stage is set for the highly anticipated match against Alexander Zverev, Fery will look to draw on his experience and skill to push his opponent to the limit and potentially create another upset in the tournament.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England Player Reacts to Mexico Coach's Heckle
content:
England winger Anthony Gordon has downplayed a heated exchange with Mexico manager Javier Aguirre during their recent World Cup match. A viral video clip showed Aguirre swearing at Gordon, but the English player has chosen to brush off the incident. According to Gordon, the confrontation was "just a bit of fun", suggesting that he did not take offense to the Mexican coach's outburst.

The incident occurred during a tense moment in the match, with emotions running high on both sides. Despite the intense language used by Aguirre, Gordon's response indicates that he does not believe the exchange was a significant issue. The England player's ability to laugh off the incident may help to diffuse any potential tension between the two teams. The World Cup is known for its high-stakes matches and intense rivalries, but Gordon's lighthearted response may help to shift the focus back to the football.

The match itself was a closely contested affair, with both teams giving their all in pursuit of victory. Gordon's comments on the incident with Aguirre will likely be seen as a positive sign of sportsmanship and a willingness to move on from the controversy. As the World Cup continues, players and coaches will be under intense scrutiny, and Gordon's response to the incident may set a positive tone for the rest of the tournament.
author: BBC Sport

title: Djokovic Faces Sinner in Wimbledon Semis
content:
Novak Djokovic and Jannik Sinner are set to face off in the Wimbledon semi-finals, marking a rematch between the two tennis stars. This upcoming match comes after both players have navigated their way through the tournament, albeit with differing levels of challenge and success. Djokovic, a seasoned veteran with a storied history at Wimbledon, has brought his characteristic level of skill and determination to the court, while Sinner has shown impressive resilience and adaptability in his own right.

As the tournament has progressed, both Djokovic and Sinner have demonstrated their unique strengths and abilities, with Djokovic drawing upon his extensive experience and Sinner showcasing his growing prowess as a rising star in the tennis world. Their semi-final match is highly anticipated, given the contrast in their tournament journeys thus far. While Djokovic has largely dominated his opponents, Sinner has faced tougher challenges, pushing through intense matches to secure his place in the semi-finals. The stage is now set for an intriguing showdown between these two talented athletes, each seeking to outmaneuver the other and claim a spot in the final.

The semi-final match between Djokovic and Sinner promises to be an exciting and closely watched contest, with both players vying for a coveted spot in the Wimbledon final. As the tennis world turns its attention to this high-stakes match, fans and spectators alike will be eager to see which player emerges victorious, and whether Djokovic's experience will prove too great for Sinner to overcome, or if the young Italian can pull off a major upset and continue his impressive run at the tournament.
author: BBC Sport

title: Spain Coach Luis de la Fuente Discusses Team Identity
content:
As Spain prepares to face Belgium in the World Cup quarter-finals, the team's identity and strategy have come under scrutiny. In a recent interview, Spain boss Luis de la Fuente shared his thoughts on the team's approach and philosophy. De la Fuente emphasized the importance of maintaining a strong sense of identity and cohesion within the team, highlighting the need for his players to work together seamlessly in order to achieve success.

De la Fuente also discussed the role of individual players, including Lamine Yamal, who has been making waves with his impressive performances. The Spain boss praised Yamal's skills and adaptability, suggesting that he has been a valuable asset to the team. With the quarter-final match against Belgium looming, de la Fuente's comments provide insight into Spain's mindset and approach as they look to advance to the next stage of the tournament. The match is expected to be highly competitive, with both teams boasting talented squads and a strong desire to win.

The outcome of the quarter-final match will have significant implications for both teams, and de la Fuente's strategy and player selections will be closely watched. As Spain takes on Belgium, fans and pundits alike will be eager to see how the team's identity and individual players, including Yamal, contribute to the overall performance. With the stakes high and the competition fierce, the match promises to be an exciting and closely contested encounter.
author: BBC Sport

title: Ann Widdecombe Dies Aged 78
content:
Ann Widdecombe, a British politician and former Member of Parliament, rose to prominence in the latter stages of her career as a vocal advocate for Brexit. With a career spanning multiple decades, Widdecombe initially gained recognition for her work within the Conservative Party, serving as a member of parliament from 1987 to 2010. Her early years in politics were marked by her involvement in various roles, including Minister of State for Employment and Minister of State for Prisons.

As the Brexit debate gained momentum, Widdecombe emerged as a key figure, leveraging her experience and platform to argue in favor of the United Kingdom's departure from the European Union. Her pro-Brexit stance was characterized by her unwavering commitment to the cause, which resonated with many who shared her views on sovereignty and national identity. Widdecombe's ability to articulate her perspective and engage with audiences helped to establish her as a prominent voice within the pro-Brexit movement, transcending her earlier work within the Conservative Party.

In conclusion, Ann Widdecombe's evolution into a dominant pro-Brexit voice marked a significant shift in her career, as she harnessed her political experience and passion to advocate for a cause that resonated deeply with her. Through her tireless efforts, Widdecombe played a notable role in shaping the Brexit debate, leaving a lasting impact on British politics and cementing her legacy as a vocal and dedicated champion of the pro-Brexit movement.
author: BBC Politics

title: Scientists Observe Prestellar Core Dynamics Before Star Formation
content:
Stars such as our Sun begin their lives when cold, dense concentrations of gas and dust—known as prestellar cores—collapse under their own gravity. These cores, which are held together by gravitational forces, represent the earliest stage of star formation. While the broad outline of this process is understood, many details about how material accretes onto the nascent star and how angular momentum is redistributed remain uncertain.

Recent observations with advanced radio telescopes have begun to illuminate these inner workings. By probing the millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths emitted by the dense gas, astronomers can trace the motion of material within the collapsing core and identify the formation of protostellar disks. These high‑resolution studies reveal complex velocity patterns and chemical gradients that help constrain models of how stars gather mass and shed excess angular momentum.

The new data underscore the value of radio astronomy in addressing longstanding questions about stellar birth. As instrumentation continues to improve, researchers anticipate further breakthroughs that will refine our understanding of the physical processes governing the earliest stages of star formation.
author: Phys.org

title: Uber Eats $15 Promo Code Available in July 2026
content:
Uber Eats has rolled out a new suite of savings options aimed at both new and existing customers, allowing users to cut delivery fees and meal costs through verified promo codes, first‑time user offers, and Uber One membership discounts. The platform’s promotional engine now features a rotating list of codes that can be applied at checkout, with each code verified for authenticity and expiration dates. Users can find these codes on the Uber Eats app, partner websites, and official social‑media channels, ensuring that the discounts are both legitimate and timely.

For those who have never ordered through Uber Eats before, a dedicated new‑user promotion offers a substantial discount on the first delivery, typically ranging from 20 % off to a flat‑rate reduction on the delivery fee. In addition, the Uber One subscription—available in several tiers—provides a continuous discount on delivery charges, with higher tiers unlocking a 10 % reduction and access to exclusive partner deals. These offers are designed to encourage trial and repeat usage, while also rewarding loyal customers with consistent savings.

Overall, the combination of verified promo codes, first‑time user incentives, and Uber One discounts creates a layered savings strategy that can significantly reduce the cost of food delivery. By leveraging these options, consumers can enjoy lower delivery fees and discounted meals without compromising on the convenience that Uber Eats delivers.
author: Wired

title: Chewy Promo Codes: $20 Off First Order & More in July 2026
content:
Chewy, the online retailer specializing in pet supplies, has announced a series of promotional codes for July 2026 aimed at reducing costs for customers nationwide. The latest offers include a $30 discount applicable to orders meeting a minimum spend threshold, a $20 reduction on first‑time purchases of $49 or more, and a limited‑time 50 % markdown on select pet food brands. Shoppers can redeem the codes during checkout by entering the alphanumeric strings provided on Chewy’s website or through partner newsletters, with each promotion subject to standard terms such as one‑use per account and expiration at the end of the month.

Industry analysts note that the July discounts align with Chewy’s broader strategy to attract new customers while encouraging repeat business from existing pet owners. The company reports that similar campaigns have historically driven a measurable uptick in order volume and average basket size. Consumers are advised to review the specific eligibility criteria for each code, as exclusions may apply to certain product categories or brand‑specific items. The promotions are expected to conclude on July 31, after which Chewy will likely introduce new offers for the subsequent quarter.
author: Wired

title: UN AI for Good Summit Addresses Governance Challenges Amid Tech Boom
content:
At the UN’s AI for Good summit, live‑coding workshops ran alongside a palpable sense of Silicon Valley optimism, yet the event’s central focus remained the question of whether global governance can keep pace with the rapid development of artificial intelligence. Delegates from governments, academia, and industry gathered to showcase real‑time AI prototypes while debating the regulatory frameworks needed to manage the technology’s societal impact.

The summit’s sessions highlighted both the promise and the risks of AI. Participants demonstrated applications ranging from climate modeling to medical diagnostics, underscoring the potential for positive global outcomes. At the same time, experts warned that the speed of innovation—often driven by private sector competition—may outstrip existing international norms. Discussions addressed the need for coordinated standards, transparency, and ethical guidelines, with several countries proposing joint initiatives to monitor algorithmic bias and data privacy.

In closing, summit leaders called for an accelerated, multilateral effort to update governance mechanisms, noting that without timely reforms, the technology race could outstrip the world’s ability to manage its consequences. The UN’s statement emphasized the urgency of establishing a flexible, enforceable framework that can adapt to future AI advances while safeguarding human rights and global stability.
author: Wired

title: Vivo joint venture signals new phase in India's smartphone manufacturing boom
content:
Vivo has launched a joint venture with Indian electronics manufacturer XYZ Ltd. to establish a full‑scale smartphone assembly and research facility in Tamil Nadu. The partnership, announced in March, commits roughly $500 million to a plant capable of producing up to 10 million units annually, with an additional $100 million earmarked for a local research and development centre. By localising production, the venture aims to meet India’s “Make in India” requirements, reduce the impact of import duties on components, and shorten supply‑chain lead times for the country’s second‑largest smartphone market.

The collaboration aligns with recent policy shifts that encourage foreign firms to increase domestic content in their products. Under the agreement, XYZ will provide manufacturing expertise and access to a network of local suppliers, while Vivo contributes its brand portfolio, software ecosystem and global design capabilities. The joint venture is expected to begin commercial shipments by the fourth quarter of 2025 and will create approximately 3,000 jobs across engineering, production and logistics functions.

Industry analysts view the arrangement as a potential blueprint for other Chinese smartphone makers seeking to deepen their foothold in India amid heightened regulatory scrutiny and competitive pressure. By sharing capital costs, leveraging local partnerships and complying with government incentives, firms such as Xiaomi, Oppo and Realme could replicate Vivo’s model to sustain growth and navigate the evolving Indian market landscape.
author: TechCrunch

title: SK hynix targets $26.5 billion raise in US Nasdaq listing amid AI demand
content:
South Korean semiconductor firm SK hynix announced the pricing of its U.S. initial public offering on Friday, targeting a raise of roughly $26.5 billion. The company will list about 18 million shares on the Nasdaq, a transaction that would rank among the largest equity offerings ever conducted on the exchange. The pricing reflects strong investor demand driven by the firm’s position as a leading supplier of advanced memory chips used in artificial‑intelligence (AI) data centers.

SK hynix’s profit surge has been attributed to the global race to build AI‑focused data facilities, which has heightened demand for high‑performance memory solutions. By tapping the buoyant AI market, the chip maker aims to capitalize on heightened capital flows into technology stocks, while the proceeds are expected to fund further expansion of its manufacturing capacity and research initiatives. The listing underscores the broader trend of semiconductor companies leveraging AI‑related growth to attract sizable funding in international markets.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Iran buries Supreme Leader Khamenei in Mashhad as crowds gather
content:
Former Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei’s coffin, wrapped in a flag, was carried into the shrine of Imam Reza in Mashhad, his hometown in eastern Iran, amid a large crowd of mourners. The procession, which moved through the shrine’s courtyard, was accompanied by prayers and the solemn chanting of the faithful, while the public watched from outside the complex.  

The ceremony was marked by the absence of Khamenei’s son, successor Ali Reza Mojtaba Khamenei, who did not attend the funeral rites. The event drew thousands of people who gathered to pay respects to the former leader, whose death has prompted a nationwide period of mourning and a formal state funeral.  

As the flag‑covered coffin was lowered into the shrine’s sacred precinct, the crowd dispersed, and the shrine’s doors remained closed to the public, concluding the solemn tribute to the former Supreme Leader.
author: Euronews

title: France Defeats Morocco 2-0 to Reach World Cup Semi-Finals
content:
In a match that drew fans across continents, France secured a berth in the FIFA World Cup semi‑finals with a 2‑0 victory over Morocco on July 9. The game, played at the Stade de France in Paris, saw the French side dominate possession and create several key chances, ultimately finding the net twice to seal the win. The triumph was celebrated by jubilant supporters in Paris and echoed back to the United States, where fans gathered at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, to cheer on their team.

The match carried significant weight for both squads. France, the defending champions, had already advanced from their group but faced a formidable Moroccan side that had impressed in earlier rounds. The 2‑0 result not only confirmed France’s place in the semi‑finals but also highlighted their tactical discipline and offensive potency. Morocco, meanwhile, were denied a historic run to the knockout stages, ending a campaign that had seen them upset several higher‑ranked teams.

With the semi‑finals approaching, France will now prepare to face one of the remaining finalists, while Morocco will reflect on a campaign that exceeded expectations. The victory underscores France’s continued strength on the world stage and sets the stage for a high‑stakes showdown in the next round of the tournament.
author: Euronews

title: Mourners bury former Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in Mashhad
content:
On 9 July, thousands of mourners gathered in Mashhad to pay their respects to former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The crowds marched through the city’s streets before proceeding to the Imam Reza Shrine, where the burial ceremony took place. The procession was marked by solemn chants and the display of national flags, underscoring the reverence with which the event was observed.

The Imam Reza Shrine, one of Iran’s most sacred sites, served as the final resting place for Khamenei, who had led the country for decades. The burial attracted dignitaries from across the nation and international observers, reflecting the leader’s significant influence on Iranian politics and society. Security was heightened throughout Mashhad to accommodate the large turnout and ensure the smooth conduct of the rites.

Following the burial, mourners dispersed with a sense of closure, while the shrine’s gates remained open for visitors wishing to pay their respects. The event marked the end of an era in Iranian leadership, with the nation now turning its attention to the next chapter in its political history.
author: Euronews

title: North Korea Plans to Strengthen Nuclear Arsenal and Modernize Naval Bases
content:
North Korean officials announced plans to speed up the construction of modern naval bases and to upgrade combat systems, the state news agency Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported on Tuesday. The directive was delivered during a high‑level meeting of senior military and party leaders, which emphasized the need to enhance the country’s maritime defense infrastructure in line with ongoing efforts to modernize the armed forces.

KCNA said the accelerated building program will focus on expanding existing facilities and establishing new bases equipped with advanced technology, while the combat‑system upgrades will incorporate newer weaponry and electronic warfare capabilities. The announcement follows a series of statements in recent months highlighting North Korea’s priority on strengthening its naval power, and it underscores the regime’s continued investment in military development despite international sanctions.
author: Euronews

title: China Investigates 28-Dead Shoe Factory Fire in Jinjiang
content:
China’s authorities have launched an investigation into a fatal fire that occurred on 9 July at a shoe factory in Jinjiang, Fujian Province. The blaze, which was reported to have caused 28 deaths, has prompted an inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the incident and the factory’s safety protocols.

Preliminary reports indicate that the fire broke out in the manufacturing area of the plant, quickly spreading and trapping workers inside. Emergency services responded promptly, but the rapid escalation of the fire limited rescue efforts. Investigators are examining the building’s fire suppression systems, electrical wiring, and compliance with local safety regulations.

The investigation remains ongoing, with officials seeking to determine the cause of the fire and whether any violations of occupational safety standards contributed to the tragedy. No additional casualties have been reported beyond the 28 confirmed deaths, and further details will be released as the inquiry progresses.
author: Euronews

title: Moroccan community gathers in Boston to watch World Cup 2026 quarter-final vs France
content:
Boston, Massachusetts, hosts one of the largest Moroccan communities in the United States, a fact that was on full display during the 2022 FIFA World Cup quarter‑final between Morocco and France. Thousands of community members gathered in the city’s downtown area, lining up to watch the match on large screens and to cheer on the national team that had made history by reaching the semi‑finals for the first time.

The crowd, which included families, students, and local business owners, wore Moroccan colors and flags, creating a vibrant atmosphere that echoed the excitement of the game. Organizers noted that the turnout was the largest seen for any diaspora event in Boston that year, and local media reported that the energy in the streets helped bring a sense of unity among residents of diverse backgrounds.

The enthusiastic support from Boston’s Moroccan community highlights the strong ties between the diaspora and their homeland, and underscores the impact of the national team’s performance on fans abroad. Their presence at the quarter‑final against France serves as a reminder of how international sporting events can galvanize communities and foster a shared sense of pride.
author: France 24

title: North Korea to Expand Nuclear Arsenal and Spy Activities in South Korea
content:
North Korea announced on Friday that it intends to strengthen its nuclear arsenal “both in quality and quantity,” according to a statement from the state media outlet Rodong Sinmun. The declaration followed a decision made by a military commission meeting, underscoring the regime’s ongoing effort to modernize its nuclear weapons capability amid continued international scrutiny.

In addition to the nuclear upgrade, the North also revealed plans to intensify its espionage operations against South Korea “in a radical way.” The move comes as Seoul has repeatedly warned of growing threats from the north, citing increased surveillance and covert activities along the demilitarized zone. The announcement signals a heightened focus on intelligence gathering that could complicate diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions on the peninsula.

The statements arrive at a time when the international community remains vigilant over North Korea’s nuclear tests and missile launches. While the regime has not provided detailed timelines for the proposed enhancements, the announcement is likely to prompt renewed calls from the United States and South Korea for a return to negotiations and a stricter enforcement of sanctions.
author: France 24

title: Bayeux Tapestry arrives in London on year-long loan from France
content:
The medieval Bayeux Tapestry, a 1,000‑year‑old embroidered record of the Norman Conquest, arrived in London early on Friday. The 70‑meter long cloth, which has been housed in France since 1924, is now on loan to the British Museum for a one‑year exhibition.

Security concerns prompted a highly confidential transport plan. The tapestry was moved in a secure, undisclosed route and was only revealed to the public upon its arrival. The British Museum will display the piece in its Special Collections gallery, allowing visitors to view the historic narrative in its original scale for the first time in a millennium.

The loan arrangement underscores the cultural cooperation between France and the United Kingdom. After the exhibition period ends, the tapestry will return to its French home, continuing its long history of preservation and public display.
author: France 24

title: France defeats Morocco 2-0 to reach World Cup semi-finals
content:
Les Bleus secured a place in the World Cup semi‑finals on Thursday, marking the third consecutive tournament in which France has reached this stage. Didier Deschamps’ side faced Morocco, whose disciplined defence limited France’s attacking options during the opening half‑hour.

The French attack broke through in the second half, with Kylian Mbappé opening the scoring before Ousmane Dembélé added a second, delivering a 2‑0 victory. With the win, France will meet the winner of the Spain‑Belgium quarter‑final for a spot in the final, continuing their pursuit of the championship.
author: France 24

title: Iran allegedly plotted to assassinate Trump, Israeli intel claims
content:
A fresh alleged plot to kill former U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed by Israeli intelligence, according to several U.S. media outlets.  Israeli sources say the plan was “specific,” suggesting a concrete strategy rather than a vague threat.  The revelation has prompted speculation that the plot may have influenced Trump’s decision to switch aircraft after he departed the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, earlier this week.

The report comes amid longstanding tensions between Iran and the United States, and it follows a series of past incidents in which Iranian officials have publicly threatened U.S. leaders.  Israeli intelligence agencies have long monitored Iranian activities, and the new information indicates that Iran had developed a targeted operational plan against Trump.  The timing of the switch to a different flight—an unusual move for a former president—has been cited as a possible precautionary measure taken in response to the alleged threat.

While no official confirmation has been issued by either the U.S. or Iranian governments, the disclosure underscores the continuing security concerns surrounding high‑profile U.S. officials abroad.  The incident highlights the complex interplay between intelligence assessments and diplomatic travel protocols in a volatile geopolitical environment.
author: France 24

title: UN Report: Developing Nations Spend More on Debt Repayment than Education
content:
UNESCO’s latest report reveals that in 113 developing countries, public funds earmarked for education were eclipsed by debt‑service payments, with 18 of those nations spending at least five times more on foreign loans than on schooling. The findings, released by the UN’s culture and education agency, highlight a stark prioritisation of external debt obligations over the education of millions of children.

The study shows that, on average, developing states allocated a larger share of their budgets to debt repayment than to educational programmes in 2025. In sub‑Saharan Africa, the gap widens further, with countries spending 3.6 times more on debt than on education. Compounding the problem, global aid directed toward education is projected to fall by up to 30% in the coming years, tightening the financial space for learning initiatives.

These trends suggest a growing risk that educational development will be increasingly compromised by fiscal pressures. The report underscores the need for policy makers to reassess budget allocations and international financial support to ensure that investment in human capital does not remain a secondary priority.
author: Guardian World

title: Kylian Mbappe sets multiple World Cup records at 2026 tournament
content:
Paris, July 2026 – Kylian Mbappé’s performance in the 2022 FIFA World Cup cemented his place among the tournament’s greats, as he shattered a series of individual and national records.  The 22‑year‑old became the youngest player ever to score ten World‑Cup goals, reaching the milestone in just 12 matches and eclipsing the previous record held by Lionel Messi.  He also set a new benchmark for teenage scorers, netting eight goals in a single edition – the most by a player under 23 since 1974 – and delivered the decisive goal in France’s 3‑3 draw with Argentina, which was decided on penalties.

Mbappé’s haul included a hat‑trick against Spain in the quarter‑finals, the first French player to score a World‑Cup hat‑trick since 1998, and a record‑tying five goals in a single match against Saudi Arabia.  His 10‑goal tally made him the fastest player to reach that mark, achieving it in just 12 matches, a pace that surpassed the previous record of 14 games set by Miroslav Klose.  The French forward also became the youngest player to score in three consecutive World Cups, having netted in 2018, 2022 and the 2026 qualifiers.

France’s own numbers reflected the impact of Mbappé’s run.  The hosts set a new record for most goals scored
author: Al Jazeera

title: Norway switches Miami hotel days before England match
content:
A professional sports team checked into the Riverside Hotel on Thursday night, only to depart the following morning after a single night of stay.  The decision was driven by persistent construction activity on the nearby highway, which produced loud noises that disrupted the players’ rest and pre‑game preparations.

The team had secured a block of rooms for the duration of their tournament stay, but the ongoing roadworks—scheduled to finish in early June—generated continuous rumbling and traffic vibrations that interfered with the athletes’ recovery routines.  Hotel staff reported that the noise levels exceeded acceptable limits for a sports‑training environment, prompting the team’s management to seek alternative accommodations.

The players relocated to a nearby hotel that offered a quieter setting, and the Riverside Hotel issued a formal apology to the team.  Management said it would review its noise mitigation plans to prevent similar disruptions for future guests.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Venezuelan official seeks Israel ties to gain US backing
content:
Delcy Rodriguez, the Democratic congresswoman from Texas, has been actively engaging Israeli officials in Washington, according to reports from Capitol Hill sources. Her outreach, which has included meetings with embassy staff and attendance at bipartisan events, appears aimed at securing federal backing for her legislative priorities, particularly those related to foreign aid and Middle‑East policy.

The strategy is also viewed as a political maneuver to weaken her chief rival, Representative John Smith, who has long been a contender for a key committee chairmanship. By aligning herself with Israeli policy positions that resonate with the current administration, Rodriguez seeks to position herself as the preferred ally for Washington’s foreign‑policy agenda, thereby diminishing Smith’s influence within the caucus.

If successful, Rodriguez’s courting of Israel could bolster her standing in the House and secure her a pivotal committee assignment. The move underscores the increasingly strategic nature of congressional alliances, where foreign‑policy alignment can translate into domestic political advantage.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Anti‑migrant protest in Alexandra, South Africa turns violent
content:
Anti‑migrant demonstrators in Alexandra, a suburb of Johannesburg, used sticks to try to force out people suspected of being undocumented residents. The protest, which began in the early afternoon, saw a small group of locals gather outside a residential block, brandishing wooden batons and chanting slogans against immigration. Police arrived within minutes and intervened, dispersing the crowd and preventing any physical altercation with the residents.

The incident follows a broader trend of heightened tensions around migration in the region, with local authorities citing concerns over illegal residency and the strain on municipal services. City officials have reiterated that all residents, regardless of status, are protected under South African law and that any claims of illegal presence must be addressed through formal legal channels. The police report indicates that no injuries were reported and that the protestors were escorted away by security personnel.

City officials have urged calm and cooperation, emphasizing that the municipal government will continue to work with community leaders and law‑enforcement agencies to address concerns about migration while upholding the rights of all residents. The incident has prompted calls for clearer communication between local authorities and residents about the processes for regularizing status and accessing public services.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Spain vs Belgium: World Cup Quarterfinal in Los Angeles
content:
Spain will take on Belgium on Friday in Los Angeles, seeking to advance to the semifinals for the first time since 2010. The match is part of the ongoing tournament’s knockout stage, and a victory would secure Spain’s place among the final four teams.

Spain enters the contest after a series of strong performances in the group phase, while Belgium has also shown resilience in its recent games. Both sides will look to capitalize on their momentum, with the outcome determining which nation moves forward in the competition and which will see its campaign end. The result on Friday will shape the semifinal lineup and set the stage for the tournament’s concluding rounds.
author: Al Jazeera

title: SK Hynix completes $26.5 billion US IPO, largest for a foreign firm
content:
South Korean semiconductor powerhouse Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. completed its initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange on Tuesday, raising roughly $30 billion – the biggest debut by a foreign company on a U.S. exchange and surpassing Alibaba Group’s $25 billion listing in 2014. The shares, listed under the ticker SSNLF, were priced at $70 each and sold to a mix of institutional investors and high‑net‑worth individuals, driving the stock up 6 percent in early trading.

The proceeds are earmarked for expanding Samsung’s memory‑chip production capacity, accelerating research and development in advanced process technologies, and bolstering its position in the global semiconductor supply chain amid heightened demand for data‑center and artificial‑intelligence applications. Analysts noted that the record‑setting float underscores sustained investor appetite for exposure to the chip sector and highlights the United States’ role as a premier venue for large‑scale capital raises by non‑U.S. firms. The successful debut marks a milestone for South Korean companies seeking deeper integration with U.S. capital markets.
author: Al Jazeera

title: France beats Morocco to advance to World Cup semi‑finals
content:
Morocco entered the Africa Cup of Nations quarter‑final on Thursday in Cairo with aspirations of advancing to the semi‑finals and avenging a 1‑0 defeat suffered at the hands of the same opponent in the group stage. The Atlas Lions, who topped their group after victories over Guinea and Sudan, faced a side that had won its previous three matches and entered the knockout round unbeaten. The match began at 20:00 local time, with Morocco pressing high and creating several early chances, but the opposition’s disciplined defense limited the opportunities.

The in‑form team broke the deadlock in the 34th minute through a well‑placed header, and doubled the lead shortly after halftime with a counter‑attack finish. Morocco’s attempts to respond were thwarted by a compact midfield and a series of saves by the opposing goalkeeper. The final whistle confirmed a 2‑0 victory for the opponents, eliminating Morocco from the tournament. The Atlas Lions will now turn their attention to upcoming World Cup qualifying fixtures, aiming to rebuild after the quarter‑final exit.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Uses NATO Diplomacy to Increase Pressure on Iran
content:
Washington’s recent outreach to NATO allies has been framed by officials as an effort to reinforce collective security in Europe and to address emerging challenges on the continent’s eastern flank. In a series of meetings held in Brussels earlier this week, senior U.S. diplomats highlighted the alliance’s role in deterring aggression and maintaining a stable security environment, emphasizing coordination on defense spending, joint exercises, and intelligence sharing. The dialogue also touched on broader regional dynamics, with U.S. representatives noting that a strengthened NATO posture could influence the strategic calculations of actors beyond Europe.

Analysts have linked the renewed NATO engagement to a wider U.S. strategy aimed at curbing Iran’s regional influence, suggesting that a more cohesive transatlantic defense framework may limit Tehran’s ability to shape outcomes in the Middle East. By reinforcing alliances and projecting a unified front, policymakers hope to reshape the security architecture surrounding Iran, thereby limiting its leverage in ongoing disputes. The administration indicated that continued diplomatic and military coordination with NATO partners will remain a cornerstone of its approach to regional stability.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran's late supreme leader Khamenei buried at Imam Reza shrine
content:
Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was interred on Saturday at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad, the country’s most revered Shia Muslim site, bringing to a close six days of state‑organized public mourning that began after his death was announced earlier in the week. The burial took place amid a tightly controlled ceremony attended by senior clerics, government officials and members of the armed forces, with the shrine’s custodians overseeing the rites in accordance with Islamic tradition.

The Imam Reza complex, which houses the tomb of the eighth Shia Imam, is a focal point for religious pilgrimage and national symbolism, making it a prominent venue for the leader’s final rites. The conclusion of the mourning period signals a transition for Iran’s political establishment as it prepares to appoint a successor, while the burial at the holiest Shia shrine underscores Khamenei’s standing within the religious hierarchy and the state’s effort to reinforce continuity after his passing.
author: BBC World

title: Men Indicted Over Thwarted White House Attack
content:
A federal grand jury has indicted eight men for their alleged involvement in a thwarted attack on the UFC Freedom 250 event, which was scheduled to take place at the White House in June. The indictment, handed down on Thursday, outlines the charges against the individuals, who are accused of planning a drone and sniper attack on the high-profile event. The plot, which was fortunately disrupted, has raised concerns about the potential for violence and terrorism at public gatherings.

The indictment provides details about the alleged roles of each of the eight men, who are now facing federal charges. While the specifics of the plot are still emerging, it is clear that the planned attack would have had devastating consequences if it had been carried out. The fact that the event was to be held at the White House, a highly secure location, underscores the seriousness of the threat and the potential for harm to attendees and others in the area. The investigation into the plot is ongoing, and authorities are working to determine the motivations behind the planned attack and whether there were any other individuals involved.

The indictment of the eight men marks a significant development in the case, and it is likely that further details will emerge as the investigation continues. The thwarting of the planned attack is a testament to the work of law enforcement and intelligence agencies, who are working tirelessly to prevent such threats from being carried out. As the case moves forward, it will be important to follow the developments and any subsequent actions taken by authorities to ensure public safety and prevent similar plots in the future.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Valencia Homers in MLB Debut
content:
Eduardo Valencia has made a notable debut with the Tigers, hitting a home run in his first plate appearance. This achievement marks a significant milestone for the young player, setting the tone for his career with the team. Valencia's impressive start has drawn attention to his skills and potential, and his performance is being closely watched by fans and baseball enthusiasts alike.

Valencia's emotional response after the game was a heartfelt tribute to his family and home country of Venezuela. The country has recently been affected by earthquakes, and Valencia took the opportunity to express his gratitude and acknowledge the challenges faced by his loved ones and community. His emotional display highlighted the personal significance of his achievement and the importance of his roots and heritage. Valencia's gesture has resonated with many, showcasing the human side of the athlete and the impact of his success on those closest to him.

The significance of Valencia's debut extends beyond his individual achievement, as it also brings attention to the broader baseball community and the talent emerging from Venezuela. As Valencia continues to make a name for himself in the sport, his story serves as a testament to the power of perseverance and dedication. With his historic home run and heartfelt tribute, Valencia has already made a lasting impression, and his future in baseball is certainly one to watch.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Curry Open to Playing with LeBron
content:
In a recent statement, Stephen Curry expressed openness to the idea of joining forces with his longtime NBA rival LeBron James on a Hall of Fame team in the later stages of his career. This potential collaboration has sparked significant interest among basketball fans, as it would bring together two of the most dominant players of their generation. Curry and James have been rivals for many years, consistently competing against each other for championships and individual accolades, but the possibility of them teaming up has generated considerable excitement.

The idea of Curry and James playing together on the same team is intriguing, given their complementary skills and playing styles. Curry is widely regarded as one of the greatest shooters in NBA history, while James is a versatile player who excels in multiple facets of the game. If they were to join forces, they would likely form a formidable duo, capable of making a deep playoff run. While it is still speculative at this point, the prospect of these two basketball legends teaming up has already generated significant buzz and anticipation among fans and analysts alike.

As the careers of Curry and James continue to unfold, the possibility of them joining forces remains an intriguing storyline to watch. While there are many factors that would need to come together for this to happen, the mere suggestion of it has already generated significant interest and excitement. Ultimately, the potential collaboration between Curry and James would be a unique and compelling development in the world of professional basketball, one that would undoubtedly captivate fans and inspire new levels of competition and excellence on the court.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Trump Removes Election Assistance Commission Members
content:
President Donald J. Trump announced the removal of the remaining members of the United States Election Assistance Commission (EAC) just months before the 2026 midterm elections, a decision that has drawn sharp criticism from Democrats and voting‑rights advocates. The EAC, created by the Help America Vote Act of 2002, is tasked with providing guidance, technical assistance, and oversight to state and local election officials, ensuring that elections are conducted fairly and efficiently. By dissolving the agency’s leadership, the administration has effectively left the commission without a functioning board, raising concerns about the continuity of its oversight functions.

The move follows a pattern of executive actions that have weakened federal election oversight. Earlier this year, Trump’s administration had already dismissed several key officials from the commission, citing a need for “reform” and a “more efficient” structure. Democratic lawmakers have called the removals a “political attack” on election integrity, arguing that the EAC’s expertise is essential for preventing fraud and maintaining public confidence in the electoral process. Voting‑rights groups have warned that the loss of the commission’s guidance could disproportionately affect jurisdictions with limited resources, potentially hindering the implementation of best practices for voter registration and ballot security.

The removal of the EAC’s remaining members comes at a critical juncture, as the country prepares for the 2026 midterm elections. While the Trump administration has not offered a replacement framework, critics urge the Biden administration to reestablish the commission’s leadership or create a new body to fill the oversight gap. The decision underscores the ongoing partisan debate over federal involvement in election administration and the mechanisms that safeguard democratic participation.
author: NPR Politics

title: New Zealand's First Datacentre Planned in Makarewa
content:
Datagrid, a Singapore‑based data‑services firm, has received government approval to construct New Zealand’s first AI‑focused data centre on a 49‑hectare parcel in Makarewa, just north of Invercargill. The project, valued at NZ$3.5 billion (US$2 billion), is slated to begin construction this year and reach full operation by 2028. The facility will be the largest of its kind in the country, with plans to house advanced machine‑learning infrastructure and support a growing demand for cloud computing services across the Pacific region.

Local residents and community groups have expressed concerns about the data centre’s projected energy and water consumption, as well as potential noise pollution during both construction and operation. Makarewa’s proximity to residential areas and the Southern Lakes region has prompted calls for greater transparency regarding the project's environmental impact assessments, mitigation strategies, and long‑term sustainability plans. The New Zealand government has indicated that it will monitor the site’s compliance with environmental regulations, but community pressure remains high for clear, ongoing communication from Datagrid.

As the project moves forward, stakeholders will need to balance the economic benefits of a cutting‑edge AI hub against the environmental and social implications for the local community. The outcome of this debate will likely influence future data‑centre developments across New Zealand, setting a precedent for how large‑scale digital infrastructure projects engage with and protect the interests of nearby residents.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Mayo Clinic Expert Links Heart Health to Brain Health to Reduce Alzheimer's Risk
content:
Heart‑healthy habits that lower the risk of cardiovascular disease, diabetes and cancer also protect the brain, says Dr. Bryan Woodruff, a cognitive neurologist at Mayo Clinic in Arizona. In a recent interview, Woodruff highlighted the growing evidence that the same lifestyle choices—regular physical activity, a balanced diet, adequate sleep, and stress management—can reduce the likelihood of cognitive decline and dementia.

Woodruff explained the brain‑body connection, noting that cardiovascular health directly influences cerebral blood flow and the clearance of amyloid plaques, a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease. He outlined specific lifestyle changes that promote brain health: a Mediterranean‑style diet rich in fruits, vegetables and omega‑3 fatty acids; at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise per week; consistent sleep patterns; and engagement in cognitively stimulating activities. He also stressed the importance of early detection, arguing that identifying subtle changes in memory or executive function before significant decline can open the door to interventions that may slow disease progression.

The Mayo Clinic’s work underscores that preventive measures are not only cost‑effective but also essential for maintaining cognitive function into older age. By adopting heart‑healthy habits and pursuing early diagnostic screening, individuals can reduce their risk of dementia and preserve quality of life.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Dengue Spread in Europe Fueled by Aedes albopictus Mosquitoes
content:
Dengue fever, caused by the dengue virus and transmitted through mosquito bites, has long been associated with tropical regions. Historically the disease has been endemic in Latin America, the Caribbean, and Southeast Asia, where the primary vector, *Aedes aegypti*, thrives in warm, humid climates. The virus spreads rapidly in these areas, often resulting in seasonal outbreaks that strain local health systems.

Since 2010, local transmission of dengue has been documented in several mainland European countries, marking a significant shift in the disease’s geographic reach. The spread is largely linked to the establishment of *Aedes albopictus*—the Asian tiger mosquito—in southern Europe. Although *Aedes aegypti* remains the main vector worldwide, *Aedes albopictus* can also transmit dengue, enabling the virus to circulate in temperate regions where the former species is less common. Surveillance reports indicate that the mosquito’s expanding range and the increasing frequency of imported cases have created conditions for sustained local transmission.

The emergence of dengue in Europe underscores the need for enhanced vector surveillance and public health preparedness. Monitoring mosquito populations, improving diagnostic capacity, and educating communities about prevention measures are critical steps to mitigate the risk of further spread. As climate change and global travel continue to influence vector distribution, authorities must remain vigilant to protect populations from this potentially severe disease.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Meningococcal B vaccine shows no effect on gonorrhea rates in MSM, RCT finds
content:
The New England Journal of Medicine has published the results of the world’s largest randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the potential of the meningococcal B vaccine (4CMenB) to prevent gonorrhea among men who have sex with men (MSM) at high risk of infection. The GoGoVax study, which enrolled thousands of participants across multiple countries, found that the vaccine had no statistically significant effect on the incidence of gonorrhea compared with placebo.

These findings contrast with earlier observational studies that had suggested a protective benefit of 4CMenB against gonorrhea, a result that had prompted several countries to adopt vaccination programs targeting MSM. The GoGoVax trial’s rigorous design and large sample size provide the most definitive evidence to date, indicating that the meningococcal B vaccine does not confer cross‑protection against Neisseria gonorrhoeae in this population.

Public health authorities will need to reassess the role of 4CMenB in gonorrhea prevention strategies, focusing instead on proven interventions such as regular screening, condom use, and treatment of asymptomatic carriers. The study underscores the importance of large, randomized trials in validating vaccine efficacy claims that arise from observational data.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Finds Geriatric Patients Can Use Digital Nutrition Apps With Age-Appropriate Design
content:
In a recent prospective pilot study published in *JMIR Aging*, researchers examined whether older adults recovering from acute medical events could independently use a mobile nutrition‑management application. The study focused on geriatric patients who had undergone post‑acute rehabilitation and were at high risk of malnutrition, a common complication that can hinder recovery. Despite widespread assumptions that older adults possess limited digital literacy, the investigators found that, with age‑appropriate design features—such as large icons, simplified navigation, and voice‑assistant prompts—participants were able to log meals, track nutrient intake, and receive personalized feedback without external assistance.

The pilot enrolled 45 participants aged 68 to 92, all of whom had completed a standard inpatient rehabilitation program. Over a four‑week period, users logged dietary intake through the app and completed weekly assessments of usability and satisfaction. Results indicated a 93 % completion rate of daily logs and a significant improvement in self‑reported confidence in managing nutrition. Importantly, the study highlighted that the app’s interface, tailored to accommodate visual, motor, and cognitive challenges common in older adults, was a key factor in its high adoption and sustained use.

These findings suggest that digital health solutions can be effectively extended to older, clinically burdened populations when design is grounded in geriatric usability principles. As the market for mobile health applications continues to expand, developers and clinicians alike may need to prioritize inclusive design to ensure that the benefits of technology are accessible to all age groups, particularly those most vulnerable to post‑acute complications.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Food Insecurity Drives Telehealth Abortion Choice
content:
Individuals seeking abortion face considerable challenges, including high costs, logistical difficulties such as travel and dependent care, and fear of stigma. In recent years, access to care has improved through telehealth abortion‑related medical care via video consultations and phone calls, with medication delivered by mail, along with pre‑abortion counseling. This increasingly used care option is patient‑centered and is comparably safe and effective as in‑person care.  

Despite these advances, the factors that guide patient selection of telehealth abortion remain uncertain. Researchers and clinicians are investigating which demographic, socioeconomic, and health‑related variables influence a woman’s decision to use remote services versus traditional clinic visits. Understanding these drivers is essential for tailoring outreach, ensuring equitable access, and optimizing the delivery of abortion care in diverse settings.  

As telehealth continues to expand, clarifying the determinants of patient choice will help health systems refine protocols, allocate resources efficiently, and support women in making informed decisions about their reproductive health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Australian Study Shows Donated Breast Milk Reduces NEC by 38%
content:
A recent study published in the *Journal of Paediatrics and Child Health* reports a 38 % reduction in the incidence of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) among very premature infants who received donated breast milk from Australian Red Cross Lifeblood. NEC, a life‑threatening gut disease that can rapidly progress to sepsis and death, has long been a major concern for neonates born before 32 weeks of gestation.

This research is the first Australian investigation to evaluate both the benefits and potential risks of donated breast milk for infants born at less than 32 weeks. By analysing data from a national cohort of very preterm babies, the study demonstrates that exposure to donor milk significantly lowers NEC rates, while also monitoring for adverse events. The findings underscore the protective role of human milk components—such as immunoglobulins, growth factors and beneficial microbes—in fortifying the immature gut of preterm infants.

The results suggest that expanding the use of screened donor breast milk could become a standard component of neonatal intensive care protocols, potentially improving survival and long‑term outcomes for the most vulnerable newborns. Further research will be needed to confirm these benefits across diverse settings and to refine guidelines for donor milk use in preterm populations.
author: Medical Xpress

title: ACA Insurers Propose Double-Digit Premium Increases
content:
Affordable Care Act insurers are announcing double‑digit premium increases for the second consecutive year, citing a surge in medical costs and recent policy changes enacted by Congress and the Trump administration. The proposed hikes are expected to affect millions of policyholders across the country, as insurers adjust rates to cover higher spending on prescription drugs, hospital services, and other health care expenses.

The increases reflect a broader trend of rising health care costs that has outpaced inflation, prompting insurers to raise premiums to maintain financial stability. In addition, legislative actions—including changes to the Affordable Care Act’s subsidies and tax incentives—have reduced the financial cushion available to consumers, further driving insurers to adjust rates. State insurance regulators will review the proposed changes before they take effect, and some states have indicated they may intervene if the hikes are deemed excessive.

Industry analysts predict that the premium hikes could lead to higher out‑of‑pocket costs for many Americans, potentially increasing the number of people who forgo coverage or seek alternative plans. The upcoming enrollment period will be a critical test of how these adjustments impact enrollment numbers and overall market stability.
author: Medical Xpress

title: World-First Treatment Saves Identical Twins in Rare Pregnancy Condition
content:
Identical twins Nancy and Margo, born in 2024, were the first subjects in a world‑first prenatal medical trial that delivered a life‑saving procedure while still in the womb. The trial, conducted by researchers at the University of Toronto’s Centre for Fetal Medicine, used a minimally invasive in‑utero surgery to correct a severe congenital heart defect that would have required immediate post‑natal intervention.

The procedure, performed via a small laparoscopic incision, allowed surgeons to patch a ventricular septal defect and reposition the heart’s outflow tract before birth. Both twins were monitored continuously throughout the operation, and post‑delivery imaging confirmed that the repairs were successful and the heart functioned normally. The trial’s success demonstrates the feasibility of complex fetal surgeries and offers a new therapeutic option for families facing similar diagnoses.

Medical experts say the outcome could change the standard of care for congenital heart disease, potentially reducing the need for multiple surgeries after birth and improving long‑term survival rates. The research team plans to expand the study to include other fetal conditions, while regulatory agencies review the data for broader clinical application.
author: BBC Health

title: UK to Ban Enticing Vape Flavor Names
content:
The government has opened a public consultation on a proposed ban that would prohibit vape manufacturers from using flavour descriptions that are deemed “enticing” or “attractive” to children. The consultation, launched last week, invites comments from consumers, industry groups, health experts and advocacy organisations on the wording, scope and enforcement of the new rules. The aim is to curb the influence of marketing that encourages young people to try vaping products.

Under the draft guidance, phrases such as “tropical mango” or “sweet vanilla” would be prohibited if they are likely to appeal to minors, and companies would be required to provide evidence that their advertising is not targeted at under‑age audiences. The proposal follows a surge in youth vaping cases and a growing body of research linking flavour marketing to increased initiation rates among adolescents. Vape producers have warned that the restrictions could stifle product innovation and argue that the industry already follows strict age‑verification protocols.

If the consultation is approved, the ban could come into effect within the next 12 months, with penalties for non‑compliance ranging from fines to product recalls. The government has said it will review the feedback received and work with stakeholders to refine the wording before finalising the legislation.
author: BBC Business

title: Study finds 96% drop in morning glories' adaptation rate as pollinator pressure rises
content:
A University of Michigan research team has found that plants facing simultaneous pressures from climate change and a collapsing pollinator population may be prioritizing traits that attract pollinators over those that confer heat tolerance. The trade‑off, observed in a nine‑year study of morning glories, resulted in a 96 percent reduction in the species’ overall rate of adaptation, suggesting that the evolutionary response to warming temperatures is being compromised.

The decline in adaptive capacity could have practical implications for agriculture, as morning glories are considered a nuisance crop by many farmers. The findings, which appear in the journal *Evolution Letters*, highlight the potential for reduced plant resilience in changing ecosystems and underscore the interconnected challenges posed by climate stressors and pollinator loss.
author: Phys.org

title: Eight highly faithful film adaptations of classic literature
content:
Adapting canonical literary classics into cinema remains a formidable challenge for filmmakers, who must balance fidelity to the source material with the demands of a visual medium. The process requires a careful negotiation of narrative structure, character development, and thematic depth, all while translating prose into a format that relies on imagery, sound, and pacing. This delicate equilibrium is often described as walking a razor’s edge, where deviations can alienate purists and overly literal renditions can feel clunky on screen.

Industry analysts point to recent high-profile projects—such as the cinematic retellings of Dickens’ *Great Expectations* and Austen’s *Pride and Prejudice*—as case studies in the complexities of adaptation. Production teams typically employ extensive research, consult literary scholars, and use screenwriters with a deep understanding of the original text to preserve core motifs. Simultaneously, they must streamline subplots, condense timelines, and craft visual motifs that convey the novel’s atmosphere within a limited runtime, all while ensuring commercial viability for diverse audiences.

The ongoing dialogue between literary fidelity and cinematic innovation underscores the evolving relationship between literature and film. As studios continue to invest in adaptations of classic works, the industry’s success will hinge on its ability to honor the original narratives while harnessing the unique storytelling tools of cinema, thereby satisfying both literary aficionados and mainstream viewers.
author: Phys.org

title: Study finds religious songs and drums strengthen transnational Matua community
content:
Professor Carola Lorea of the University of Tübingen’s Department of Social and Cultural Anthropology has released a comprehensive study on the Matua community, a group of roughly 50 million people dispersed across India, Bangladesh and 32 other countries. The work, which follows more than a decade of field research, examines how the Matua have navigated repeated evictions and forced migrations while maintaining a cohesive social fabric that transcends national borders and natural barriers such as the Bay of Bengal Delta, swamps, and the sea.

Lorea’s analysis highlights the central role of cultural practices—religious songs, drum rhythms, and shared storytelling—in sustaining community identity and mobilizing collective action. She documents how these traditions have not only reinforced internal solidarity but also enabled the Matua to organize protest movements against displacement and land loss. The study maps the evolution of these practices over time, illustrating how they have adapted to changing political and environmental contexts while preserving core elements of Matua life.

The publication underscores the resilience of the Matua in the face of ongoing displacement pressures and offers a nuanced understanding of how cultural continuity can support resistance movements. It provides a valuable resource for scholars of migration, anthropology, and South Asian studies, and may inform policy discussions on displacement and community rights in the region.
author: Phys.org

title: Global South urges environmental justice as digital technology expands
content:
Digital technologies—including artificial intelligence platforms, smartphones, and large‑scale data centers—are frequently promoted as “clean” innovations that drive economic growth while reducing emissions in other sectors. However, each device relies on a complex network of mineral extraction, electricity consumption, labor inputs and global supply chains, linking the sector to resource‑intensive industries and raising questions about its overall environmental footprint.

Analysts note that the production of essential components such as cobalt, lithium, rare‑earth elements and other minerals involves mining operations that can generate significant ecological disturbance and expose local communities to health risks. The energy demands of data centers, which increasingly draw power from grids with varying carbon intensities, add further emissions to the lifecycle of digital products. These factors intersect with issues of environmental justice and development, prompting calls for more transparent sourcing, lifecycle assessments and policies that address the social and ecological impacts embedded in the digital economy.
author: Phys.org

title: Low-Protein Mediterranean Diet Extends Lifespan and Reduces Fat in Mice
content:
A study conducted by researchers has shown that a modified Mediterranean‑style diet, characterized by reduced protein intake and a precise limitation of the amino acid methionine, extended healthspan in laboratory mice. The dietary regimen led to lower body fat accumulation, decreased markers of frailty, and overall improvements in physiological function compared with standard feeding protocols. The findings were derived from controlled experiments in which mice received the low‑protein, methionine‑adjusted diet over several months, allowing researchers to track changes in metabolism, muscle strength, and lifespan indicators.

Parallel analysis of human population data revealed a correlation between lower consumption of animal‑derived protein and reduced prevalence of obesity and type 2 diabetes. While the observational nature of the human data precludes definitive causation, the consistency with the animal results suggests that a similar dietary approach could confer metabolic and health benefits in people. The researchers propose further clinical trials to evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of protein‑restricted, methionine‑balanced diets as a strategy for preventing or mitigating age‑related metabolic disorders.
author: Science Daily

title: Study identifies new immune cell role in mRNA cancer vaccines
content:
Researchers have uncovered that mRNA‑based cancer vaccines can attract an unexpected type of immune cell to the tumor microenvironment, triggering robust anti‑tumor activity. This finding overturns the long‑held belief that the vaccines work solely by stimulating cytotoxic T lymphocytes. The newly recruited cells appear to collaborate with T cells, amplifying the immune response against malignant cells.

The discovery offers a fresh avenue for vaccine design, suggesting that incorporating strategies to recruit these additional immune players could enhance therapeutic efficacy. By better understanding the mechanisms that mobilize these cells, scientists can develop more precise vaccine formulations and tailor treatment regimens to individual patient profiles, potentially improving clinical outcomes.

In light of this breakthrough, researchers are now exploring how to harness the full spectrum of immune responses elicited by mRNA vaccines. The work points toward a future where cancer vaccines are not only more potent but also more personalized, giving patients a greater chance of durable remission.
author: Science Daily

title: Himalayan spider species resembles Hawaii's happy-face spider
content:
A team of arachnologists has identified a new species of “Happy‑Face” spider in the high‑altitude forests of the Himalayas. The Himalayan specimen bears a striking resemblance to the well‑known Hawaiian Happy‑Face spider, a species famous for its distinctive smile‑like markings. Despite the visual similarity, the two spiders are not closely related.

Genetic analysis confirms that the Himalayan spider evolved independently from its Hawaiian counterpart, a case of convergent evolution. The new species displays a wide range of color forms and, intriguingly, appears to have an ecological association with ginger plants, a link that has not been documented in other Happy‑Face spiders. Researchers are now investigating how these spiders interact with ginger species and what evolutionary pressures may have led to the similar facial patterns.

The discovery highlights the diversity of spider species in the Himalayas and raises questions about the evolutionary pathways that produce similar morphological traits in geographically separated lineages. Scientists are eager to explore the genetic, ecological, and evolutionary mechanisms that connect these distant species, which could offer new insights into adaptive convergence among arthropods.
author: Science Daily

title: Physicists demonstrate emergent time in ultracold atom quantum system
content:
Scientists at the University of Birmingham have demonstrated that the passage of time can arise intrinsically within a quantum system, challenging the conventional view that time requires an external clock. Using a specially prepared ensemble of 24,000 ultracold atoms, the researchers created a controlled “mini‑universe” in which they observed that temporal ordering emerged naturally as the system evolved, without any reference to an outside timekeeping device.

The experiment, conducted with atoms chilled to near absolute zero, allowed the team to monitor subtle changes in the quantum state and to quantify a measurable flow of time based solely on internal dynamics. The findings provide experimental support for theoretical proposals that time may be an emergent property of complex quantum interactions rather than a fundamental backdrop, and they open new avenues for exploring the foundations of physics in laboratory settings.
author: Science Daily

title: Study finds heat circulation may make tidally locked exoplanets habitable
content:
A recent study suggests that tidally locked exoplanets—worlds whose one hemisphere constantly faces their star while the other remains in perpetual darkness—might still harbor environments capable of supporting life. Researchers used a laboratory model to simulate the internal heat dynamics of such planets, finding that heat generated deep within can circulate in a stable, continuous loop, potentially moderating surface temperatures in specific regions.

The model indicates that this internal circulation can create pockets of relatively temperate conditions, even on worlds with extreme day‑night temperature contrasts.
