By redistributing heat from the scorching day side to the frozen night side, the planet’s interior may maintain a more balanced climate than previously assumed, offering a plausible niche for life to develop or persist.

These findings challenge the prevailing view that tidally locked exoplanets are largely inhospitable. If internal heat circulation can indeed create habitable zones, future observational missions may need to reconsider the potential for life on such extreme worlds.
author: Science Daily

title: NISAR satellite detects ground displacement in La Guaira after June 2026 earthquakes
content:
Radar data from the NISAR satellite indicate that La Guaira and surrounding areas suffered notable ground displacement during the June 2026 seismic events. The satellite’s interferometric measurements reveal horizontal shifts of up to 30 centimetres and vertical movements of roughly 15 centimetres, suggesting that the region’s underlying fault systems were significantly re‑activated by the tremors.

The June 2026 earthquakes, which reached magnitudes between 5.8 and 6.3, were recorded by both local seismic stations and international networks. NISAR’s high‑resolution imagery complements these observations by providing precise surface deformation maps, allowing scientists to assess the extent of crustal strain release and to refine models of the regional tectonic framework. Preliminary analyses also point to a potential redistribution of stress along the nearby fault lines, which may influence future seismic hazard assessments.

These findings underscore the value of space‑based radar for monitoring ground deformation in real time. By offering detailed, rapid assessments of fault movement, NISAR data help authorities evaluate infrastructure risk and inform emergency response strategies in vulnerable coastal communities.
author: NASA News

title: Startup creates real-time AI tutor for children aged 4‑9
content:
A startup has announced the completion of an AI‑driven tutoring platform designed for children aged four to nine, offering instruction in reading, mathematics, English as a second language and additional subjects. The developers highlighted that creating an effective educational dialogue required a redesign of the conventional tool‑use loop, leading to the construction of a custom “tutor harness” that combines a streaming interpreter for real‑time action execution with an asynchronous planner model that anticipates conversational steps and initiates learning‑focused calls. The system is also equipped with a safety layer that evaluates each interaction without disrupting the flow of the lesson, aiming to ensure that instructional decisions are made at the optimal moment rather than merely providing rapid answers.

The team described the platform as a response to the broader challenge of integrating artificial intelligence responsibly into early childhood education, emphasizing that the architecture balances responsiveness, pedagogical relevance, and safety. The announcement, posted on Hacker News, has attracted considerable attention, with the discussion thread receiving over 60 points and dozens of comments seeking technical clarification and offering critical feedback. The developers indicated openness to further input from the community as they continue to refine the tutor’s capabilities.
author: Hacker News

title: Factors driving high costs of U.S. ambulance rides
content:
A recent post on the personal blog of David Oks titled “Why American Ambulance Rides Are …” has sparked considerable discussion online, garnering 136 up‑votes and 172 comments on Hacker News. The article examines the high frequency and cost of ambulance transports in the United States, attributing the trend to a combination of insurance reimbursement structures, limited alternatives for non‑emergency patients, and regulatory frameworks that incentivize hospital admissions. Oks outlines how many rides are initiated for conditions that could be managed through urgent‑care clinics or telemedicine, yet the prevailing fee‑for‑service model rewards ambulance providers and emergency departments, leading to inflated utilization rates.

The piece also highlights regional disparities, noting that rural areas often face longer response times and fewer transport options, while urban centers experience congestion that further drives up expenses. Oks cites data from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and several health‑policy studies to illustrate that the average ambulance bill can exceed $1,200, a figure that frequently surpasses patients’ insurance coverage limits. The article concludes by suggesting policy reforms such as bundled payments, stricter triage protocols, and expanded community health resources to curb unnecessary transports and reduce the financial burden on both patients and the healthcare system.
author: Hacker News

title: Study Links Maternal Phone Use to Children Feeling Less Loved
content:
A research article identified by the DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1766665 has been published in the peer‑reviewed journal *Frontiers in Psychology*. The paper appears in the 2026 volume of the journal and is accessible through the publisher’s website. While the specific subject matter of the study is not detailed in the source information, its placement in a leading psychology outlet indicates that it contributes to scholarly discourse within the field.

The publication quickly attracted attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where a discussion thread linked to the article garnered 35 points and generated nine comments. The engagement suggests that the study resonated with a broader audience beyond academia, prompting readers to share observations and queries about its findings. The visibility on such platforms may increase the article’s reach and influence within both scientific and public domains.
author: Hacker News

title: Cloudflare blog details steps to create a custom vulnerability harness
content:
Cloudflare’s engineering team released a detailed guide titled “Build Your Own Vulnerability Harness,” outlining a framework for creating custom tools that automate the detection and exploitation of software flaws. The post walks readers through the design of a modular harness, covering aspects such as payload generation, environment isolation, and result reporting, while emphasizing best practices for safe testing and responsible disclosure. By leveraging Cloudflare’s own infrastructure and open‑source components, the guide aims to lower the barrier for security researchers and development teams seeking to integrate continuous vulnerability assessment into their workflows.

The article quickly attracted attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where it earned 23 points and generated ten comments discussing its practicality and potential applications. Commenters highlighted the usefulness of a reusable harness for both internal security programs and broader community efforts, noting the balance between thorough testing and minimizing disruption to production systems. Cloudflare’s publication reflects a growing trend among large internet service providers to share security tooling publicly, fostering collaboration and enhancing overall ecosystem resilience.
author: Hacker News

title: Ben Bernanke Joins Anthropic Oversight Trust
content:
Anthropic, the artificial‑intelligence research firm known for its focus on safety‑centric language models, announced on Tuesday that former Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke will join the company’s advisory board. The appointment, detailed in a press release on Anthropic’s website, cites Bernanke’s extensive experience in macroeconomic policy and financial regulation as a valuable asset for guiding the firm’s approach to the broader economic and societal impacts of advanced AI systems. In a brief statement, Bernanke expressed enthusiasm for contributing to “the responsible development of technologies that will shape the global economy,” while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei highlighted the need for “deep expertise in public policy and systemic risk” as AI capabilities expand.

The move comes as AI developers face increasing scrutiny from regulators and lawmakers concerning issues such as market stability, data privacy, and algorithmic bias. By adding a former central‑bank leader to its advisory roster, Anthropic aims to strengthen its engagement with policymakers and to inform its internal governance frameworks. Industry observers noted the appointment reflects a growing trend of AI firms seeking guidance from seasoned public‑sector figures to navigate the complex intersection of technology and economic policy. Anthropic indicated that Bernanke will begin contributing to board discussions later this quarter, with no immediate changes to its product roadmap disclosed.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenAI designates GPT‑5.6 as preferred model for Microsoft Copilot 365
content:
OpenAI has announced a new family of language models that will continue to underpin Microsoft’s suite of workplace and productivity applications. The updated models, which include the latest iterations of the GPT series, are designed to deliver more reliable, context‑aware responses and tighter integration with Microsoft’s cloud services.

Microsoft will embed these models across its flagship productivity tools, such as Word, Outlook, Teams, and Power Point, enhancing features like smart drafting, real‑time translation, and advanced data analysis. The partnership also extends to the Microsoft Graph API, enabling developers to build custom applications that leverage the models’ capabilities for workflow automation and knowledge management.

By extending OpenAI’s technology into Microsoft’s enterprise ecosystem, the collaboration aims to streamline daily work tasks and improve productivity for businesses worldwide. The rollout is expected to roll out in phases over the coming months, with ongoing updates to refine performance and security.
author: TechCrunch

title: Telstra CEO Vicki Brady questioned after nationwide outage
content:
Telstra’s chief executive, Vicki Brady, returned to the office after annual leave to face a flurry of questions following the company’s nationwide outage on Wednesday, which disrupted train services, payment systems and triple‑zero emergency calls. Brady denied that the failure was linked to recent job restructuring, stating that “people and processes worked as they should have.” She announced that Telstra would launch a thorough investigation into the software glitch that caused the outage and clarified that the company was not reviewing executive bonuses in light of the incident, correcting an earlier headline that had suggested otherwise.

The outage, which left thousands of Australians without access to essential services, has drawn scrutiny from regulators and the public. Telstra’s response focuses on a detailed technical review and a commitment to restoring confidence in its network reliability. As the investigation proceeds, the company aims to identify the root cause and implement measures to prevent a recurrence, while maintaining its obligations to emergency services and the broader community.
author: Guardian Technology

title: ASA says ads for rapid‑cooling portable air conditioners are misleading
content:
The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) has ruled that several advertisements claiming that small, portable cooling devices can rapidly lower room temperatures are misleading and “too good to be true.”  The ASA’s decision, issued after a review of complaints, found that the claims made by the manufacturers were not supported by evidence and that the devices’ performance was significantly lower than advertised.  The authority noted that the promotional material implied a rapid, substantial drop in ambient temperature, whereas independent tests showed only modest cooling over extended periods.

In light of the ruling, the advertisers are required to amend or withdraw the offending claims and provide clearer, evidence‑based information about the devices’ capabilities.  The ASA’s action underscores the regulator’s commitment to ensuring that consumer advertising remains accurate and not deceptive, particularly in the growing market for energy‑efficient home appliances.
author: BBC Technology

title: Dembélé scores as France reaches third straight World Cup semi‑final
content:
French striker Ousmane Dembélé capped a spirited performance for Les Bleus with a goal against Morocco on Thursday, helping France secure a vital victory in the FIFA World Cup group stage. The 2025 Ballon d’Or winner quickly shifted his focus to the next phase of the tournament, noting that the upcoming match would be his third consecutive World Cup semi‑final appearance.

Dembélé praised team captain Kylian Mbappé, who also found the net in the same game, highlighting the player’s leadership and goal‑scoring prowess. “Mbappé’s presence on the pitch is a constant source of inspiration,” Dembélé said, underscoring the duo’s importance to France’s campaign. With the semi‑final looming, the French side will look to build on their recent form and secure a place in the final.
author: France 24

title: 12 die in Almeria wildfire, victims found in cars
content:
Twelve people were killed in a wildfire that broke out near Almería in southern Spain late on Thursday, regional authorities said. The fatalities occurred in the hamlet of Bedar, with several victims discovered inside their vehicles as the flames swept through the area.

The Andalusian regional government confirmed the deaths in a statement and reported that firefighters are continuing to battle the blaze in an effort to bring it under control. Emergency services are focusing on containment while assessing the extent of the damage, and authorities have not yet released information on the cause of the fire.
author: France 24

title: Warren Zaïre-Emery emotional after debut in France's 2-0 win over Morocco
content:
French midfielder Warren Zaïre‑Emery, who entered the match from the bench for Les Bleus, was visibly emotional when speaking to reporters after France’s 2‑0 win over Morocco. The 20‑year‑old highlighted the team’s strong performance and the significance of the victory, while acknowledging that the triumph was part of a broader campaign.

Zaïre‑Emery also reflected on his own season, noting his contributions at Paris Saint‑Germain and his growing role with the national side. He emphasized that, despite the recent success, there remains considerable work ahead for both himself and the squad as they continue to pursue upcoming objectives.
author: France 24

title: Mbappé says he lost focus after missing penalty versus Morocco
content:
Kylian Mbappé scored a late goal in France’s 2‑1 victory over Morocco, but the captain was quick to point out his own shortcomings. After missing a penalty in the first half, he admitted he had lost focus and failed to convert the opportunity, a mistake he said “really bothered me.” The late strike, however, helped seal the win and prevented Morocco from taking the lead.

When reporters asked whether the current French squad could be considered the strongest side he has ever seen, Mbappé cautioned against complacency. He highlighted that France’s recent unbeaten run in the 2026 edition of the FIFA World Cup—though still in the future—should not lull the team into a sense of rest. Instead, he stressed the need for continuous improvement and vigilance if France is to maintain its competitive edge on the world stage.
author: France 24

title: US airstrikes and Iranian missile launches raise ceasefire concerns
content:
U.S. forces launched a new series of airstrikes against Iranian targets early Thursday, according to U.S. officials. The strikes were described as a response to Iranian military actions in the region and were aimed at preventing further escalation.

In retaliation, Tehran fired missiles at Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait and Jordan—countries that host U.S. troops—raising tensions in an area already under a fragile interim ceasefire designed to curb the broader Middle East conflict. The missile attacks also reportedly caused explosions near an Iranian nuclear power plant, adding a nuclear dimension to the hostilities. U.S. and allied commanders said they were monitoring the situation closely and were prepared to respond if necessary.

The exchange of fire underscores the volatility of the region and the potential for a wider conflict. Diplomatic efforts to maintain the ceasefire have been strained, and observers warn that further incidents could destabilize the fragile balance in the Gulf and surrounding areas.
author: France 24

title: UK Labour leader Andy Burnham vows to address Gaza suffering after apology
content:
Andy Burnham, the Labour Party’s deputy leader, issued a public apology on social media for the party’s initial response to the recent Israeli attacks in Gaza. In a post on his verified account, Burnham acknowledged that Labour’s early statements had been “insufficient and poorly timed,” and he expressed regret for any distress caused by the party’s stance.

The apology follows criticism that the party’s early comments were perceived as too cautious and not fully supportive of the Palestinian perspective. Burnham reiterated Labour’s commitment to a two‑state solution and called for renewed efforts to secure a ceasefire and humanitarian assistance for civilians in the region. He also pledged to review the party’s communication strategy on Middle East policy to ensure future statements better reflect the party’s values and the concerns of its constituents.

Burnham’s remarks come amid heightened tensions in Gaza and a broader debate within UK politics about the appropriate response to the conflict. By acknowledging the misstep and outlining corrective measures, the Labour Party seeks to reaffirm its position on international humanitarian issues while maintaining engagement with voters who are closely watching the unfolding situation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: World Bank and IMF Loans Shift African Policymaking
content:
African governments are increasingly re‑examining the costs and benefits of concessional financing as debt pressures mount across the continent. Concessional loans—characterised by low or zero interest rates, extended grace periods, and generous repayment terms—have long been a key tool for countries grappling with high debt‑to‑GDP ratios. However, the growing fiscal strain has prompted leaders to scrutinise whether such aid truly delivers sustainable relief or merely postpones inevitable repayments.

Recent assessments by the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank highlight that many African states rely on concessional funding to finance public services, infrastructure, and pandemic recovery. Yet the cumulative debt burden, coupled with rising global interest rates, raises concerns about future fiscal flexibility. Governments are therefore weighing options such as debt‑swap arrangements, targeted grants, and stricter eligibility criteria for concessional credit. The goal is to strike a balance between immediate liquidity needs and long‑term macro‑economic stability, ensuring that borrowed resources do not compromise future growth prospects.

In response, several African nations are engaging in multilateral dialogues to refine concessional loan frameworks, incorporating stricter monitoring and performance indicators. By recalibrating these financial instruments, policymakers aim to preserve the essential support that concessional financing offers while mitigating the risk of unsustainable debt trajectories. The outcome of these reassessments will shape the continent’s fiscal trajectory over the coming years.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Supreme Court independence questioned as threats to judges rise
content:
Law professor and former Department of Justice official Kim Wehle warned that an escalation in threats directed at judges is undermining the United States’ rule of law. Speaking at a congressional briefing on judicial independence on Tuesday, Wehle said that the frequency and intensity of harassment—ranging from online vitriol to direct physical threats—have risen sharply in recent years, creating a climate that discourages impartial adjudication and jeopardizes public confidence in the courts.

Wehle cited data from the Federal Judicial Center indicating a 40 percent increase in reported threats against federal judges since 2018, as well as high‑profile incidents in which judges have faced doxxing, death threats, and attempts to influence rulings through partisan pressure. She emphasized that such intimidation not only endangers individual jurists but also erodes the institutional safeguards that separate the judiciary from political interference. Experts and advocacy groups have called for stronger protective measures and clearer enforcement mechanisms to preserve judicial independence and maintain the integrity of the legal system.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli strike kills aid worker Mohammed al-Wahidi and three others in Gaza
content:
Israeli forces carried out a strike on the evening of Monday that killed Mohammed al‑Wahidi and three other individuals. The attack occurred in a residential area in the West Bank, according to statements from the Israeli military and local residents. Al‑Wahidi, a 34‑year‑old farmer from the town of Nablus, was identified by witnesses as a member of a local family that has lived in the area for generations.

The incident took place just hours before the Egypt versus Argentina international football match, which was scheduled to begin on Tuesday. The timing of the strike drew criticism from several human rights groups, who called for an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding the casualties. The Israeli Defense Forces have not yet released details on the target or the rationale for the operation.

The death toll adds to the mounting tensions in the region, and the international community has urged both sides to exercise restraint. As the match proceeds, authorities in both Egypt and Argentina have issued statements urging fans to remain calm and to avoid any demonstrations that could disrupt the event.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Muchova defeats Gauff to reach first Wimbledon final
content:
Karolina Muchova secured a place in the championship match after prevailing in her semifinal, setting up an all‑[nationality] final against fellow countrywoman Anastasia Noskova. The decisive victory came as Muchova dispatched her opponent in straight sets, confirming her strong form heading into the tournament’s concluding round.

Noskova earned her spot in the final by overcoming Ukrainian contender Kateryna Kostyuk in the opposite semifinal, also in straight sets. The two compatriots will now contest the title, with the upcoming final marking the culmination of a tightly contested women's draw.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic drops sharply amid renewed US-Iran fighting
content:
Brent crude futures remained largely unchanged on Tuesday, hovering near $84 per barrel, even as shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz—a chokepoint that handles roughly a third of global oil shipments—experienced a sharp decline. Data from the International Maritime Organization showed a 27% drop in vessel transits compared with the same period last year, reflecting heightened rerouting by tankers amid escalating regional tensions and recent sanctions on Iranian oil exports. Analysts noted that the reduction in traffic has not translated into immediate price pressure, as global inventories remain ample and demand forecasts for the fourth quarter are modest.

The steadiness of Brent prices underscores the market’s reliance on broader supply‑demand fundamentals rather than short‑term disruptions in a single corridor. While the dip in Hormuz traffic may prompt some shippers to seek alternative routes such as the Cape of Good Hope, the overall impact on crude supplies is expected to be limited. Traders will monitor further developments in the region, but for now the market appears to be absorbing the logistical slowdown without significant price volatility.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran claims strikes hit military sites in Bushehr and Konarak, US denies involvement
content:
Iranian state media announced that military headquarters in Iran’s Bushehr province and the coastal city of Konarak were struck by aerial attacks. The reports, issued by the official news agency, indicated that the facilities sustained damage but did not provide immediate casualty figures or details on the weapons used.

The statements came amid heightened regional security concerns, with Iranian authorities vowing to investigate the incidents and respond as necessary. No group claimed responsibility at the time of reporting, and officials urged the public to await further official updates while security forces secured the affected sites.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Zelenskyy calls for rapid start of Patriot missile production in Ukraine
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump announced his support earlier this week for Ukraine’s initiative to produce missiles domestically, marking a notable endorsement of Kyiv’s effort to expand its own defense manufacturing capabilities. The statement, released through the White House communications office, indicated that the United States will continue to cooperate with Ukrainian defense firms, providing technical assistance and facilitating the transfer of relevant technologies while respecting existing export‑control regulations.

The move comes amid ongoing U.S. military assistance to Ukraine, which has included the provision of advanced weapon systems such as HIMARS rockets and Javelin anti‑tank missiles. By backing Ukraine’s domestic production, the administration aims to bolster the country’s self‑sufficiency in armaments and sustain the flow of munitions needed for its current security challenges. Officials said the decision aligns with broader U.S. policy to support allied nations in developing indigenous defense capacities without altering the overall framework of American security aid.
author: Al Jazeera

title: SK Hynix raises $26.5 billion in US share sale, biggest foreign Nasdaq debut
content:
Shares of a foreign‑listed company are slated to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Friday, marking what analysts say will be the largest initial public offering ever by a non‑U.S. firm. The offering, which follows a multi‑year roadshow and regulatory clearance in both the United States and the company’s home jurisdiction, is expected to raise several billion dollars and bring the firm’s market capitalization into the top tier of technology listings on the exchange.

Market observers note that the debut underscores the Nasdaq’s growing appeal to overseas enterprises seeking broader investor access and liquidity. If the shares perform as projected, the transaction could set a new benchmark for cross‑border listings, prompting other multinational corporations to consider similar routes for capital raising. The trading launch on Friday will be closely watched for its impact on Nasdaq volumes and the broader perception of foreign participation in U.S. equity markets.
author: BBC World

title: Twelve killed in Almería wildfire as heatwave hits southern Europe
content:
Six people were injured after a fire broke out in the town of Los Gallardos, located in the province of Almería, Spain. Local emergency services responded promptly, extinguishing the blaze and transporting the victims to nearby medical facilities for treatment. The injured individuals, whose ages and conditions have not been disclosed, were reported to be in stable condition upon arrival at the hospitals.

Authorities from the Almería fire department and municipal officials have opened an investigation to determine the cause of the incident. No fatalities have been reported, and the affected area is being cleared for safety inspections before normal activities resume. The incident underscores the ongoing need for rapid emergency response in the region.
author: BBC World

title: Klopp Recalls Failed Liverpool Pursuit of Mbappe
content:
Liverpool Manager Jurgen Klopp Recalls Failed Attempt to Sign Kylian Mbappe

In a recent revelation, Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp has shared a unique anecdote from his past, detailing a failed attempt to sign French football sensation Kylian Mbappe for the Premier League club a decade ago. According to Klopp, he was invited to fly with Mbappe and his family on a private plane as part of the recruitment efforts. The Liverpool manager humorously described the experience, stating that he "flew around in a circle" with the Mbappe family, indicating the casual and relaxed nature of the meeting.

The failed attempt to sign Mbappe, who has since become one of the world's top players, underscores the challenges faced by Liverpool in securing high-profile transfers. At the time, Mbappe was just 16 years old and was already making waves in the football world. His subsequent transfer to Monaco and later Paris Saint-Germain has made him a highly sought-after player, with his current contract situation remaining a topic of interest among football fans and pundits.

Klopp's lighthearted account of the experience highlights the human side of high-stakes football negotiations, where even the most powerful managers can be put in unusual situations. While the failed attempt to sign Mbappe ultimately didn't materialize, it has provided an entertaining glimpse into the world of top-level football recruitment and the often-unconventional methods used to secure the best talent.
author: BBC Sport

title: France into semi-finals after comfortable win over Morocco
content:
In a convincing display of attacking prowess, France secured their spot in the World Cup semi-finals with a 2-0 victory over Morocco. The match saw Kylian Mbappe redeem himself after a penalty miss earlier in the game, scoring his eighth goal of the tournament to seal the win for his team. The French forward's impressive performance was complemented by Ousmane Dembele, who added a second goal to the scoreboard, further solidifying France's dominance on the field.

The match got off to a tense start, with Morocco putting up a strong defense against the French attack. However, it was only a matter of time before France's superior skill and experience began to tell. Mbappe's earlier penalty miss seemed like a blip on the radar, as he made up for it with a clinical finish in the second half. Dembele's goal followed shortly after, and the Moroccan defense was unable to withstand the French onslaught.

With this win, France has now moved into the semi-finals, where they will face off against either Argentina or the Netherlands. The team's coach will be looking to build on this momentum and propel his team towards a potential World Cup title. As for Morocco, they can hold their heads high after a commendable performance in the tournament, and will look to build on this experience for future competitions.
author: BBC Sport

title: Marc Guehi Injury Rears Its Head Ahead of Norway Match
content:
England's prospects in the ongoing European Under-21 Championship face a potential setback as defender Marc Guehi struggles with a slight hamstring injury. The 23-year-old, who has been a crucial component of Gareth Southgate's backline, is now at risk of missing Saturday's quarter-final match against Norway. Guehi's fitness status is being closely monitored by the England coaching staff, with a final decision on his participation expected in the coming days.

Guehi has been a key player for England in the tournament, providing solidity and experience at the heart of the defense. His absence would be a significant blow to the team's chances, particularly given the tough opposition they face in Norway. The Scandinavian side has been in impressive form, and England will need all their strength and depth to overcome them. With Guehi's injury clouding his availability, the England coaching staff will have to carefully weigh their options and make a decision that best serves the team's interests.

As England prepare to face Norway on Saturday, the focus will be on Guehi's fitness and whether he will be able to recover in time to take to the field. The team's medical staff will be working tirelessly to ensure Guehi's condition is assessed accurately, and a decision is made that prioritizes both his health and the team's chances of success in the tournament.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump’s Air Force One switcheroo highlights security concerns around Qatari model
content:
President Trump's decision to use an older Air Force One for part of his recent return trip has sparked concerns about the security of the newly refurbished and gifted plane from Qatar. The incident has led to questions about whether the advanced security features of the new aircraft were sufficient to warrant its use for presidential travel. According to sources, the White House attributed the decision to "an abundance of caution," suggesting that officials may have been erring on the side of safety.

The use of the older aircraft, which was designed to provide an additional layer of security, has raised eyebrows among experts who have questioned the logic behind the decision. The newly refurbished plane, gifted by Qatar, was intended to provide the President with the latest in advanced security features and technological advancements. However, the incident has highlighted the importance of thorough evaluation and testing of new security protocols to ensure the President's safety.

The incident has also sparked renewed scrutiny of the security measures in place for presidential travel, with some experts calling for a more transparent and thorough assessment of the risks associated with using new and untested security systems. As the debate continues, the White House remains tight-lipped about the specific reasons behind the decision, leaving many to wonder about the true extent of the security concerns surrounding the new Air Force One.
author: The Hill

title: House Republican Introduces Bill to Limit Birthright Citizenship
content:
In a move aimed at revisiting the long-standing concept of birthright citizenship, freshman House Representative John McGuire (R-Va.) has introduced the Birthright Citizenship Clarification Act. The bill seeks to codify a key aspect of President Trump's 2019 executive order, which aimed to limit birthright citizenship by challenging the "jus soli" or "right of the soil" principle. This principle, established by the 14th Amendment to the US Constitution, grants citizenship to anyone born within a nation's territory, regardless of their parents' nationality or immigration status.

The introduction of McGuire's bill comes just days after the Supreme Court declined to hear a case related to birthright citizenship, effectively allowing the existing laws to remain in place. The court's decision has been seen as a setback for those advocating for changes to the current system. McGuire's bill, however, is an attempt to revive the debate and push for a legislative solution. By codifying the executive order, the bill would effectively strip birthright citizenship from individuals born to non-citizen parents in the United States, a move that is likely to face significant opposition from immigrant advocacy groups and many Democrats.

The Birthright Citizenship Clarification Act is the latest development in a long-standing debate over the scope and application of the 14th Amendment. As the bill makes its way through Congress, it is expected to face intense scrutiny and opposition from various stakeholders. The outcome of this legislative effort will ultimately depend on the willingness of lawmakers to revisit and potentially alter a cornerstone of US citizenship law.
author: The Hill

title: Lower Dementia Risk Linked to SGLT2 Inhibitors in Seniors
content:
A recent study published in JAMA Network Open has shed light on the potential link between sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and a reduced risk of dementia in older adults with mood and psychotic disorders. The study, which analyzed data from over 17,000 patients, found that those taking SGLT2 inhibitors had a significantly lower risk of developing dementia compared to those not taking the medication.

SGLT2 inhibitors are a class of medications commonly prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes by helping the body remove excess glucose from the blood through the urine. Researchers believe that the potential neuroprotective effects of SGLT2 inhibitors may be related to their ability to reduce inflammation and oxidative stress in the brain. The study's findings suggest that SGLT2 inhibitors may have a broader therapeutic application beyond diabetes management, particularly for older adults with mood and psychotic disorders who are at increased risk of dementia.

While the study's results are promising, further research is needed to confirm the association between SGLT2 inhibitor use and dementia risk reduction. Nevertheless, the findings have significant implications for the potential use of SGLT2 inhibitors in the prevention and treatment of dementia, and highlight the need for further investigation into the medication's neuroprotective effects.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Hip Fractures Linked to Collagen Fiber Orientation, Not Just Bone Density
content:
Scientists at the Paul Scherrer Institute PSI have made a groundbreaking discovery regarding the causes of femoral neck fractures. While low bone density is often cited as a primary factor, researchers have found that the nanostructure of bone tissue also plays a crucial role. Specifically, the orientation of collagen fibers, which are the building blocks of bones, has been identified as a significant contributor to the risk of fractures.

Using a novel X-ray technique, the scientists were able to examine the internal structure of bone tissue at the nanoscale. This allowed them to observe the orientation of collagen fibers and its impact on bone strength. The research revealed that the orientation of these fibers can affect the way stress is distributed within the bone, making it more susceptible to fractures. This finding challenges the long-held assumption that femoral neck fractures are solely the result of insufficient bone density.

The discovery has significant implications for the prevention and treatment of femoral neck fractures. By understanding the role of collagen fiber orientation in bone strength, researchers may be able to develop new strategies for preventing fractures and improving bone health. This could involve the development of new treatments or therapies that target the nanostructure of bone tissue, rather than just focusing on increasing bone density.
author: Medical Xpress

title: US Children's Mental Health Treatment Reaches New High
content:
A recent national study conducted by researchers from Penn State College of Medicine has revealed a striking trend in mental health treatment among children and adolescents in the United States. When schools closed in the spring of 2020 at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, a significant decline was observed in the number of young individuals seeking mental health treatment. The report indicates that this number plummeted by more than half during this period.

However, the study found that by 2022, the number of children and adolescents receiving mental health treatment had not only rebounded but had actually surpassed pre-pandemic levels. This unexpected increase is a cause for concern, as it may suggest that the pandemic has had a lasting impact on the mental health of young individuals. The researchers behind the study are now urging healthcare professionals and policymakers to take note of this trend and develop strategies to address the growing mental health needs of this vulnerable population.

The findings of this study serve as a reminder of the far-reaching consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly on the mental health of children and adolescents. As the nation continues to navigate the aftermath of the pandemic, it is essential to prioritize the mental well-being of this demographic and provide them with the necessary support and resources to overcome the challenges they have faced.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Medical Errors Claim 200,000 US Lives Annually
content:
A recent report by the Johns Hopkins University estimates that medical errors claim over 250,000 lives annually in the United States, making them one of the leading causes of death in the country. This alarming statistic has prompted the non-profit organization, the World Health Organization (WHO), to launch a comprehensive initiative aimed at reducing preventable medical errors. According to the WHO, medical errors can occur due to a variety of factors, including inadequate staffing, poor communication among healthcare professionals, and outdated medical technology.

The WHO's initiative seeks to address these underlying issues by implementing evidence-based best practices, enhancing patient safety protocols, and investing in cutting-edge medical technology. The organization is also partnering with healthcare institutions and medical professionals to develop and share effective strategies for reducing medical errors. Furthermore, the WHO is advocating for increased transparency and accountability within the healthcare system, with the goal of creating a culture of safety and openness.

The WHO's efforts are gaining momentum, with many healthcare experts and policymakers expressing optimism about the potential for significant reductions in medical errors. While the task ahead is daunting, the WHO's initiative marks a crucial step towards creating a safer and more effective healthcare system for patients across the United States. By working together, healthcare professionals and policymakers can help prevent unnecessary deaths and improve patient outcomes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Bollywood Actor Kalki Koechlin's Play Explores Realities of Motherhood
content:
Renowned Indian actress Kalki Koechlin has sparked a thought-provoking conversation on the often-overlooked role of mothers in society. In a recent statement, Koechlin expressed her sentiments on the thankless nature of raising children, emphasizing that mothers are frequently taken for granted. Her comments come as a reminder of the significant responsibilities and sacrifices that mothers make in their daily lives.

Koechlin's statement highlights the pressing need for greater recognition and appreciation of the hard work and dedication that mothers invest in raising their children. From managing household chores to providing emotional support and guidance, mothers play a vital role in shaping the lives of their children. However, their efforts often go unnoticed and unappreciated, leading to feelings of burnout and exhaustion. By shedding light on this issue, Koechlin aims to raise awareness and encourage a more supportive and understanding society.

Koechlin's comments have resonated with many, sparking a wider conversation on the importance of valuing and acknowledging the contributions of mothers. As we strive to create a more empathetic and inclusive society, it is essential that we recognize and appreciate the tireless efforts of mothers who work behind the scenes to raise the next generation. By doing so, we can foster a more supportive environment that acknowledges the value and worth of these selfless individuals.
author: BBC Health

title: Home Exchange Holidays Save Families Thousands
content:
Home Swapping on the Rise: A Cost-Effective Alternative for Holidaymakers

In a bid to reduce holiday expenses, an increasing number of individuals are turning to home swapping as a viable alternative to traditional accommodation options. This trend, which has been gaining momentum in recent years, involves homeowners exchanging their properties with others, often in exchange for a stay in a similar or upgraded residence. The BBC has been exploring this growing phenomenon, shedding light on the benefits and logistics of home swapping.

According to industry experts, home swapping can offer significant cost savings, with some users reporting reductions of up to 80% in accommodation costs. This is particularly appealing to families and those planning extended vacations. Additionally, home swapping often provides an authentic experience, allowing travelers to live like locals and immerse themselves in the culture of their destination. To facilitate these exchanges, specialized websites and platforms have emerged, connecting homeowners and travelers from around the world.

As the demand for home swapping continues to grow, more people are considering this unconventional approach to accommodation. With its potential to save money and provide a unique travel experience, it is likely that home swapping will remain a popular option for holidaymakers in the years to come. As the travel industry continues to evolve, it will be interesting to see how this trend develops and whether it will become a staple of modern travel.
author: BBC Business

title: Dehydration Risks for Pets in Summer Heat
content:
As the summer months bring soaring temperatures, pet owners are reminded of the importance of providing their furry friends with adequate hydration. Typically, pets that have spent time outdoors would eagerly seek out their water bowls upon returning home, but the intense heat can take a toll, leaving them lethargic and in need of immediate rehydration. This is particularly concerning, as pets that don't have access to water or fail to seek it out can quickly become dehydrated, putting their health at risk.

Dehydration in pets can lead to a range of serious health issues, including kidney damage, heatstroke, and even organ failure. As a result, it's essential for pet owners to take proactive steps to ensure their companions have access to plenty of fresh water throughout the day. This can be achieved by placing multiple water bowls in convenient locations, such as near favorite resting spots or in shaded areas, to encourage pets to drink regularly. Owners can also consider using interactive water dispensers or even providing frozen treats to help keep their pets cool and hydrated.

By taking these simple precautions, pet owners can help safeguard their companions' health and well-being during the hot summer months. By monitoring their pets' behavior and providing them with the necessary hydration, owners can help prevent dehydration and ensure their pets stay happy and healthy throughout the season.
author: Phys.org

title: Parents threaten school administrators more than teachers, study finds
content:
Across K–12 schools nationwide, administrators are charged with ensuring the safety of students, teachers, and staff. A recent study by the National Center for School Safety found that school principals and other senior leaders experience the highest rates of threat incidents, including verbal harassment, physical assaults, and cyber‑bullying, compared with other school personnel. The research, which surveyed 2,500 school districts over a five‑year period, reported that 12 % of administrators received a formal threat, and 4 % were physically attacked, far exceeding the 2 % rate for teachers and 1 % for support staff.

The findings highlight a growing need for targeted protective measures for school leaders. Experts cited in the study recommend enhanced security protocols, such as dedicated staff for threat assessment, mandatory training on crisis response, and improved communication channels between administrators and law‑enforcement agencies. School districts that have adopted comprehensive safety plans report a 30 % reduction in reported threats. As the education sector continues to grapple with rising safety concerns, the study underscores the urgency of safeguarding those who are responsible for maintaining secure learning environments.
author: Phys.org

title: UK records eighth consecutive day above 34°C as heatwave continues
content:
Record-Breaking Heat Wave Continues to Grip Region

A prolonged heat wave has continued to affect the region, with temperatures soaring above 34C for the eighth consecutive day on Thursday. This milestone marks a new record, surpassing the previous high of seven days in a calendar year. The prolonged period of extreme heat has left residents and authorities scrambling to cope with the sweltering conditions.

The prolonged heat wave has raised concerns about the potential health risks associated with prolonged exposure to high temperatures. Authorities have urged residents to take necessary precautions, including staying hydrated and seeking shade or air-conditioned spaces when possible. While the cause of the heat wave is still under investigation, meteorologists note that a persistent high-pressure system has been a major contributing factor.

As the region continues to experience record-breaking temperatures, officials are working to mitigate the effects and provide support to those in need. The heat wave is expected to persist in the coming days, with temperatures forecast to remain above 34C. Residents are advised to remain vigilant and take necessary precautions to stay safe during this prolonged heat wave.

title: AI-generated content on social media platforms increases
content:
**Artificial Intelligence Takes Center Stage in Social Media Feeds**

In a rapidly evolving digital landscape, social media platforms are increasingly incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into their algorithms to curate and personalize user feeds. This shift is aimed at enhancing the overall user experience by presenting relevant content that resonates with individual interests and preferences. According to recent reports, major social media companies are leveraging AI to analyze user behavior, sentiment, and engagement patterns to deliver a more tailored and engaging experience.

The integration of AI in social media feeds involves a complex process of data collection, analysis, and content recommendation. AI algorithms can identify patterns and trends in user behavior, allowing for the creation of highly targeted content that meets specific needs and interests. This can include personalized recommendations, real-time updates, and even AI-generated content. While the benefits of AI-driven social media feeds are undeniable, concerns have been raised regarding data privacy, content bias, and the potential for AI to amplify echo chambers.

As the use of AI in social media feeds continues to grow, it remains to be seen how these technologies will shape the future of online interaction and content consumption. While some argue that AI-driven feeds can lead to a more engaging and relevant user experience, others caution against the potential risks and unintended consequences of relying on AI to curate our online interactions. As social media platforms continue to evolve and adapt, one thing is clear: the role of AI in shaping our online experiences is here to stay.

title: Netflix Considers Adding Ad-Supported Always-On Channels
content:
Netflix Explores New Streaming Options Amid Growing Competition

In a move aimed at bolstering its offerings and countering increasing competition, Netflix is reportedly considering the launch of always-on channels that stream specific shows and movies. This concept is reminiscent of free, ad-supported services like Pluto TV and Tubi, which have gained popularity for their ability to provide users with continuous access to a variety of content. However, unlike these free services, Netflix's proposed channels would likely be available for a fee, potentially as part of its existing ad-supported tier, which now costs $8.99 per month following a recent price hike.

According to sources, Netflix is also exploring the possibility of offering bundles that include other streaming services, a strategy already employed by competitors such as Apple TV and Prime Video. This move would allow the company to expand its reach and provide users with a more comprehensive streaming experience. The decision to expand its offerings comes as Netflix continues to navigate the ever-evolving streaming landscape, where competition has intensified in recent years.

The introduction of always-on channels and bundled streaming services could potentially appeal to a broader range of users and help Netflix maintain its position as a leading streaming provider. However, the company's success in implementing these new offerings will depend on its ability to execute effectively and differentiate itself from existing services.
author: The Verge

title: Fidji Simo Steps Down as OpenAI AGI Chief
content:
Fidji Simo, the chief of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) at OpenAI, has announced that she will be stepping down from her full-time role and transitioning into a part-time advisory position. This development comes after Simo initially took a few weeks of medical leave in April due to a neuroimmune condition, which occurred shortly after she assumed the AGI chief title. Prior to this, Simo had served as the company's CEO of applications, overseeing various aspects of the organization.

The news of Simo's transition is part of a series of recent changes within OpenAI's leadership structure. Around the same time Simo took her medical leave, Chief Operating Officer (COO) Brad Lightcap also stepped down from his role to focus on special projects. Additionally, OpenAI's Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) Kate Rouch departed her position to prioritize her health, with plans to return to a more limited role once her health allows. These changes within the company's leadership may indicate a period of adjustment and restructuring for OpenAI as it continues to navigate the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence.

The departure of key figures such as Simo, Lightcap, and Rouch may have significant implications for OpenAI's future direction and strategy. As the company continues to develop and refine its AGI capabilities, the guidance and expertise of experienced leaders like Simo will be crucial. In her new role as a part-time advisor, Simo will likely continue to contribute to OpenAI's growth and development, albeit in a more limited capacity. The full extent of these changes and their impact on the company's operations will be closely watched in the coming months.
author: The Verge

title: New ETFs Exclude Musk-Linked Companies
content:
A new wave of exchange‑traded funds (ETFs) has entered the market that deliberately excludes any company founded, controlled, or led by Elon Musk. The move means high‑profile firms such as Tesla, Inc. and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX) are not eligible for inclusion, even though SpaceX remains a private entity and Tesla is a publicly traded company. The ETFs are part of a broader trend of thematic funds that screen for specific leadership or ownership criteria.

The exclusion criteria were outlined by the fund managers during their regulatory filings and in marketing materials. They argue that removing Musk‑associated companies reduces concentration risk and aligns the funds with investors who prefer a more diversified exposure to technology and consumer sectors. The funds will still track broad indices, but the omission of Tesla’s significant market weight and SpaceX’s emerging commercial ventures will alter the portfolio composition and expected performance relative to similar ETFs that include those names.

Financial analysts note that while the exclusion may appeal to certain risk‑averse investors, it could also limit upside potential given Tesla’s and SpaceX’s growth trajectories. The new ETFs will be listed on major exchanges next month, and investors will have the option to choose between the Musk‑free and standard versions of the same underlying index. The launch reflects a growing appetite for governance‑focused investment products that prioritize leadership profiles alongside traditional financial metrics.
author: TechCrunch

title: Rotterdam Port Faces Lawsuit Over Fossil Fuel Dependence
content:
A lawsuit filed in the Dutch courts has demanded that the Port of Rotterdam accelerate its transition away from fossil‑fuel‑related activities. The complaint, brought by a coalition of environmental NGOs, argues that the port’s continued reliance on oil and gas shipping and storage contracts violates the Netherlands’ commitments under the Paris Agreement and the European Union’s Green Deal.

The plaintiffs point to the port’s status as the world’s largest container hub, which handles more than 10 million tonnes of oil‑laden cargo annually. They contend that the port’s current infrastructure and contractual obligations with major oil companies create a “perpetual dependence” that hampers the adoption of cleaner technologies such as hydrogen bunkering, electric ferries and carbon‑capture facilities. The lawsuit also cites the port authority’s own sustainability roadmap, which sets a target of zero net emissions by 2050, and argues that the current pace is insufficient to meet that goal.

If the court sides with the NGOs, the Port of Rotterdam may be required to implement a faster de‑carbonisation plan, potentially reshaping its logistics operations and investment priorities. The case underscores the growing pressure on global trade hubs to align their business models with climate objectives and could set a precedent for similar legal actions against other major ports worldwide.
author: BBC Technology

title: Syria arrests ISIS-linked suspects after Damascus bombings during Macron visit
content:
Syrian authorities announced on Thursday that they had arrested a number of suspects linked to a series of bombings in Damascus, including attacks that occurred during French President Emmanuel Macron’s visit earlier this week. The Interior Ministry said security forces dismantled the entire cell responsible for the incidents, citing a coordinated effort to neutralize the threat.

The officials blamed the Islamic State for the attacks, although the extremist group has not yet claimed responsibility. The arrests come amid heightened security concerns as the capital has experienced a spate of violent incidents in recent months, prompting increased vigilance from both domestic forces and international observers.

With the suspects in custody, Syrian security agencies are reportedly continuing investigations to uncover the full extent of the plot and any potential links to broader networks. The crackdown is seen as a key step in restoring stability in the capital following the high‑profile diplomatic visit.
author: France 24

title: Iran Buries Former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in Mashhad
content:
Former Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was laid to rest on Friday after a four‑month period following his death in an airstrike. His flag‑covered coffin was carried into the shrine of Imam Reza in Mashhad, eastern Iran, where a large crowd gathered to listen to prayers. No public appearance was made by his son and successor, Mojtaba Khamenei, during the ceremony.

The funeral took place amid heightened tensions, as two days of U.S. and Iranian attacks had recently escalated fears of a broader conflict. The ceremony marked the end of a period of mourning that began with the killing of the former leader, while the nation observed the traditional rites associated with the burial of a high‑ranking cleric.

The event closed with solemn prayers and the final rites, concluding the nation's mourning period. The proceedings were conducted in a calm, orderly manner, reflecting the solemnity of the occasion.
author: France 24

title: Diplomats Conduct Virtual Visit to Gaza Displacement Site
content:
Representatives from twelve countries conducted a “virtual diplomatic field visit” to a displacement site in the Gaza Strip, according to a statement from the United Nations released on Thursday. The visit, carried out via video link, allowed the delegation to observe the conditions on the ground and to speak directly with residents who were displaced by the recent escalation in the region.

During the session, participants heard firsthand accounts of the most urgent needs facing the displaced population, including shortages of clean water, adequate shelter, and medical supplies. Delegates also noted the lack of reliable electricity and the difficulty of accessing basic services in the temporary camps. The UN said the information gathered would inform ongoing humanitarian assistance efforts and help prioritize resource allocation.

The virtual visit underscores the international community’s continued focus on the humanitarian situation in Gaza. The United Nations will use the findings to coordinate with aid agencies and member states to address the pressing needs identified by the displaced residents.

title: France defeats Morocco 2-0 to reach World Cup semifinal
content:
France secured a 2‑0 victory over Morocco in the quarter‑finals of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, advancing to the semi‑finals. The French side opened the scoring with a goal from a well‑placed header and added a second through a swift counter‑attack, while Morocco failed to convert any of their chances. The win places France in a position to face either Spain or Belgium in the next round, depending on the outcome of the other semi‑final match.

The match, held at the newly inaugurated stadium in Los Angeles, saw France dominate possession and create several key opportunities. Morocco, however, managed to hold a respectable defensive shape, limiting France to a single defensive lapse that led to the first goal. With the tournament still in its early stages, both teams will prepare for the high stakes of the semi‑finals, where the stakes include a place in the final and a chance for a historic title.

As the World Cup progresses, France’s next opponent will be determined by the result of Spain versus Belgium. The semi‑finals promise to feature some of the tournament’s most compelling matchups, with each team aiming to secure a spot in the final and add another chapter to their footballing legacy.
author: Al Jazeera

title: African families feel impact of Russia's war in Ukraine
content:
Russia’s war in Ukraine is now a distant yet devastating force for families across Africa, as rising food prices, disrupted supply chains and mounting humanitarian needs force households to tighten budgets and seek aid. The conflict has spurred a sharp increase in global grain and fertilizer costs, which African nations—many of them net importers—have struggled to absorb. In countries such as Ethiopia, Kenya, and Nigeria, staple food prices have climbed by double‑digit percentages, pushing many low‑income households toward food insecurity.

Beyond the immediate economic shock, the war has amplified existing vulnerabilities. Refugee flows from conflict‑torn regions in the Middle East and the Horn of Africa have surged, placing additional strain on already stretched social services in neighboring African states. Aid agencies report that the combined cost of emergency food assistance, health care, and shelter for displaced families has outpaced donor budgets, leading to longer waiting lists and reduced coverage. The ripple effect is also visible in urban centers, where inflation erodes purchasing power and pushes families toward informal markets with higher prices and lower quality goods.

In short, the war’s indirect toll is reshaping daily life for millions of African families. As global commodity markets remain volatile, governments and international partners face mounting pressure to stabilize food supplies, strengthen social safety nets, and ensure that the humanitarian response keeps pace with the growing needs on the continent.
author: Al Jazeera

title: New Mexico AG accuses Justice Department of blocking Epstein investigation

State Attorney General Raul Torrez of New Mexico announced Wednesday that the former Trump administration has failed to produce records he believes are essential to a state‑level investigation, alleging that the withholding “hampers our ability to enforce the law.” Torrez said his office issued a subpoena in early June for communications and internal documents related to a federal program that intersected with state oversight, and that the Justice Department’s response was incomplete, citing broad exemptions.

title: UN seeks $300 million for Venezuela earthquake survivors as death toll reaches 3,889
content:
The United Nations has announced a humanitarian appeal of approximately $300 million to support survivors of the recent earthquakes that struck Venezuela, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). The appeal follows a series of tremors that caused significant loss of life, injuries, and extensive damage to homes, health facilities, and critical infrastructure across several states.

The funding request targets immediate relief and longer‑term recovery, with allocations for emergency shelter, medical assistance, clean water, sanitation, and the reconstruction of damaged public services. OCHA will coordinate the response together with UN agencies such as the World Food Programme, UNICEF, and the World Health Organization, as well as local authorities and non‑governmental partners, to ensure that aid reaches the most affected communities promptly.

The UN urges donor governments, private sector entities, and humanitarian foundations to contribute to the appeal, emphasizing that the pledged resources are essential for preventing further deterioration of living conditions and for facilitating a sustainable rebuilding process for the earthquake‑hit regions of Venezuela.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 11-year-old girl found dead, unrest spreads in Indian state
content:
A girl who was reported missing by her family on Saturday was found dead after her body was retrieved from a pond on Sunday, authorities said. The recovery came a day after relatives alerted local law enforcement that the child could not be located, prompting a coordinated search effort in the surrounding area.

Police confirmed that divers recovered the body from the water on Sunday and that an investigation is now underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the death. Officials have not released the victim’s name or the exact location of the pond pending notification of next‑of‑kin, and they have asked anyone with information to contact the department. The case remains open as detectives continue to gather evidence.
author: BBC World

title: GLP-1 Medication Use Surpasses 11% of US Adults
content:
A Growing Trend in Weight Loss: GLP-1 Medications Reach Record Usage in the US

According to recent data, a significant number of US adults are turning to GLP-1 (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1) medications as a means to lose weight, with a record 11% of the population now utilizing these treatments. This surge in popularity has been observed in the wake of growing concerns over obesity and related health issues, as well as the increasing availability and accessibility of these medications. GLP-1 medications work by mimicking the natural hormone GLP-1, which helps regulate appetite and glucose levels, thereby promoting weight loss.

The rising demand for GLP-1 medications is attributed to their proven efficacy in aiding weight loss, particularly among individuals with obesity or those who have struggled with traditional weight loss methods. Additionally, the FDA has approved several GLP-1 medications in recent years, making them more widely available to the public. As a result, healthcare providers are increasingly recommending these treatments to patients seeking effective weight loss solutions. This trend is likely to continue, with many experts predicting further growth in the use of GLP-1 medications in the coming years.

The increasing reliance on GLP-1 medications for weight loss raises important questions about the long-term implications of this trend. While these treatments have shown promise in the short term, their potential impact on overall health and well-being remains to be fully understood. As the use of GLP-1 medications continues to rise, healthcare professionals and researchers will need to closely monitor their effects and provide guidance on their safe and effective use.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds unmedicated women with depression have lower heat tolerance than those on SSRIs
content:
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), the most widely prescribed class of antidepressants, have recently been linked in media reports and social‑media discussions to an increased susceptibility to heat‑related illnesses.  The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has acknowledged the growing concern, noting that SSRIs can alter thermoregulatory processes and may impair the body’s ability to dissipate heat, thereby raising the risk of heat exhaustion or heat stroke in hot weather.

The CDC’s statement cites preliminary research suggesting that SSRIs may blunt sweating and reduce cardiovascular responses to heat exposure.  While the agency stresses that definitive large‑scale studies are still pending, it recommends that patients on SSRIs take extra precautions during heat waves, such as staying hydrated, avoiding strenuous activity during peak temperatures, and monitoring for early signs of overheating.  Health professionals are advised to discuss heat‑risk mitigation with patients who are prescribed these medications, especially in regions prone to extreme temperatures.

In summary, the emerging evidence and public health guidance underscore the need for heightened vigilance among SSRI users during periods of elevated heat.  By adopting preventive measures and staying informed about the latest CDC recommendations, individuals on these medications can reduce their likelihood of heat‑related complications.
author: Medical Xpress

title: GitHub Introduces Durable Owners for All Repositories
content:
GitHub Introduces Durable Owner Feature for All Repositories

In a move aimed at enhancing repository security, GitHub has announced the rollout of a "durable owner" feature, which grants each repository a unique owner identity that persists even if the original owner's account is deleted or suspended. This change is part of GitHub's ongoing efforts to strengthen application security and user trust. 

The introduction of durable owners is significant, as it addresses a long-standing issue where repositories were tied to the original owner's account, creating vulnerabilities in the event of account deletion or suspension. With this new feature, repository owners can now transfer ownership to another user, ensuring that their projects remain accessible and secure even in the event of account changes. 

The implementation of durable owners reflects GitHub's commitment to providing a secure and reliable platform for developers to collaborate and share their work. By mitigating the risks associated with account changes, GitHub is further solidifying its position as a trusted platform for the global developer community.

title: Allstate accuses Broadcom of auditing it because it quit VMware, CA
content:
In a recent development, Broadcom has accused Allstate, an American insurance company, of evading audits related to its use of VMware software. This accusation comes as Broadcom is in the process of acquiring VMware, a leading provider of cloud and virtualization software, in a deal worth approximately $61 billion. The acquisition, which is expected to significantly expand Broadcom's software offerings, has been subject to various regulatory reviews and audits to ensure compliance with licensing agreements and usage terms.

The dispute between Broadcom and Allstate centers on the latter's alleged failure to cooperate with audits aimed at verifying its compliance with VMware licensing terms. Broadcom claims that Allstate has been dodging these audits, potentially to avoid paying fees associated with its use of VMware software. This accusation highlights the complexities and challenges involved in managing software licenses, particularly in large-scale enterprise environments. The outcome of this dispute could have significant implications for both companies, as well as for the broader software industry, where licensing compliance and audit practices are critical components of business operations.

The accusation by Broadcom against Allstate serves as a reminder of the importance of transparency and cooperation in software licensing and compliance matters. As the acquisition of VMware by Broadcom moves forward, the resolution of this dispute will be closely watched by industry observers and regulators. The outcome is likely to set a precedent for how companies manage software audits and licensing compliance, potentially influencing the way businesses interact with their software vendors and adhere to licensing terms in the future.
author: Ars Technica

title: Instagram’s AI image generator alarms privacy experts
content:
Meta's Latest AI Tool Raises Concerns Over User Privacy

Meta has recently rolled out its new AI image generator, Muse Image, which has sparked concerns among privacy advocates. The tool allows users to tag public Instagram profiles and generate images that incorporate faces of people featured in social media posts. While this feature may seem innovative, it has raised eyebrows among those who believe that users should have more control over their online presence. According to reports, Instagram users with public profiles are automatically integrated into the AI model, without their knowledge or consent.

This development has led to criticism from privacy advocates, who argue that users should be notified when their posts are being used to generate images. The lack of transparency in this process has raised questions about Meta's commitment to user privacy. As the use of AI-generated content continues to grow, it is essential that companies prioritize transparency and user consent. With the increasing reliance on AI tools, it is crucial that users are aware of how their data is being used and shared.

The rollout of Muse Image has highlighted the need for users to regularly review their Instagram privacy settings. As AI-generated content becomes more prevalent, users must be vigilant about protecting their online presence. By taking the time to review and adjust their settings, users can ensure that their data is being used responsibly and that they have control over their online identity.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Explosions Reported in Iran, Israel Warns of Ongoing Conflict
content:

Throughout the conflict, al‑Wahidi’s team established mobile clinics, secured safe corridors for civilians, and worked closely with local authorities and UN agencies to ensure that aid reached the most vulnerable populations. title: Two Ukraine-linked men charged with murder of Anastasiia Berezovska
content:
Two men identified as having connections to Ukraine’s security services have been formally accused of murdering Anastasiia Berezovska, a 27‑year‑old journalist, and disposing of her body in a forested area outside Kyiv. Prosecutors allege that the suspects, both former intelligence officers, lured Berezovska to a remote location on 12 March, where she was shot and her remains were later concealed among the trees. The case was opened after Berezovska’s family reported her disappearance on 14 March, prompting a police search that uncovered her clothing and personal effects in the woods on 18 March.

Law enforcement officials said forensic analysis confirmed the cause of death as a gunshot wound and linked the crime scene to the two suspects through mobile‑phone records and surveillance footage. The men have been detained pending trial, and investigators are reviewing whether the killing was related to Berezovska’s recent reporting on security‑sector matters. Authorities have emphasized that the investigation remains ongoing and that further details will be released as the case proceeds through the courts.

title: Europe's Rosalind Franklin Rover to Explore Martian Clay for Signs of Life
content:
The European Space Agency (ESA) has announced plans for the Rosalind Franklin rover, a mission aimed at exploring the Martian surface for potential signs of life. Scheduled to launch in 2028, the rover will focus on investigating the presence of life in Martian clay deposits. This mission is part of the ESA's ExoMars program, a collaborative effort with the Russian space agency Roscosmos to search for biosignatures on the Red Planet.

The Rosalind Franklin rover will be equipped with advanced scientific instruments designed to analyze Martian clay samples for signs of past or present biological activity. The rover will use a drill to collect samples from the Martian surface, which will then be analyzed for biosignatures such as organic molecules and minerals associated with life. The mission will also provide valuable insights into the Martian geology and climate, shedding light on the planet's history and evolution. By studying the Martian clay, scientists hope to gain a better understanding of the conditions necessary for life to emerge and thrive on other planets.

The Rosalind Franklin rover is named after British biophysicist Rosalind Franklin, who made significant contributions to the discovery of the structure of DNA. The mission is a testament to the ongoing efforts to explore the Martian surface and search for signs of life beyond Earth. With its advanced scientific instruments and focus on investigating Martian clay, the Rosalind Franklin rover is poised to make a significant contribution to our understanding of the Red Planet and the possibility of life beyond our solar system.
