title: Non‑quantum space‑time theory proposed to explain gravity‑quantum interaction
content:
Physicists have long struggled to reconcile Einstein’s description of gravity with the probabilistic framework of quantum mechanics.  A new proposal, however, suggests that the key may lie in a “non‑quantum” model of space‑time that treats the fabric of the cosmos as a deterministic field rather than a set of quantum states.  The theory, developed by a collaboration of theoretical physicists at the Institute for Fundamental Physics, argues that gravity emerges from the geometry of this field, while quantum phenomena arise from statistical fluctuations on top of it.

Unlike conventional approaches such as string theory or loop quantum gravity, the non‑quantum space‑time model does not require a quantized metric.  Instead, it introduces a continuous background field governed by a set of differential equations that reproduce Einstein’s equations in the macroscopic limit.  Preliminary calculations indicate that the model can account for the observed bending of light around massive objects and the gravitational redshift measured in laboratory experiments, while also providing a natural explanation for the apparent randomness of quantum measurements through stochastic perturbations of the field.

If further mathematical scrutiny and experimental tests confirm the model’s predictions, it could reshape the quest for a unified theory.  The research team plans to publish a detailed derivation in the upcoming issue of *Physical Review Letters* and to collaborate with experimental groups to search for subtle deviations from standard quantum mechanics that would support the non‑quantum space‑time hypothesis.
author: New Scientist

title: June European heatwave may have caused up to 20,000 deaths
content:
Europe’s most intense heatwave yet, which swept the continent in late June and early July, is still unfolding, and an exact death toll will not be known for several months.  In the meantime, researchers are using statistical models that compare excess mortality during the current heatwave to the patterns observed in past hot spells to estimate the number of deaths attributable to the extreme temperatures.  By examining the number of people who died during previous heatwaves in the same regions and adjusting for demographic changes, scientists can approximate the likely impact of the current event.

The methodology relies on data from national health agencies, which record all-cause mortality on a daily basis.  Analysts calculate the expected number of deaths for a given period based on long‑term trends and then subtract this baseline from the observed deaths.  The resulting excess is attributed to the heatwave, after controlling for other factors such as influenza activity or other epidemics.  Early analyses suggest that the current heatwave could add several thousand deaths across Europe, but the final figure will only be confirmed once all mortality records are fully processed and verified.
author: New Scientist

title: Purine-rich Bacterial Genes Shield RNA from Rho Factor
content:
Researchers have identified a critical mechanism for enhancing gene expression in certain bacterial species: shielding messenger RNA (mRNA) from the Rho transcription‑termination factor. Rho is a quality‑control protein that recognizes specific RNA sequences and prematurely terminates transcription, thereby limiting the production of therapeutic proteins. By engineering RNA transcripts that either lack Rho‑binding motifs or incorporate structural elements that block Rho access, scientists can maintain continuous transcription and achieve higher yields of desired proteins.

The discovery underscores the importance of understanding sequence requirements for expressible genes in bacterial expression systems. Detailed mapping of Rho‑sensitive sites and the development of RNA‑shielding strategies enable more reliable production of complex therapeutic agents, including enzymes, antibodies, and vaccine antigens. This approach also offers a pathway to refine synthetic biology tools, ensuring that engineered bacteria can efficiently produce high‑value proteins without being curtailed by endogenous quality‑control mechanisms.

In practical terms, the ability to shield transcripts from Rho could streamline the manufacturing of biologics, reduce production costs, and expand the range of proteins that can be expressed in bacterial hosts. As expression engineering continues to evolve, these insights provide a foundational strategy for optimizing bacterial platforms used in drug development and industrial biotechnology.
author: MIT News

title: MIT Human Insight Collaborative launches SHASS Faculty Fellows Program
content:
The SHASS Faculty Fellows Program, run by the MIT Human Insight Collaborative, has launched a new initiative to support emerging research projects within the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences (SHASS). The program offers faculty members a structured environment to develop interdisciplinary studies that integrate human insight with scientific and technological perspectives.

Through a combination of seed funding, dedicated research time, and facilitated discussion forums, the Fellows Program encourages collaboration across traditionally separate departments. Participants receive mentorship from peers and experts in related fields, fostering a network that can translate complex human-centered questions into actionable research outcomes. The collaborative framework also provides a platform for faculty to present preliminary findings, receive constructive feedback, and refine project scopes before pursuing larger grants.

By bridging disciplinary boundaries and providing targeted resources, the SHASS Faculty Fellows Program aims to accelerate innovative scholarship that addresses contemporary social and cultural challenges. The initiative underscores MIT’s commitment to fostering interdisciplinary inquiry and positions SHASS faculty to contribute meaningfully to both academic discourse and real‑world impact.
author: MIT News

title: Sitting Over 30 Minutes Increases Cancer Death Risk, Study Finds
content:
A new longitudinal study of more than 90,000 adults tracked over ten years has found that sitting or lying down while awake for periods longer than 30 minutes each day is linked to a higher risk of death from cancer. The researchers observed that each additional hour of uninterrupted inactivity corresponded with a measurable increase in cancer‑related mortality, suggesting that even modest extensions of sedentary time can have serious health consequences.

The analysis also indicated that incorporating light physical tasks—such as ironing, standing while cooking, or brief walks—may offset some of the risk associated with prolonged sitting. While the study does not establish a causal relationship, it underscores the potential benefits of breaking up sedentary periods with low‑intensity activity. Health officials are advised to consider these findings when updating guidelines aimed at reducing the adverse effects of sedentary behaviour.
author: Guardian Science

title: James Webb Telescope Images Infrared Features in FS Tau Star System
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has released a new infrared image of the FS Tau star system, a young binary pair located about 460 light‑years away in the Taurus constellation. The observation, taken with JWST’s NIRCam instrument, penetrates the dense dust that has long obscured the region, revealing a wealth of previously hidden structures. In addition to a striking array of background galaxies that appear suddenly bright against the dusty backdrop, the image shows a complex network of jets and outflows emanating from the binary stars.

The high‑resolution data highlight the circumstellar disks surrounding each star, along with shock fronts where material is being ejected at high velocity. Infrared wavelengths allow the telescope to see through the thick dust lanes that block visible light, providing a clearer view of the star‑forming environment. The background galaxies, seen as faint, distant light sources, offer a serendipitous glimpse of the distant universe, underscoring JWST’s dual capability to study both nearby star formation and the far‑field cosmos.

These observations demonstrate JWST’s unprecedented ability to probe the earliest stages of stellar evolution while simultaneously capturing distant extragalactic objects. The detailed view of FS Tau will help astronomers refine models of protoplanetary disk dynamics and the mechanisms that drive stellar jets, advancing our understanding of how stars and planetary systems form in dusty environments.
author: NASA News

title: Astronaut Chris Williams Captures Sunrise from ISS on June 26, 2026
content:
NASA astronaut Chris Williams captured a striking image of an orbital sunrise from the International Space Station (ISS) on June 26, 2026. The photograph, taken as the station emerged from Earth’s shadow, illustrates the rapid succession of daylight that crew members experience while orbiting the planet at an altitude of roughly 400 kilometers. The ISS completes a full circuit of Earth approximately every 90 minutes, allowing it to witness 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets within a single 24‑hour period.

The ISS, a multinational research laboratory that has been continuously inhabited since 2000, uses its high‑velocity orbit to conduct experiments in microgravity across a range of scientific disciplines, from materials science to human health. Williams’ image, credited to NASA, underscores both the unique visual perspective afforded by the station’s rapid orbit and its ongoing role as a platform for scientific discovery in low‑Earth orbit.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Artemis II Live Stream Sets New Agency Record
content:
NASA’s live coverage of the Artemis II mission captured an unprecedented level of public interest, logging more than 149.4 million total views across the agency’s digital platforms. The viewership tally includes streams of the crew launch, the spacecraft’s lunar flyby, and the splashdown, all broadcast on NASA‑owned channels that offered continuous, 24‑hour coverage of the Orion vehicle and its journey to the Moon.

The record‑breaking engagement underscores a sustained global audience for the United States’ first crewed lunar‑orbit flight since the Apollo program. By delivering round‑the‑clock video feeds and interactive content, NASA not only highlighted the technical milestones of Artemis II but also reinforced its outreach strategy aimed at broadening public participation in deep‑space exploration.
author: NASA News

title: Northeastern US experiences extreme heat and humidity with potential record temperatures
content:
A national weather service has warned that several regions across the country could experience record‑high temperatures during the upcoming long weekend, with forecasts indicating peaks that may surpass previous summer extremes. The advisory highlights the central and southern interior, where mercury readings are projected to climb into the high 40s °C (mid‑100s °F), while coastal areas are expected to see temperatures in the low 30s °C (high 80s °F), levels not recorded in the past decade.

Authorities have issued heat‑related health advisories and urged residents to stay hydrated, limit outdoor activity during peak heat hours, and check on vulnerable individuals. The elevated temperatures also raise concerns for increased wildfire risk and strain on energy grids, prompting utility companies to prepare for higher demand. The forecast underscores the importance of preparedness as the region navigates an unusually hot weekend.
author: BBC Science

title: Heatwave Forecast Threatens North America and Potentially Taylor Swift's Wedding
content:
Simon King reports that a severe heatwave is currently threatening large swaths of North America, with temperatures projected to exceed 40 °C (104 °F) in many regions. Meteorological agencies have issued heat advisories across the United States, Canada, and parts of Mexico, warning of the increased risk of heat‑related illnesses and potential strain on power grids. The forecast calls for sustained high temperatures over the next week, with several areas experiencing record‑breaking heat.

Health officials emphasize that vulnerable populations—including the elderly, children, and those with preexisting medical conditions—are at heightened risk. Hospitals in affected cities have already reported a rise in emergency visits for heatstroke, dehydration, and cardiovascular complications. In response, local authorities have opened cooling centers, increased public water distribution, and urged residents to stay hydrated and avoid outdoor activity during peak heat hours. Energy regulators are monitoring power usage to prevent outages, while emergency services are on standby for potential heat‑related incidents.

The heatwave underscores the growing impact of climate variability on North American weather patterns. While the immediate focus remains on public safety and infrastructure resilience, officials are also reviewing long‑term strategies to mitigate future heat events. As temperatures continue to climb, communities across the continent are urged to heed advisories and take precautionary measures to safeguard health and wellbeing.
author: BBC Science

title: Short Leash AI Coding Method Aims to Beat Fable
content:
Okturtles’ latest blog post, “Short‑Leash AI Method,” introduces a new technique for training large language models with a reduced context window. The method, which the authors call a “short leash,” limits the amount of preceding text the model can attend to during generation, thereby cutting computational overhead while preserving key contextual cues. According to the post, the approach can be applied to existing transformer architectures without requiring new hardware or extensive retraining, and preliminary experiments show comparable performance to full‑context models on a range of natural‑language benchmarks.

The Short‑Leash framework is designed to streamline inference for deployment on edge devices and lower‑cost servers. By constraining the attention span, the authors report a 30‑percent reduction in memory usage and a 20‑percent speed‑up in token generation on standard GPU setups. The blog also outlines a simple API for integrating the method into popular machine‑learning libraries, and provides open‑source code under an MIT license. The authors note that while the technique may slightly degrade performance on tasks that rely heavily on long‑range dependencies, it offers a practical trade‑off for many real‑world applications where latency and resource limits are critical.

The post has generated modest engagement on Hacker News, where it currently holds 40 up‑votes and 24 comments. Discussion threads focus on the method’s scalability, potential for reducing carbon footprint, and comparisons to other lightweight transformer variants. Several commenters point out that the Short‑Leash approach could complement existing pruning and quantization techniques, while others raise questions about its efficacy on more complex, multi‑document tasks. Overall, the community response suggests that the technique is of interest to practitioners looking to balance model performance with deployment constraints.
author: Hacker News

title: Astronomers Release Catalog of Rotation Periods for Over One Million Stars
content:
A collaborative team of astronomers has released a comprehensive catalog containing rotation periods for more than one million stars, marking one of the largest compilations of stellar spin rates to date. The dataset, derived primarily from photometric observations collected by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and supplemented with archival Kepler measurements, provides rotation periods ranging from a few hours to several months across a broad spectrum of stellar types and ages. By applying automated period‑finding algorithms and rigorous validation procedures, the researchers identified periodic brightness modulations caused by starspots, enabling precise determination of rotation rates for stars previously lacking such information.

The new catalog is expected to enhance studies of stellar magnetic activity, angular momentum evolution, and gyrochronology, offering a valuable benchmark for models that link rotation to stellar age. The authors have made the full dataset publicly available through an online repository, encouraging its integration into ongoing surveys and theoretical work. Early analyses already suggest refinements to age‑rotation relations for low‑mass stars and reveal patterns of differential rotation in certain stellar populations. The release has attracted attention within the astrophysics community, as reflected in discussion threads on platforms such as Hacker News, where the announcement garnered notable interest and brief commentary.
author: Hacker News

title: EFF Sends Letter to FTC Regarding X Consent Order
content:
The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) submitted a formal letter to the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) on July 2, 2026, urging the agency to tighten the terms of its recently issued consent order with X, the social‑media platform formerly known as Twitter. The correspondence, made public in a PDF released by the EFF, argues that the current order does not sufficiently protect user privacy, lacks enforceable provisions for data‑handling transparency, and fails to address X’s ongoing collection of location and biometric information without explicit consent. The EFF’s legal team cites recent FTC guidance on privacy and data security, contending that the consent order should be amended to require independent audits, clearer user opt‑out mechanisms, and a schedule for public reporting on compliance.

In the letter, the EFF also highlights X’s history of algorithmic opacity and the platform’s role in amplifying misinformation, urging the FTC to incorporate safeguards that limit the use of personal data for targeted advertising and content recommendation. The organization points to specific sections of the consent order that it believes are overly vague, requesting that the FTC define measurable benchmarks and impose penalties for non‑compliance that are proportionate to the scale of any violations. The EFF’s comments were posted alongside a discussion thread on Hacker News (item 48766209), where the submission garnered 75 up‑votes and generated 18 comments from industry observers and privacy advocates.

The FTC has not yet responded to the EFF’s recommendations, but the agency is expected to review the feedback as part of its ongoing oversight of X’s privacy practices. If the FTC adopts the suggested revisions, X could face stricter regulatory obligations that would reshape how the platform handles user data and algorithmic decision‑making, potentially setting a precedent for future consent orders with large social‑media companies.
author: Hacker News

title: Great Salt Lake Tracker article posted on Grow the Flow website
content:
GrowthEflow Utah has launched “LakeTracker,” an online platform that provides real-time data on water levels, temperature, and quality for the state’s major reservoirs. The service aggregates inputs from state agencies, satellite observations, and on‑site sensors, presenting the information through an interactive map and downloadable datasets. Designed for policymakers, researchers, and the public, the tool aims to improve transparency around water resource management amid ongoing drought conditions in the Intermountain West.

Developers of LakeTracker highlighted its capacity to alert users to significant fluctuations, support irrigation planning, and aid in ecological monitoring. The platform also integrates historical trends, allowing comparisons across seasons and years. Early feedback from environmental groups and municipal water managers has been positive, with users noting the ease of access and the potential for more informed decision‑making. The launch coincides with heightened scrutiny of water allocation policies and a broader push for data‑driven approaches to address regional water scarcity.

GrowthEflow Utah expects the tracker to become a central hub for water‑related data, encouraging community engagement and fostering collaborative solutions to the state’s water challenges. Ongoing updates and expanded sensor networks are planned for the coming year, positioning LakeTracker as a long‑term resource for sustainable water management in Utah.
author: Hacker News

title: Wireless LAN SD standard enables Wi‑Fi connectivity in SD cards
content:
The SD Association has released an updated overview of its SDIO/ISDIO specifications that highlights the capabilities of Wireless LAN SD cards, a class of devices that embed Wi‑Fi functionality directly into the Secure Digital (SD) form factor. The documentation details how these cards can provide high‑speed, low‑power wireless connectivity for a range of host devices, from smartphones and tablets to embedded systems, by leveraging the SDIO interface to transmit and receive data without the need for separate network hardware. The specification outlines supported protocols, data rates, power management features, and compliance testing procedures, positioning the technology as a versatile solution for manufacturers seeking to add wireless networking to products with limited space and power budgets.

The release has generated discussion among developers and industry observers, as reflected in a recent Hacker News thread that garnered 18 points and 18 comments. Participants noted the potential for rapid adoption in Internet‑of‑Things (IoT) applications and praised the standard’s emphasis on backward compatibility with existing SD hosts. Critics, however, raised questions about driver support across different operating systems and the security implications of integrating Wi‑Fi directly into removable storage. Overall, the updated SDIO overview signals a continued push toward broader integration of wireless capabilities within compact, modular hardware components.
author: Hacker News

title: LMDB 1.0 released with documentation online
content:
A technical write‑up posted on LMDB Tech has drawn notable attention from the developer community, earning 45 points and prompting 17 comments on the Hacker News discussion thread (item 48766598). The article, hosted at the LMDB Tech documentation site, was linked in the Hacker News post, where users quickly engaged with the content, reflecting the platform’s role as a hub for sharing and evaluating emerging software resources.

The discussion centers on LMDB’s design and performance characteristics, highlighting its use‑case scenarios, benchmarking results, and integration considerations for modern applications. Participants in the comments thread exchanged insights on implementation strategies, compared LMDB with alternative key‑value stores, and raised questions about scalability and reliability. The level of engagement underscores the continued interest in lightweight, high‑throughput database solutions within the open‑source and systems‑programming communities.
author: Hacker News

title: Virginia Enacts Ban on Sale of Geolocation Data
content:
Virginia has enacted a statewide ban on the commercial sale of geolocation data, marking one of the most comprehensive privacy measures in the United States to date. The legislation, which took effect on July 1, 2024, prohibits any entity from selling precise location information that can be linked to an individual without explicit consent, and it applies to both in‑state and out‑of‑state businesses that collect data from Virginia residents.

Under the new law, “geolocation data” is defined as any digital record that reveals the precise physical location of a person’s device at a specific time, including GPS coordinates, Wi‑Fi triangulation, and cell‑tower signals. The ban does not extend to data used for emergency services, law‑enforcement investigations, or anonymized aggregates that cannot be re‑identified. Violations are subject to civil penalties of up to $7,500 per incident, and the state’s Attorney General is authorized to enforce compliance through investigations and litigation. The measure follows similar statutes adopted in Colorado, Connecticut, and Utah, reflecting a growing trend among states to restrict the monetization of location‑based information amid rising concerns over surveillance and data misuse.

The law’s passage has drawn attention from privacy advocates and technology firms alike, with the announcement receiving 164 points and 20 comments on the Hacker News discussion forum, indicating significant public interest. Companies that collect or process geolocation data are now required to revise their data‑handling practices, obtain clear consent from users, and implement robust safeguards to avoid penalties, signaling a shift toward stricter data‑privacy standards nationwide.
author: Hacker News

title: BlastRadar provides instant production risk scores for Git diffs
content:
Blastradar, a newly released web application hosted on Vercel, was announced earlier this week as a real‑time monitoring tool for tracking high‑impact events across multiple data streams. The platform aggregates information from public APIs and presents it through an interactive dashboard, allowing users to filter and visualize occurrences based on severity, location, and category. Its developers describe the service as lightweight, serverless, and designed for rapid deployment, leveraging Vercel’s edge network to minimize latency.

Since its launch, Blastradar has attracted modest attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where the submission received eight points and has not yet generated public comments. The initial response highlights interest in the tool’s simplicity and potential for integration into existing workflows. Developers indicated plans to expand data source support and introduce customizable alert mechanisms in forthcoming updates.
author: Hacker News

title: Startup launches tool to combat groupthink in large language models
content:
The weekday newsletter The Download highlights a growing concern among artificial‑intelligence developers: large language models (LLMs) are increasingly producing homogeneous responses, a phenomenon described as “groupthink.” The briefing notes that the pattern emerges across major chatbots—including Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini—when users request simple, open‑ended tasks such as generating a random number. The uniformity of answers has prompted industry observers to call for mechanisms that can inject genuine variability into model outputs.

In response, a newly launched startup has introduced a tool designed to break the conformity cycle. By prompting users to ask any chatbot for a random number between 1 and a chosen limit, the service forces the underlying model to draw from a broader distribution of possible answers, thereby encouraging more diverse reasoning paths. The initiative aims to demonstrate that modest changes in user interaction can help LLMs escape entrenched response patterns, offering a practical step toward more varied and resilient conversational AI.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: AI deployed to manage turbine operations for efficiency and safety
content:
Artificial intelligence, long celebrated for chatbots and image‑generation tools, is increasingly being deployed as a foundational operating layer in sectors where physical infrastructure, continuous operation and safety are critical. Energy utilities, petrochemical plants, transportation networks and heavy‑manufacturing facilities are integrating AI into their control systems to monitor equipment, predict failures and optimize processes, turning vast streams of sensor data into actionable insights. Industry analysts note that the shift reflects a broader move from experimental pilots to production‑grade deployments, driven by the need to reduce downtime, improve efficiency and meet stringent regulatory standards.

Across these domains, AI algorithms are tasked with predictive maintenance, real‑time anomaly detection and autonomous decision‑making that can adjust valve positions, reroute power flows or trigger emergency shutdowns without human intervention. Early adopters such as a major European power grid operator have reported a 15 percent reduction in unplanned outages, while a North American refinery credited AI‑guided process controls with a 3 percent increase in yield and lower emissions. As the technology matures, firms are investing in robust data pipelines, cybersecurity safeguards and governance frameworks to ensure reliability and compliance, positioning AI as an essential component of the industrial ecosystem’s future resilience and productivity.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: AI Enhances Operational Excellence
content:
**Lean Six Sigma and BPM Drive Operational Clarity in Modern Enterprises**  
Lean Six Sigma and Business Process Management (BPM) emerged in the late 20th century as structured responses to the growing complexity of corporate operations. By offering statistical rigor and quality control, Lean Six Sigma promised measurable improvements in defect rates and cost efficiency. BPM, meanwhile, introduced comprehensive end‑to‑end mapping of workflows across departments, enabling organizations to visualize and streamline processes that previously operated in silos. Together, these frameworks provided a repeatable methodology for turning chaotic, sprawling operations into disciplined, data‑driven systems.

The adoption of Lean Six Sigma and BPM has been fueled by the need for continuous improvement and regulatory compliance across industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and finance. Companies that implemented these methodologies reported reductions in cycle times, lower waste, and enhanced customer satisfaction. Moreover, the integration of digital tools—such as process mining and real‑time analytics—has amplified the effectiveness of both frameworks, allowing firms to monitor performance metrics and adjust strategies in near real time.

Today, organizations continue to refine Lean Six Sigma and BPM practices, blending them with agile and DevOps principles to address the demands of rapid digital transformation. While challenges remain—such as sustaining cultural change and ensuring cross‑functional alignment—the proven track record of these frameworks underscores their enduring relevance in achieving operational excellence.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Key Google account settings to adjust for better privacy and security
content:
Google has rolled out an expanded suite of privacy controls that let users fine‑tune settings for account recovery, ad personalization, and the visibility of information on their Google profiles. The new options, accessible through the account management dashboard, enable individuals to specify which recovery methods—such as phone numbers, secondary email addresses, or security questions—are active, and to select the degree of personalization applied to advertisements displayed across Google services. Users can also determine which elements of their profile, including name, photo, and activity status, are visible to the public or restricted to contacts.

The changes come amid heightened scrutiny of data‑handling practices and a broader industry shift toward greater transparency and user empowerment. By offering granular control over personal data, Google aims to address regulatory expectations and consumer demand for clearer privacy choices. Analysts note that the streamlined interface may simplify compliance for both individual users and businesses that rely on Google’s ecosystem, potentially setting a benchmark for privacy management across major tech platforms.
author: Wired

title: DEA to Temporarily Schedule Kratom Compound 7-OH as Controlled Substance
content:
The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration announced that it will temporarily schedule the synthetic opioid known colloquially as “gas station heroin” as a controlled substance. The decision follows a series of investigations that linked the drug’s rapid rise in street use to a spike in overdose deaths across several states. By placing the compound on the temporary schedule, the agency aims to curb its distribution while it gathers additional data on its pharmacology and public‑health impact.

The move is seen as a significant win for the Marijuana and Hemp Advocacy Group (MAHA) and the mainstream kratom industry, both of which have long campaigned for clearer regulatory frameworks. MAHA has argued that a controlled‑substance designation for the opioid will help protect consumers and reduce the illicit market that often competes with legal kratom products. The kratom community, which relies on a regulated supply chain to maintain product safety, welcomed the ruling as a step toward greater legitimacy for their industry.

While the temporary scheduling will restrict the drug’s manufacture, distribution, and possession, the DEA has indicated that the measure is provisional pending further research. Stakeholders in the kratom sector expect the ruling to reduce the risk of cross‑market contamination and to support ongoing efforts to establish standardized testing protocols for herbal supplements.
author: Wired

title: Cursor aims to keep third‑party AI models after SpaceX acquisition
content:
Cursor, the AI‑powered productivity platform, announced that it has been acquired by SpaceX, the aerospace company founded by Elon Musk. The deal, which was disclosed in a joint statement by both firms, is part of SpaceX’s broader strategy to diversify into emerging technology sectors beyond space exploration. The acquisition will be structured as a strategic partnership, with Cursor retaining its independent operating team and brand identity.

Under the terms of the agreement, Cursor plans to continue offering a suite of third‑party AI models to its users, a move that signals the company’s commitment to an open‑AI ecosystem. By preserving access to external models, Cursor aims to foster collaboration among frontier AI labs, allowing developers to experiment with cutting‑edge capabilities while maintaining a unified user experience. The partnership will also enable SpaceX to leverage Cursor’s platform for internal data‑analysis and automation projects, creating a feedback loop that could accelerate innovation across both companies.

SpaceX’s acquisition of Cursor underscores the growing convergence of AI and aerospace technologies. While the exact timeline for integration remains unspecified, industry observers expect the collaboration to deepen cross‑disciplinary research and expand the availability of advanced AI tools. The move positions SpaceX as a key player in the AI landscape, while giving Cursor a powerful new partner to sustain its open‑model strategy.
author: Wired

title: Spotify acknowledges streaming fraud impacting Kalshi markets
content:
Kalshi, the U.S. exchange that lets traders bet on real‑world events, has seen a sudden withdrawal of interest in its Spotify‑related markets. One of the platform’s most active participants, who has built a reputation for consistently high‑volume trades, told WIRED that he will not engage in any Spotify‑linked contracts until the current dispute is resolved. The trader’s decision comes amid growing uncertainty over the legality and integrity of those markets.

The controversy centers on a recent policy change by Spotify that restricts the use of its data for third‑party betting platforms. Kalshi’s rules require that all event contracts be based on publicly verifiable outcomes, and Spotify’s new restrictions have led to questions about whether its streaming metrics can still be reliably used as a basis for market outcomes. Kalshi has issued a statement affirming its commitment to regulatory compliance, but has yet to clarify how it will address the potential breach of its own disclosure standards. The trader’s boycott signals a broader concern among the community that the integrity of the Spotify markets may be compromised until the platform’s policy and Kalshi’s compliance framework are aligned.
author: Wired

title: Love Island USA app surpasses 10 million users, outpacing many election turnouts
content:
The executive producer of “Love Island USA” recently highlighted the scale of audience engagement on the show’s companion app, noting that “we have more people voting on the ‘Love Island USA’ app than we do in many political elections taking place across the country.” The statement underscores the popularity of the interactive feature, which allows viewers to cast votes on contestants’ fates, influence challenges, and shape outcomes in real time. According to data released by the network, the app has recorded millions of votes each week, surpassing voter turnout figures reported in several state and local elections during recent cycles.

Industry analysts suggest that the comparison reflects broader trends in digital participation, where entertainment platforms can mobilize large audiences through gamified experiences. While the producer’s comment is anecdotal, it draws attention to the growing influence of streaming‑related voting mechanisms and raises questions about the role of such engagement metrics in measuring public interest. The network plans to expand the app’s capabilities for upcoming seasons, aiming to maintain high levels of viewer interaction.
author: Wired

title: Tesla reports 25% rise in Q2 vehicle deliveries
content:
Tesla released its second‑quarter production and delivery figures, indicating the company is rebounding after a challenging sales year in 2025. Between April and June, the automaker produced 451,758 vehicles, up roughly 10 percent from the 410,244 units manufactured in the same quarter a year earlier. The output consisted of 442,936 Model 3 and Model Y cars, alongside 8,822 units classified as “other vehicles,” which include the Cybertruck and the Tesla Semi. Earlier in the year, Tesla discontinued the Model S and Model X, narrowing its product lineup to focus on its high‑volume models.

Deliveries for the quarter reached 480,126 vehicles, surpassing the production total and signaling strong demand for the company’s streamlined offerings. The rise in both production and deliveries suggests that Tesla is beginning to recover from the sales slump experienced in 2025, positioning the firm for a more stable performance in the remainder of the fiscal year.
author: The Verge

title: Universal hosts influencer screenings for Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey
content:
Universal’s handling of advanced screenings for Christopher Nolan’s *The Odyssey* has sparked discussion about the role of social‑media influencers in film promotion. For several days it appeared that the studio had decided to exclude influencers from early showings, leaving many in the press community to wonder whether the decision was a deliberate shift away from the new media segment. However, on Monday the studio opened special screenings that brought influencers and traditional critics together at the Associated Press junket, demonstrating that Universal had not abandoned its earlier commitments.

The decision to include influencers alongside journalists reflects a broader industry trend: creators with large followings now represent a substantial portion of the media ecosystem, offering studios a direct line to engaged audiences. By inviting them to the same event as established critics, Universal acknowledged that influencer coverage can be as influential as traditional reviews in shaping public perception. The studio’s approach suggests a willingness to adapt its marketing strategy to the realities of modern film promotion, where online buzz often rivals, and sometimes surpasses, conventional media coverage.

In the end, Universal’s move underscores a shift in how studios engage with the press. While the initial confusion over influencer access may have caused a brief stir, the company’s willingness to integrate both traditional and digital voices indicates a recognition that a diversified media strategy is essential for reaching contemporary audiences. The *Odyssey* junket serves as a case study in balancing legacy journalism with the growing power of online content creators.
author: The Verge

title: Sony to Stop PlayStation Disc Production, Microsoft Expands Digital Games
content:
Sony announced plans to cease production of physical PlayStation discs, signaling a shift toward an entirely digital distribution model for its gaming ecosystem. The decision, discussed on the latest episode of The Vergecast, reflects a broader industry trend as Microsoft continues to expand its strategy of digitizing game libraries across its platforms. Both companies cite operational efficiencies, reduced manufacturing costs, and streamlined supply chains as primary motivations for moving away from traditional media formats that have dominated the market for decades.

Analysts note that the transition aligns with consumer preferences for instant access and the growing prevalence of high‑speed internet, which facilitate large‑scale digital downloads and streaming. While the move may simplify inventory management and lower environmental impact, it also marks the end of an era in which physical game discs, consoles, and accessories were central to the gaming experience. The industry now faces the challenge of ensuring reliable digital infrastructure and addressing concerns over ownership rights as physical media fades from the market.
author: The Verge

title: Weber Cuts Prices on Grills and Griddles Ahead of July 4th
content:
Weber is rolling out a series of discounts on its grills, smokers and griddles ahead of the July 4th holiday, offering price reductions of roughly $50 compared with typical retail listings. The Spirit E‑325, a three‑burner model, is now priced at $499 for propane (regularly $549) and $549 for natural‑gas (regularly $599), providing a 360‑square‑inch cooking area plus a 90‑square‑inch warming rack and two high‑heat searing zones. The Slate 30‑inch rust‑resistant griddle has been cut by $50 to $649, featuring a 500‑degree Fahrenheit surface, wind guards and a capacity for about 22 burgers, while the 17‑inch tabletop version is available for $249 after a similar discount, targeting portable use such as camping. Both the griddle and the Spirit E‑325 are listed on Weber’s website at the reduced rates, with comparable pricing noted at Home Depot and Ace Hardware.

For customers seeking higher‑end equipment, Weber’s Searwood XL 600 pellet grill is $100 off, now $1,199, offering a 972‑square‑inch cooking space, temperature range from 180 °F for smoking to 600 °F for searing, and the ability to handle roughly 20 burgers across its dual layers. A smaller Searwood 600 model is also discounted, though it carries a $200 price gap relative to the XL version. These promotions position Weber’s lineup as a cost‑effective option for both occasional backyard cookouts and more elaborate grilling setups as the summer holiday approaches.
author: The Verge

title: Meta Launches New AI-Powered Pocket App
content:
Meta has unveiled a new app called Pocket, re‑introducing the name that once belonged to Mozilla’s popular read‑it‑later service. The new Pocket is positioned as an AI‑centric platform that allows users to create and share small interactive “gizmos” generated from AI prompts, according to Business Insider. The launch follows Meta’s broader push into artificial intelligence, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg repeatedly describing AI as the next frontier for social media and outlining a vision where users can craft interactive experiences for their networks.

The re‑branding of Pocket comes after Meta hired engineers from Atma Sciences Inc., a company that previously developed an app of the same name. By repurposing the Pocket brand, Meta signals a shift from its original bookmarking focus to a more dynamic, AI‑driven content creation model. The new Pocket app is part of Zuckerberg’s broader strategy to embed AI tools across Meta’s suite of products, encouraging users to generate and exchange AI‑generated media within the company’s ecosystem.

While the original Pocket app was shut down last year, Meta’s iteration promises a different user experience, emphasizing real‑time AI interaction rather than simple article saving. The company’s move underscores its commitment to integrating AI into everyday social media use, aiming to keep users engaged through novel, shareable AI‑generated content.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla driver charged with manslaughter after crash kills Texas woman
content:
A 44‑year‑old Texas resident, Michael Butler, has been charged with manslaughter after his Tesla Model 3 struck and killed a woman inside her home last month. Butler was arrested on Wednesday and, according to an arrest affidavit, claimed that the vehicle was operating under Tesla’s Full‑Self Driving (FSD) system at the time of the fatal collision. The case was first reported by The Wall Street Journal and local outlet KHOU 11, and the latest court filings confirm the charges.

Court documents reveal that a police officer extracted data from Butler’s phone, uncovering a series of FSD‑related Google searches from May 2026, including queries such as “Tesla FSD not aggressive enough 2026 model.” The searches suggest Butler was actively researching the capabilities and limitations of Tesla’s autonomous driving features. The evidence is being used to assess whether the driver’s reliance on FSD contributed to the accident.

The investigation continues as prosecutors examine the extent to which Tesla’s autonomous system and the driver’s actions led to the fatal incident. The case highlights ongoing scrutiny of self‑driving technology and its role in traffic safety.
author: The Verge

title: Trump Negotiates 5% Stake in OpenAI, Below Sanders Target
content:
Insiders report that OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman is currently in active discussions with members of the former Trump administration.  The conversations, which have not been publicly confirmed, are said to focus on the regulatory landscape for artificial intelligence and potential collaboration on policy initiatives that could shape the industry’s future.

Altman has long been a key voice in U.S. tech policy, and his outreach to the Trump team follows a period in which the administration expressed both support for AI innovation and concerns about its societal impacts.  Analysts note that the talks could involve proposals for new oversight frameworks, funding for research, or guidance on the deployment of large language models in government applications.

The details of the negotiations remain undisclosed, and no official statement has been issued by either party.  As the discussions continue, observers will be watching for any agreements that might influence the direction of AI regulation and development in the United States.
author: Ars Technica

title: EU upholds $4.7 billion fine against Google over Android bundling
content:
The European Commission has opened formal proceedings against Google, accusing the company of abusing its dominant position by bundling its search engine and Chrome browser with the Android operating system. The investigation, launched under the EU’s antitrust rules, alleges that the practice forces device manufacturers and users to accept Google’s services as a condition for accessing the Android platform, thereby limiting competition from rival search and browser providers. The Commission’s complaint cites the high market share of Android—estimated at over 70 percent of global smartphone shipments—and the near‑ubiquitous presence of Google Search and Chrome on those devices as evidence of an illegal tying arrangement.

Google has responded that the integration of its services is essential for the seamless operation of Android and that users retain the ability to set alternative defaults. The company also points to previous settlements with the EU, including a €4.34 billion fine in 2018, as precedent for resolving competition concerns. The Commission has indicated that any penalty could reach up to 10 percent of Google’s worldwide annual revenue if the allegations are upheld. The case is expected to proceed through the EU’s formal antitrust process, with a decision likely to be issued later this year, potentially reshaping the relationship between Android’s open‑source platform and Google’s proprietary services.
author: Ars Technica

title: Artificial cell divides a few times in lab experiment
content:
A newly introduced production method has been reported to function effectively in only a limited number of company divisions, a result attributed to the extensive use of supplementary materials. The technique, which integrates additional compounds into the standard manufacturing workflow, was rolled out earlier this quarter with the aim of enhancing product durability and performance across the organization’s diverse operational units.

According to internal assessments, the added materials have increased the complexity of the process, restricting its successful application to those divisions equipped with the necessary handling equipment and specialized training. Management is reviewing the findings to determine whether broader implementation is feasible or if the approach will remain confined to the few divisions where it currently delivers the intended outcomes.
author: Ars Technica

title: Africa CDC confirms Marburg case in Uganda amid Ebola outbreak
content:
Early reports suggest a possible additional case of the ongoing health incident, though officials say the spread appears to remain localized. Health authorities are reviewing the preliminary data and have not yet confirmed the new case, emphasizing that the situation is being monitored closely.

The relevant agencies continue to assess the extent of the outbreak, focusing on containment measures within the affected area. While the potential new case underscores the need for vigilance, officials maintain that the limited geographic scope reduces the likelihood of broader transmission at this time.
author: Ars Technica

title: Plex launches 5-year membership pass priced at $250
content:
Plex, the popular media‑streaming and library‑management service, announced a rollout of new premium features that will be tied to more frequent billing cycles for its subscribers. The company’s latest update introduces advanced content‑curation tools, enhanced live‑TV integrations, and expanded cloud‑storage options, all of which will be accessible through a revised subscription structure that shifts many users from annual or semi‑annual plans to monthly or quarterly payments.

The shift aims to accelerate revenue growth while delivering continuous value to customers, according to a statement from Plex’s product team. Existing users who remain on legacy plans will be prompted to transition to the new tiers during the next renewal period, with pricing adjustments reflecting the added functionalities. Plex indicated that the changes will be implemented globally over the coming weeks, and that support resources are available to guide users through the migration process.
author: Ars Technica

title: NASA has not announced firm timelines for upcoming heavy-lift rockets
content:
Several high‑profile rocket programs have announced target launch windows that later slipped, leaving the industry without a recent instance of a publicly set date being met. In the past year, SpaceX’s Starship, NASA’s Artemis I, and Blue Origin’s New Glenn each disclosed specific timelines for inaugural flights, only to postpone them due to technical setbacks, supply‑chain constraints, and additional regulatory reviews. Official statements from the companies and the agencies involved cited the need for further testing of propulsion systems, structural components, and software integration as primary reasons for the delays.

The pattern of missed dates underscores the complexity of developing next‑generation launch vehicles and the cautious approach taken by both commercial operators and government programs. While no new launch date has yet been confirmed and subsequently achieved, stakeholders continue to refine designs and conduct ground‑based evaluations. Industry analysts note that future announcements are likely to incorporate broader windows to accommodate the iterative testing process, aiming to improve the reliability of schedule commitments.
author: Ars Technica

title: FAA Proposes Quiet Supersonic Flights Over U.S. Cities
content:
U.S. regulators have unveiled a set of rules that would allow quiet supersonic aircraft to fly over land without producing the disruptive sonic boom that has historically limited high‑speed flight. The new guidelines, issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), outline technical and operational requirements for aircraft that use advanced noise‑reduction technologies and optimized flight profiles. The rules are intended to enable commercial supersonic travel while protecting communities from the shock waves that have made such flights impractical for decades.

The FAA’s proposal builds on research from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) and industry partners that demonstrate how specific engine designs, wing shapes, and flight paths can dramatically lower sonic boom intensity. Under the new framework, airlines would need to submit detailed noise‑impact studies and demonstrate compliance with a maximum allowable boom threshold before receiving certification. The agency also plans to establish monitoring stations across the United States to ensure ongoing compliance and to gather data on the real‑world effects of quiet supersonic operations.

If approved, the rules could open the door to a new era of commercial supersonic travel, potentially cutting transcontinental flight times by up to 30 percent. The FAA will hold public comment periods and stakeholder meetings in the coming months, after which it will issue final regulations. The aviation industry is watching closely, as the decision could reshape the economics of long‑haul air travel and accelerate the deployment of next‑generation supersonic aircraft.
author: Ars Technica

title: New macOS infostealer PamStealer identified
content:
A cybersecurity research team has identified a new macOS‑based infostealer that is actively targeting Apple computers, highlighting a growing focus on the platform among cybercriminals. The malware, uncovered during routine threat‑intel monitoring, is capable of harvesting credentials, payment data and personal files before exfiltrating the information to remote command‑and‑control servers. Analysts note that the code shares similarities with previously documented Windows infostealers, suggesting that threat actors are adapting proven techniques to exploit the increasing market share of Mac devices.

The discovery comes amid a broader uptick in malicious activity directed at macOS, with security firms reporting a rise in both the number of variants and the sophistication of attacks. Researchers attribute this trend to the perception that Mac users are less likely to employ robust security measures, making them attractive targets for data‑stealing operations. The findings underscore the need for heightened vigilance, regular software updates and the deployment of endpoint protection solutions across all operating systems to mitigate the expanding threat landscape.
author: Ars Technica

title: Wisk Aero accused of firing manager over safety concerns
content:
A former software manager at Wisk Aero, the electric‑vertical‑takeoff‑and‑landing (eVTOL) venture backed by Boeing, has alleged that the company accelerated its software testing schedule in preparation for a pivotal flight test slated for 2025. The manager, who worked on the autonomous flight‑control system, told reporters that internal pressure to meet the milestone led to a compressed testing timeline that, in his view, compromised thorough verification and validation processes. He said the rush began in early 2024 and involved shortening simulation cycles and reducing the scope of hardware‑in‑the‑loop assessments that are typically required for safety‑critical avionics.

Wisk has not confirmed the allegations but issued a statement saying its development program follows industry‑standard safety protocols and that all testing phases are conducted under rigorous oversight. The company is pursuing certification from the Federal Aviation Administration and aims to demonstrate a fully autonomous eVTOL flight in 2025, a key step toward commercial operations. The claim adds to ongoing scrutiny of the rapid development timelines in the emerging urban air mobility sector, highlighting the balance firms must strike between innovation speed and regulatory compliance.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic discusses custom AI chip with Samsung
content:
Qualcomm announced its first custom artificial‑intelligence chip, the Snapdragon AI Accelerator, in partnership with Samsung Electronics on Tuesday, a week after OpenAI revealed its own custom AI chip developed with Broadcom. The new accelerator is designed to run high‑throughput inference workloads on mobile and edge devices, leveraging a 4‑stage pipeline and a 16‑bit tensor processing unit that Qualcomm claims can deliver up to 1.5 TFLOPS of mixed‑precision performance.

The chip is integrated into Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 4 platform, with Samsung’s 5‑nanometer fabrication process providing a 30 % improvement in power efficiency over previous generations. According to Qualcomm, the accelerator supports both TensorFlow Lite and PyTorch Mobile, and it includes a dedicated secure enclave for privacy‑preserving inference. Industry analysts note that the partnership positions Qualcomm to compete more aggressively with NVIDIA and Intel in the mobile AI market, while Samsung gains a foothold in AI‑accelerated consumer electronics.

With the launch of the Snapdragon AI Accelerator, Qualcomm signals its intent to expand its AI ecosystem
author: TechCrunch

title: Travel app Hopper to pay $35 million FTC settlement over hidden fees
content:
Hopper, the travel‑booking app, has agreed to pay $35 million to resolve a Federal Trade Commission investigation that accused the company of employing deceptive “dark‑pattern” designs to conceal fees and mislead users about the costs and benefits of its services. The settlement follows the FTC’s claim that Hopper’s interface deliberately obscured additional charges, prompting travelers to believe they were receiving lower‑priced options than were actually available.

Under the agreement, Hopper will not admit wrongdoing but must implement a comprehensive compliance program, undergo regular third‑party audits, and provide clear, upfront disclosures of all fees and service terms. The FTC said the action reinforces its broader effort to curb manipulative design practices that can erode consumer trust in digital marketplaces. The $35 million payment marks one of the larger penalties levied for dark‑pattern violations in the travel sector.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta launches Pocket, an AI gaming app
content:
Meta has quietly introduced Pocket, an experimental AI application that allows users to create and share interactive mini‑games through text prompts. The app, launched in a limited beta, uses the company’s generative AI models to translate simple written descriptions into playable game experiences that can be embedded in social media posts or shared directly with friends.

According to Meta’s product team, Pocket is designed to lower the barrier to game creation, enabling non‑developers to produce engaging content without coding. Users type a prompt—such as “a platformer where the character collects stars”—and the system generates a playable prototype, complete with basic physics and scoring. The feature also supports collaborative editing, allowing multiple users to tweak and refine a game in real time before publishing it to the platform’s community feed.

While still in early testing, Pocket represents Meta’s broader push into generative AI tools for content creation. The company has not yet announced a public release date, but it plans to expand the app’s capabilities and integrate it with its existing social media ecosystem, potentially opening new avenues for user‑generated entertainment and interactive storytelling.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI raises challenges for Amazon and Google in meeting net‑zero goals
content:
Artificial intelligence is increasingly complicating the climate‑change commitments of major technology firms.  Amazon and Google, both of whom have pledged to reach net‑zero emissions by 2040 and 2030 respectively, are finding that the growing demand for AI training and inference is driving up the energy required by their data‑center operations.  The computational intensity of large language models and other AI workloads means that the power consumption of servers is rising faster than the rate at which these companies can add renewable‑energy capacity or improve cooling efficiency.

The impact is measurable.  Amazon’s 2023 sustainability report noted a 12 % rise in data‑center electricity use, while Google’s 2024 environmental report highlighted that AI‑related workloads now account for roughly a third of its total energy draw.  Both firms have responded by accelerating investments in renewable energy procurement, deploying advanced cooling technologies, and exploring carbon‑offset projects, yet the pace of AI adoption continues to outstrip the growth of their green‑energy portfolios.  Industry analysts warn that without a corresponding acceleration in clean‑energy deployment, the net‑zero targets could be jeopardized.

In the near term, Amazon and Google are tightening their procurement contracts for renewable power and expanding on‑site solar and wind projects to match the surge in AI demand.  They are also collaborating with suppliers to improve hardware efficiency and exploring carbon‑capture solutions for data‑center emissions.  Whether these measures will suffice remains to be seen, but the companies’ recent disclosures underscore the growing tension between AI innovation and the urgency of meeting climate commitments.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jersey Mike's IPO filing references artificial intelligence
content:
Jersey Mike’s Subs, the popular sandwich chain that filed for an initial public offering last month, disclosed in its S‑1 documents that it is exploring artificial‑intelligence (AI) technologies to enhance operations and customer experience. The filing notes that the company is evaluating AI‑driven tools for inventory forecasting, supply‑chain optimization, and personalized marketing, as well as potential applications in its kitchen automation and mobile ordering platforms. While the company’s primary focus remains on its franchise model and expansion strategy, the inclusion of AI references signals an intent to modernize back‑of‑house processes and improve data‑driven decision making.

The S‑1 also outlines the regulatory and financial implications of adopting AI, including potential capital expenditures, cybersecurity safeguards, and compliance with emerging data‑privacy standards. Jersey Mike’s management emphasized that any AI initiatives would be implemented gradually, with pilot programs in select markets before broader rollout. Investors and analysts will likely scrutinize how these technology investments align with the company’s growth trajectory and whether they translate into measurable operational efficiencies or revenue gains. As the IPO proceeds, the firm’s willingness to incorporate AI into its business model may shape perceptions of its long‑term competitiveness in the fast‑food sector.
author: TechCrunch

title: IQM goes public on Nasdaq, valued at $1.9 billion
content:
Finland‑based full‑stack quantum‑technology firm IQM Technologies announced its initial public offering on the Nasdaq today, debuting with a market valuation of approximately $1.9 billion. The company, which designs and manufactures quantum processors and related hardware, listed under the ticker “IQM” and began trading shortly after the opening bell.

The IPO marks a significant milestone for the European quantum‑computing sector, positioning IQM among the few publicly traded firms dedicated to delivering end‑to‑end quantum solutions. Analysts noted that the valuation reflects growing investor interest in quantum hardware as the industry moves toward commercial applications, while the proceeds are expected to fund expanded production capacity and further research and development initiatives.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jack Selby’s Copper Sky Capital Raises $300M Second Fund
content:
Copper Sky Capital, the venture‑capital firm founded by entrepreneur and investor Selby, disclosed in a recent regulatory filing that it is in the process of raising a second fund targeting $300 million in commitments. The filing, submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, confirms the firm’s continued expansion after the launch of its inaugural fund, which focused on early‑stage technology and consumer‑focused startups.

The new fund, slated to close later this year, aims to build on Copper Sky Capital’s track record of backing high‑growth companies and to broaden its investment scope across sectors such as fintech, health‑tech, and enterprise software. The filing indicates that the firm has already secured a portion of the capital from existing limited partners and is actively courting additional institutional investors. Completion of the $300 million raise will position Copper Sky Capital to increase its deal flow and support portfolio companies through later‑stage financing rounds, reinforcing its role in the venture‑capital ecosystem.
author: TechCrunch

title: Bitcoin treasury firm Stack BTC loses over 15% of assets after Nigel Farage promotion
content:
A bitcoin treasury company that has attracted the attention of UK political figure Nigel Farage has seen its asset value fall more than 15 percent, prompting financial analysts to caution investors about this type of investment vehicle. Farage, the leader of Reform UK, reportedly invested £215,000 in Stack BTC, a firm that buys and holds bitcoin on behalf of its shareholders and plans to acquire other companies using the proceeds generated from the cryptocurrency’s appreciation.

Stack BTC’s business model relies on the volatility of bitcoin to generate returns, with the firm’s strategy to use gains for further acquisitions. The recent decline in the company’s asset base has raised concerns among market observers, who point out that the high risk associated with cryptocurrency‑backed treasuries can lead to significant losses for investors. Analysts recommend that potential investors conduct thorough due diligence and consider the broader market conditions before allocating capital to similar entities.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta glasses voice‑boost feature limited to three free hours
content:
Meta has announced that the voice‑amplification feature built into its upcoming augmented‑reality glasses will be available for free use for up to three hours per day. The functionality, designed to increase the speaker’s volume in real‑time during conversations, is part of the company’s broader effort to integrate assistive audio tools into wearable technology.

According to the company’s product brief, users can activate the voice boost during meetings, public speaking events, or noisy environments, but the free tier will automatically deactivate after three cumulative hours of use within a 24‑hour period. Beyond that limit, users will need to subscribe to a paid plan or purchase additional usage credits. Meta said the restriction is intended to manage server load and to encourage adoption of its premium services while still offering a trial period for early adopters.

The capped free access underscores Meta’s strategy of monetizing advanced features in its glasses lineup, positioning the voice‑amplification tool as both a utility and a potential revenue stream as the device moves toward broader market release.
author: BBC Technology

title: Hundreds crowd Paris supermarkets seeking cheap air conditioners ahead of heatwave
content:
Hundreds of shoppers converged on supermarkets around Paris on Thursday, sparking scuffles and shouting as they sought discounted air‑cooling units in anticipation of an approaching heatwave. The rush to secure portable fans and small air conditioners was driven by rising temperatures forecast for the coming days, prompting residents to line up for bargains before the demand surged.

The confrontations unfolded in several major retail chains, with some customers reportedly pushing and shoving to secure the limited stock. Security staff were called in to manage the crowds, and local police officers were deployed to maintain order and ensure safety. The incident highlighted the growing public concern over the heatwave’s impact on daily life and the strain on supply chains for climate‑control appliances.

Authorities have urged calm and advised shoppers to follow safety guidelines while purchasing cooling equipment. The French government has announced plans to monitor the situation closely and to provide additional support to vulnerable populations as the heatwave intensifies.
author: France 24

title: Austria and Algeria 3-3 draw triggers online match-fixing claims
content:
A 3‑3 draw between Austria and Algeria at the FIFA World Cup in Kansas City has ignited a wave of online speculation that the match was deliberately arranged to secure both teams’ progression at the expense of Iran. Social‑media posts have circulated misleading video edits, fabricated FIFA notices and hashtags labeling the encounter the “Disgrace of Kansas City,” a reference to the 1982 “Disgrace of Gijón” when West Germany and Austria colluded to eliminate Algeria. The rumors claim that the result was pre‑planned to produce a mutually beneficial scoreline that would see the two European and African sides advance to the knockout stage while Iran, eliminated on goal difference, would be unfairly knocked out.

FIFA and the match officials have refuted the allegations, stating that no evidence of manipulation has been found and that all standard protocols, including VAR reviews, were applied throughout the game. Independent analysts have noted that the scoring pattern—three goals from each side in the final minutes—mirrored typical high‑pressing tactics rather than any coordinated effort. As investigations continue, authorities emphasize that the claims remain unsubstantiated, and the tournament proceeds with the qualified teams moving forward.
author: France 24

title: United States marks 250th anniversary of independence
content:
The United States marked the 250th anniversary of its democratic foundation on July 4, 2026, commemorating the adoption of the Declaration of Independence and the continuity of a constitutional system that has endured since the ratification of the Constitution in 1789. Nationwide events—including fireworks displays, historical exhibitions, and speeches by elected officials—celebrated the milestone, highlighting the nation’s claim to being the world’s longest‑running democracy under a single constitutional framework.

In contrast to the political fluctuations experienced by France over the same period—five republics, three monarchies and three authoritarian regimes, including the Nazi occupation—the United States has maintained an uninterrupted constitutional order for more than two centuries. U.S. officials emphasized the anniversary as a reflection of institutional resilience and the ongoing commitment to democratic principles, while diplomatic representatives from several European nations attended ceremonies to acknowledge the shared historical ties and the symbolic importance of the celebration for transatlantic relations.
author: France 24

title: Algeria holds parliamentary elections amid candidate disqualifications
content:
Algerians went to the polls on Tuesday in a tightly watched parliamentary election, while neighboring Ivory Coast grappled with a deadly flood disaster and a Cameroonian waterfront community faced an escalating waste crisis. The three events, unfolding across West and Central Africa, highlight the region’s simultaneous political, humanitarian and environmental challenges.

In Algeria, authorities barred hundreds of prospective candidates from standing, a move that critics say narrows political competition ahead of the vote. Despite the restrictions, voter turnout proceeded as scheduled, with preliminary results expected later this week. Meanwhile, severe flooding in Ivory Coast’s western provinces has claimed dozens of lives, displaced thousands and prompted a national emergency response, as rescue teams continue to search for missing persons and provide relief supplies. In Cameroon’s coastal town of Kribi, a community once known for its black volcanic sands is now inundated with tons of rubbish, overwhelming local waste management systems and threatening the area’s ecological heritage and tourism prospects.

The concurrent developments underscore the fragility of governance, public safety and environmental stewardship in the region. International observers and aid agencies are monitoring the situations, urging transparent electoral processes in Algeria, swift humanitarian assistance in Ivory Coast, and sustainable waste‑management solutions for Cameroon’s shoreline.
author: France 24

title: France resume training ahead of Paraguay World Cup clash
content:
France’s national football team, commonly known as “les Bleus,” resumed training on Monday following a commanding 3‑0 win against Sweden in their recent friendly. The victory, highlighted by a dominant first‑half performance and a clean sheet, marked the team’s most decisive result in the current preparation cycle and underscored the effectiveness of head coach Didier Deschamps’ tactical adjustments.

The squad will travel to the United States to face Paraguay in a friendly match scheduled for July 4 in Philadelphia, a fixture that serves as the final warm‑up before the upcoming international tournament. The game is expected to provide both sides with an opportunity to fine‑tune line‑ups and assess player fitness ahead of the competition’s opening stages.
author: France 24

title: Spain beat Austria 3-0 to reach World Cup 2026 last 16
content:
Spain secured a spot in the World Cup round of 16 on Thursday with a decisive 3‑0 victory over Austria. The match, played at the Santiago Bernabéu, saw the Spanish side dominate possession and create numerous scoring opportunities, while Austria struggled to establish any sustained pressure.

Spain’s goals came from a first‑half strike by forward Álvaro Morata, followed by a second‑half double from midfielder Pedri and winger Ferran Torres, each highlighting the team’s fluid attacking play. Coach Luis Enrique praised the squad’s discipline and tactical execution, noting that the win reflects Spain’s consistency throughout the tournament. With the win, Spain advances to the knockout stage, while Austria’s campaign ends with the defeat.
author: France 24

title: German reforms, Google loss, and $20 million Swift wedding highlighted
content:
The latest business and economic briefing highlights a mixed performance across global markets as investors weigh recent corporate earnings reports, central bank policy signals, and ongoing supply‑chain adjustments. Major equity indices in North America and Europe showed modest gains in the morning session, while Asian markets slipped amid concerns over slower growth in key manufacturing hubs. Commodity prices remained relatively stable, with oil hovering near the previous week’s average and copper edging higher on expectations of increased demand from the construction sector.

In the corporate sphere, several multinational firms released quarterly results that largely met analyst forecasts, though revenue growth varied by region. Meanwhile, policymakers in the United States and the Eurozone signaled a cautious approach to interest‑rate changes, emphasizing the need to balance inflation pressures with sustainable economic expansion. The combined effect of these developments suggests a tentative outlook for the near term, with market participants awaiting further data on consumer spending and employment trends to gauge the trajectory of the global economy.
author: France 24

title: Ebola outbreak in DRC kills over 400, reaches Kisangani
content:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed more than 400 lives and is expanding beyond its original focus in the country’s northeastern region. Health authorities confirmed the first case in Kisangani, a major city located several hundred kilometres from the epidemic’s epicentre, marking the virus’s entry into a densely populated urban area.

The spread to Kisangani heightens concerns among national and international health agencies, which are intensifying surveillance, contact tracing and vaccination efforts to contain the disease. Officials warned that the city’s size and transport links could accelerate transmission, prompting calls for heightened community awareness and rapid response measures as the outbreak continues to evolve.
author: France 24

title: Vatican excommunicates SSPX bishops and members after unauthorized consecrations
content:
The Vatican’s Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith has imposed severe disciplinary measures on the Society of Saint Pius X (SSPX), an ultratraditionalist Catholic group. The sanctions follow the society’s unauthorized consecration of bishops, an act that violated the Church’s canonical requirement for papal approval. The decree, issued on Thursday, restricts the SSPX’s ability to hold public liturgies and limits its use of the Tridentine Mass, while also prohibiting the society from celebrating the Eucharist in the name of the Pope.

The decision reflects the Holy See’s long‑standing effort to bring the SSPX back into full communion with Rome. In 2009, the society had entered into a provisional agreement with the Vatican, but the consecrations carried out in 2009 and 2016—without the Pope’s consent—were deemed a breach of that accord. The Congregation’s decree reiterates that the SSPX remains in a state of canonical irregularity, and it warns that further violations could lead to additional penalties or the removal of the society’s ecclesiastical status.

The Vatican’s action underscores the Church’s commitment to maintaining hierarchical unity and adherence to canon law. While the SSPX continues to operate under its own leadership, the new restrictions signal a tightening of oversight and a clear stance against unauthorized episcopal consecrations. The decree is expected to prompt further dialogue between the society and the Holy See as both sides seek a resolution that preserves doctrinal fidelity and ecclesial communion.
author: DW World

title: Turkish comedian Deniz Goktas detained upon arrival in Istanbul
content:
Turkish stand‑up comedian Deniz Goktas was detained upon his return to Turkey after a short video he posted online went viral. The clip, which included references to President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and religious themes, attracted the attention of authorities and was subsequently removed from social media platforms.
